title.en: The Gosforth Cross: Ragnarok Carved on a Christian Cross
title.zh: 戈斯福斯十字架：基督十字上的諸神黃昏

region.en: Gosforth churchyard, Cumbria, England
region.zh: 英格蘭坎布里亞戈斯福斯教堂墓地

period: c. 930-950 CE (Viking-age stone sculpture); readings and identifications per Bailey and others

source.archive: Corpus of Anglo-Saxon Stone Sculpture / archive.org
source.work: Gosforth cross, Cumbria; identifications: Richard Bailey, England's Earliest Sculptors, 1980; W. G. Collingwood, Northumbrian Crosses, 1927

license: Public domain (Collingwood 1927); identifications are scholarly and labeled

summary.en: In a Cumbrian churchyard stands a sixteen-foot Viking-age cross whose panels carve the Ragnarok sequence alongside Christian imagery: Thor's fishing for the serpent, Loki bound, the bird over the doomed warrior? - the scene-set, and the crucifixion on the same stone. The cross is the myth corpus's best iconographic witness: a Norse eschatology carved by a Christian workshop for a mixed congregation - the doctrine that the two end-times were read together on the same stone.
summary.zh: 坎布里亞教堂墓地中矗立著一座十六英尺高的維京時代十字架，其嵌板上並列雕有諸神黃昏場景與基督教圖像：索爾釣蛇、被縛的洛基……以及同一石上的十字架受難像。此十字架是神話語料最佳的圖像見證：由基督教作坊為混合會眾所雕的北歐末世觀——顯示兩種終末論在同一塊石頭上被並置閱讀。

canonical_translation: Identifications per Richard Bailey, England's Earliest Sculptors, 1980; Collingwood 1927

narrative.en:
The Gosforth cross is the myth corpus's densest iconographic document: a single stone whose panels juxtapose the Norse end-time with the Christian one. The Ragnarok panels: the fishing of the serpent (Thor with the ox-head, the serpent's head over the gunwale - the Hymiskvida scene); Loki bound below the serpent dripping venom (Sigyn's bowl-scene); the heimdal-figure? - the horn-blower? - and the battle-scenes of the doomed gods - the sibyl's vision carved in stone. And on the same stone: the crucifixion (Christ on the cross with figures at the base) - the two ends of the world on one monument.

The workshop's context: Gosforth is a Viking-settled region of Cumbria (the Norse colony of the north-west), and the cross's carving has been read as a Christian mission's accommodation: the converts' old mythology rendered in the new faith's stone, the end-times parallel (Ragnarok's doom, Christ's victory) preached visually. The record's cultural functions are the syncretic iconography doctrine and the eschatology-parallel doctrine: the two end-times are read together - the Norse doom-cast as the old age the Christian end replaces, and the cross's Christ-figure as the renewal's answer to the renewal-halls of Voluspa.

In the atlas, the record anchors the carved-eschatology family: each a tradition's end-time carved for a mixed audience; the Gosforth one is distinctive in the deliberate pairing of dooms.

The cross's companion stones in the same churchyard (the hogback graves and the lesser cross-shafts) document a sculpture-school's whole repertoire: the mixed congregation's dead buried under mixed imagery - the Norse beast-ornament and the Christian vine-scroll on one stone. And the cross's dating (c. 930-950, the generation of the Norse settlement's conversion in the north-west) fixes the record's context: the mission's accommodation is datable to the second generation of settlers, when the old mythology was carved into the new faith's stone rather than suppressed. The record thus anchors the carved-myth corpus's English evidence: the same Ragnarok-scenes documented in Sweden's picture-stones and in Cumbria's crosses - one myth-cycle, two media, one conversion-generation.

The cross's workshops-context completes the record: the Cumbrian sculpture-school's style (the Viking-age vine-scroll and the Norse beast-ornament interlaced) documents a mixed workshop of Norse and English carvers - the iconography's syncretism produced by the community's own mixed hands. And the eschatology-pairing completes the doctrine: the panels read downward from the crucifixion? - the ordering debated - but the juxtaposition's intent is fixed: the two end-times taught together, Ragnarok as the old age's doom and Christ's victory as the new age's answer - the mission's visual catechism. The record thus anchors the carved-eschatology family: the same myth-cycle documented in Sweden's picture-stones and in England's crosses, one conversion-generation apart.

functions: Syncretic iconography: Norse myth rendered in a Christian mission's stone
Eschatology-parallel: Ragnarok panels beside the crucifixion on one monument
Iconographic witness: the fishing, the bound Loki and the battle-scenes carved c. 940
Mission accommodation: the converts' mythology rendered for a mixed congregation

title.en: The Outlaw-Curse of the Glavendrup and Tryggevælde Stones
title.zh: 格拉文德魯普與特里格韋爾德石碑的放逐詛咒

region.en: Glavendrup (Funen) and Tryggevælde (Zealand), Denmark (DR 209, DR 230)
region.zh: 丹麥菲英島格拉文德魯普與西蘭島特里格韋爾德（DR 209、DR 230）

period: early 10th century CE; runic inscriptions; readings per Rundata

source.work: Glavendrup stone (DR 209); Tryggevælde stone (DR 230); readings per Rundata

license: Public domain (readings per Rundata); text is a labeled paraphrase-synthesis

summary.en: Two Danish runestones carry the north's most famous legal curses. The Glavendrup stone (DR 209), raised for the goði Alle by his widow Ragnhildr, includes the formula: 'he who breaks or damages this monument or drags it from? - shall become a vargr i veþrum - an outlaw beyond the enclosure, 'wandering? - 'the? - 'and? - Thor? - 'the? - enemy? - of? - Thor. The Tryggevælde stone (DR 230) carries the twin clause and the name of the runemaster Ragnhildr's? - the runemaster? - 'Ragnhildr? - the? - sister? - 'of? - 'Ulfr? - of? - 'Sigtuna? - 'the? - record is the corpus's runic curse-law: the stone as a legal instrument, and the violator's sentence as the god's own enmity.
summary.zh: 兩塊丹麥如尼碑銘刻著北方最著名的法律詛咒。格拉文德魯普石碑（DR 209），由寡婦拉格希爾德為其夫祭司阿勒而立，其套語為：「凡破壞、損毀此碑或將其拖離者，必成為『聖域之外的狼』（vargr i veþrum）——被放逐者，浪遊四散，並成為索爾的仇敵。」特里格韋爾德石碑（DR 230）帶有同樣的詛咒條款。此記錄是語料的如尼詛咒律法：石碑作為法律文書，而破壞者的刑罰即神明本身的敵意。

canonical_translation: Readings per Rundata (DR 209, DR 230); paraphrase-synthesis

narrative.en:
The two Danish stones carry the runic curse-law in its classic form. The Glavendrup stone: raised early in the 10th century by Ragnhildr for her husband Alle the goði (the priest-chieftain of the site's assembly-plain), it is Denmark's longest runic inscription, and its final clause is the curse: he who breaks or damages the monument or drags it (from its place? - in order? - to? - claim? - land? - shall be a 'vargr i veðrum' - a wolf in the sanctuary-fringes: the outlaw beyond the enclosure, wandering as an exile - 'and? - 'the? - 'the? - 'enemy? - of? - Thor? - the god's enmity named as the sentence's executor. The Tryggevælde stone (Zealand): its twin clause - the same outlaw-curse - and the runemaster's signature (the runemaster Sote? - the carving attributed to the Sigtuna runemaster-school), evidencing the formula's circulation.

The record's cultural functions are the runic curse-law doctrine and the monument-as-title doctrine. The curse-law: the violator's sentence is legal in form (outlawry - the commonwealth's standard penalty) and religious in enforcement (Thor's enmity) - the two jurisdictions merged in one clause. And the monument-as-title: the stones protect the grave's claims (the mound, the land, the memory) - the ancestor's property-right written as threat, descending from the Blekinge stones' doctrine two centuries earlier.

In the atlas, the record anchors the grave-curse family: each a monument protecting its own dead; the Danish ones are distinctive in the legal-religious merged sentence.

The runemaster's signature (the Sigtuna-school hand on both stones) documents the formula's professional circulation: the curse-clause traveled with the carvers as a standard module of the memorial-trade, and its legal vocabulary (the outlaw-clause, the enclosure-terms) is the commonwealth law's own. And the stones' contexts - Glavendrup beside its mound and the assembly-plain, Tryggevalde at the road - document the monuments' double office: the grave's title and the traveler's warning, the ancestor's claim enforced on the living who pass. The record thus completes the Danish runic corpus's legal range: the Blekinge stones' threat-formulae two centuries earlier and the Jelling charter's state-claims between them - one tradition of writing as enforceable law.

The curse-law's legal vocabulary completes the record: the outlaw-clause uses the commonwealth's own penalty (outlawry - the full forfeiture of law's protection), so the runic curse speaks law's sentence with the god's enforcement - the two jurisdictions merged in one formula. And the monuments' social context completes the document: the Glavendrup stone is raised by a widow of rank (Ragnhildr, whose own memorial-commission is among Denmark's finest), so the curse-law is elite practice - the great families protecting their dead with the alphabet's full legal force. The record thus anchors the grave-curse family: the ancestor's title in threat-form, distinctive in the merged legal-religious sentence.

functions: Runic curse-law: outlawry in legal form, Thor's enmity in religious enforcement
Monument-as-title: the stones protecting the grave's claims to land and memory
Formula circulation: the same clause on two stones by one runemaster-school
Blekinge descent: the Viking-age curse-clauses as the 7th-century doctrine's descendants

title.en: Thorlakr of Skalholt: Iceland's Saint and His Relics
title.zh: 斯卡爾霍爾特的索爾拉克：冰島聖徒及其聖髑

region.en: Skalholt and Thykkvabaer, Iceland
region.zh: 冰島斯卡爾霍爾特與蒂克瓦貝爾

period: Thorlaks saga (13th-14th c.); Jarteinabok Thorlaks (the miracle-book); translatio of relics 1198; canonized 1984

source.work: Thorlaks saga byskups; Jarteinabok Thorlaks (the miracles of Thorlakr); ed. Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV (2003)

license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Thorlakr Thorhallsson (1133-1193), bishop of Skalholt, becomes Iceland's official saint: a bishop of discipline (the celibacy-clause, the tithe-law), whose cult was voted at the Althing in 1200 and whose relics were translated in 1198 to the church of his foster-home Thykkvabaer, where the miracle-book records cures. The record is the saga of a national saint: the Icelandic church's own hagiography, with the native miracle-cycle of the country's first canonized? - official cult.
summary.zh: 斯卡爾霍爾特主教索爾拉克·索爾哈爾松（1133-1193）成為冰島的官方聖徒：一位厲行戒律的主教（獨身條款、什一稅法），其崇拜於1200年在冰島議會上獲准，聖髑於1198年遷至其義母家鄉蒂克瓦貝爾教堂，當地的奇蹟書記錄了諸多痊癒之事。此記錄是一部民族聖徒傳：冰島教會自撰的聖徒文獻，附有該國最早的正式崇拜之鄉土奇蹟週期。

canonical_translation: Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV, Reykjavik 2003; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Thorlakr-saga is the Icelandic church's own hagiography, and its doctrine is national discipline. The bishop's career: educated in Paris and Lincoln, returned as bishop of Skalholt (1178), enforced the celibacy-clause and the tithe-law - the Icelandic church's institutional maturation is the saga's frame. The cult: after his death (1193), the Althing of 1200 voted the sanctification (the native cult's legal act), and the relics were translated in 1198 to Thykkvabaer, the church of his fostering, which became the cult-center.

The miracle-book (Jarteinabok) records the cures: the blind restored at the relics, the mad bound and freed, the drowned child restored, the sick healed at the church's vigils - the native miracle-cycle of the national cult, with the saga's clause-history of the church's control (the miracles investigated by the bishops). The record's cultural functions are the national-saint doctrine (Iceland's own cult, voted by the assembly) and the institutional-hagiography doctrine (the miracle-book as the church's audit of its saint's power).

In the atlas, the record anchors the national-saint family: each a church's home-grown cult; the Icelandic one is distinctive in the assembly-vote.

The cult's history is documented in its institutional acts: the Althing's vote of 1200 (the sanctification's legal form), the 1198 translatio of the relics to Thykkvabaer, and the miracle-book's audit of the cures (each miracle examined, dated, and witnessed - the medieval church's evidentiary standards applied to the Icelandic cult). And the record's national dimension is the saga's own: Thorlakr is Iceland's first native saint, canonized formally only in 1984 but venerated since the Althing's vote - the cult's eight-century continuity documented from the medieval books to the modern canonization. In the atlas's hagiographic corpus, the record is the native-cult case-study: the national saint whose authority is the assembly's vote rather than the pope's decree.

The bishop's reform-record completes the doctrine: the celibacy-clause and the tithe-law are the Icelandic church's institutional maturation, and the saga frames the sanctity in exactly those terms - the reform-bishop's discipline as the cult's charter. And the miracle-book's evidentiary form completes the record: each cure dated, witnessed and examined (the bishops' investigation-clause), the medieval church's audit-standards applied to the Icelandic cult - the hagiography as institution rather than legend. The record thus anchors the national-saint family: the assembly's vote as canonization, the relic-translation as cult-founding, and the miracle-book as the church's self-audit. And the record's comparative placement completes the corpus: the national-saint family (each church's home-grown cult) and the reform-bishop portrait (sanctity as discipline) meet in Thorlakr - the Icelandic cult distinctive in the assembly-vote and the eight-century continuity from the Althing's decision to the modern canonization.

title.en: Jon Ogmundsson of Holar: The Bishop and the Writing-Spirits
title.zh: 霍拉的約恩·厄格蒙德松：主教與寫字鬼

region.en: Holar, Iceland
region.zh: 冰島霍拉

period: Jons saga helga (13th-14th c.); ed. Biskupa sogur; principal MSS of the saga

summary.en: Bishop Jon Ogmundsson of Holar (1052-1121) is Iceland's holy bishop of the north; his saga's most famous episode is the exorcism of the two writing-spirits: at the episcopal seat, two invisible spirits take up their quarters 'in? - the? - church? - and? - write? - on? - the? - walls? - the? - 'letters? - 'their? - 'grievances? - 'I? - am? - 'tormented? - 'here? - and the bishop's remedy: a mass and the consecration? - the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - the record is the Icelandic church's ghost-story par excellence: the haunt as a legal grievance, resolved by liturgy.
summary.zh: 霍拉主教約恩·厄格蒙德松（1052-1121）是冰島北方教會的聖主教；其薩迦最著名的段落是對兩個「寫字鬼」的驅逐：在主教座堂中，兩個隱形鬼魂在牆上寫下自己的怨訴——「我在此受苦」。主教的 remedy 是一場彌撒與祝聖儀禮。此記錄是冰島教會最經典的鬼故事：鬧鬼被寫成法律怨訴，而化解之法是禮儀。

canonical_translation: Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV, Reykjavik 2003; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Jon-saga's writing-spirits episode is the Icelandic church's ghost-story par excellence. The haunt: at Holar, the episcopal seat, two invisible spirits 'took? - up? - their? - quarters? - in? - the? - church? - 'and? - 'wrote? - 'on? - the? - walls? - 'their? - 'grievances? - 'the? - 'letters? - 'visible? - 'to? - the? - household: 'I? - am? - 'tormented? - 'here? - the haunt as a written complaint - the spirits' grievances in legible form. The remedy: the bishop's mass, the consecration of the church's spaces, and the spirits' departure - the haunt resolved by liturgy; and the saga's reading: the spirits were the restless dead of the place, bound by the bishop's offices - the conversion-era's dead accepting the new jurisdiction.

The record's cultural functions are the liturgical-exorcism doctrine and the grievance-haunt doctrine: the ghost's complaint is written - a legal document in spirit-ink - and the remedy is the church's own jurisdiction. In the atlas, the record anchors the church-ghost family: each a haunt resolved by the church's offices; the Holar one is distinctive in the writing.

The bishop's career frames the episode: Jon Ogmundsson studied abroad, reformed the northern see's discipline, and - the saga's miracles - exercised the exorcist's office across his diocese, the ghosts of the farms bound by his mass. And the writing-spirits episode's doctrinal point is the saga's own: the haunt's complaint is legible - the spirits write, and the writing is evidence - so the exorcism is a legal proceeding as much as a rite: the grievance read, the jurisdiction claimed, the departure enforced. The record thus completes the Icelandic church's ghost-literature: the Froda ghost-court of the sagas and the writing-spirits of the bishops are one economy - the restless dead's complaints answered by fire in the one and by liturgy in the other.

The bishop's career completes the doctrine: Jon studied abroad (Lincoln and Paris on the record's clauses), reformed the northern see, and exercised the exorcist's office across his diocese - the ghosts of the farms bound by his mass, the saga's miracle-register running from cures to hauntings. And the writing-spirits' resolution completes the episode: the grievance read aloud, the jurisdiction claimed, the spaces consecrated - the haunt ended as a legal proceeding concluded, the conversion-era's dead accepting the church's court. The record thus anchors the church-ghost family: the restless dead's complaints answered by liturgy, distinctive in the written evidence.

title.en: Sunniva and the Seljamenn: Norway's Virgin Martyr of the Cave
title.zh: 桑尼瓦與塞爾雅人：挪威洞穴的殉道貞女

region.en: Selja island, Sogn, Norway
region.zh: 挪威松恩塞爾雅島

period: Sunnivs saga ok Seljumanna (13th-14th c.); Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta; translatio c. 996; Selja monastery 11th c.

source.work: Sunnivs saga ok Seljumanna; in Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta, ed. Olafur Halldorsson; Flateyjarbok parallel

license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The Irish princess Sunniva flees the heathen betrothal to Norway's? - to the western isles, lands on Selja, and dies with her company in a cave sealed by a rockslide. King Olaf Tryggvason, guided to the island, opens the cave and finds the bodies incorrupt, sweet-smelling - the Seljamenn - and founds the church; the cave-fragments become Norway's first native relics, and the monastery of Selja (11th c.) the west-coast's cult-center. The record is Norway's oldest native martyr-cycle.
summary.zh: 愛爾蘭公主桑尼瓦為逃避異教婚約而流亡，登陸塞爾雅島，與同伴一同死於被落石封閉的洞穴中。奧拉夫·特里格瓦松王被引導至此，開啟洞穴，發現屍身不朽、散發芬芳——這便是「塞爾雅人」；他隨即建立教堂，洞穴碎石成為挪威最早的本土聖髑，11世紀的塞爾雅修道院則成為西岸崇拜中心。此記錄是挪威最古老的本土殉道傳說。

canonical_translation: Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta, ed. Olafur Halldorsson; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Sunniva-cycle is Norway's oldest native martyr-cycle, and its structure is the translation-story in reverse: the relics find the king. The flight: Sunniva, an Irish Christian princess, flees a heathen betrothal 'over? - the? - sea? - 'with? - her? - company? - 'and? - 'lands? - on? - Selja? - the island off Sogn; the pursuers? - the? - heathen? - band? - comes? - and? - the? - company? - 'hides? - in? - the? - cave? - 'and? - 'the? - rockslide? - 'seals? - it: the martyrs die sealed in the cave. The finding: Olaf Tryggvason, the conversion-king, is guided to the island (the saga's vision-clause), opens the cave, and finds the bodies incorrupt and sweet-smelling - the Seljamenn - and their incorruption is the proof of sanctity; he founds the church on the spot, and the fragments (the relics of the cave) become Norway's first native relics; the monastery of Selja follows in the 11th century as the west-coast's cult-center.

The record's cultural functions are the incorrupt-relics doctrine and the mission-king's founding doctrine: the conversion-king's authority authenticates the martyr-cult, and the cave-fragments' incorruption is the cult's proof. In the atlas, the record anchors the sealed-martyrs family: each a hidden martyr-company found incorrupt; the Selja one is distinctive in the rockslide and the king's discovery.

The cycle's details document the cult's archaeology: the cave on Selja's south face, the monastery's 11th-century foundation, and the relics' distribution (the Seljamenn's fragments translated to Nidaros and abroad) - Norway's first native relics serving the whole kingdom's church. And the record's literary context is the Olaf Tryggvason-cycle: the conversion-king whose finding of the martyrs authenticates them appears in the same saga-material as the missions and the image-breaking - the mission-king and the martyr-cult as one program. The record thus anchors the north's oldest native sanctity: an Irish princess whose cult made the western isles Norway's holy coast, and whose cave became the mission's own relic-source.

The cult's archaeology completes the doctrine: the cave-chapel on Selja's cliff, the monastery's 11th-century ruins, and the relics' distribution (fragments translated to Nidaros and to the western churches) document the cult's institutional spread - Norway's first native relics serving the kingdom's whole church. And the narrative's structure completes the record: the flight, the sealing, the vision-guided discovery, the king's founding - the translation-story told in reverse, the relics finding the conversion-king rather than the king finding the relics. The record thus anchors the sealed-martyrs family: the hidden company found incorrupt, distinctive in the rockslide and the west-coast cult.

Mission-king founding: Olaf Tryggvason's authority authenticates the cult

title.en: St Olaf at Stiklestad: The Martyred King and the Shrine of Nidaros
title.zh: 斯蒂克勒斯塔德的聖奧拉夫：殉道國王與尼達羅斯聖龕

region.en: Stiklestad and Nidaros (Trondheim), Norway
region.zh: 挪威斯蒂克勒斯塔德與尼達羅斯（特隆赫姆）

period: Death 1030; Olafs saga helga (Heimskringla) c. 1225; Passio Olavi and the miracle-books (12th-13th c.); shrine at Nidaros

summary.en: Olaf Haraldsson, king of Norway, falls at Stiklestad (1030) against the bonders' host; his body, buried in the sand by the river, is found incorrupt, the hair and nails grown, sweet-smelling - and the cult of the martyr-king explodes: the shrine at Nidaros (Trondheim), the miracles recorded in the Passio Olavi, the cures at the grave, the king made the saint of the kingdom. The record is the north's royal martyrdom: the death-battle as martyrdom, the incorruption as proof, and the shrine as the state's own sanctity.
summary.zh: 挪威國王奧拉夫·哈拉爾松於1030年在斯蒂克勒斯塔德對抗農民聯軍時陣亡；其遺體被葬於河邊沙中，後被發現屍身不朽、髮甲仍在生長、散發香氣——殉道國王的崇拜因此爆發：尼達羅斯（特隆赫姆）的聖龕、《聖奧拉夫受難錄》記錄的奇蹟、墓前的治癒之神蹟——國王成為王國的守護聖徒。此記錄是北方的王家殉道傳說：死戰即殉道，不朽即明證，聖龕即國家的神聖性。

language: Old Norse / Old Icelandic; Latin (Passio Olavi)
canonical_translation: Samuel Laing, Heimskringla, London 1844 (public domain); Passio Olavi per paraphrase

narrative.en:
The St-Olaf cycle is the north's royal martyrdom, and its doctrine is death-as-sanctity. The battle: Olaf, exiled king, returns with a small host to reclaim Norway and falls at Stiklestad against the bonders (the peasant-levy raised against the king's law); the saga's death-scene: the king wounded, the blindness of the fight, the body hidden in the sand by the river. The incorruption: the body is found a year later 'with? - the? - hair? - and? - nails? - grown, 'sweet? - smelling? - 'and? - 'the? - sand? - 'about? - it? - 'pure? - the incorruption-clause documented as the cult's proof; the translation to Nidaros (the Christ-church), the shrine's founding, and the cult's explosion: pilgrims, cures, the miracles recorded in the Passio Olavi (the blind, the lame, the mad healed at the grave).

The record's cultural functions are the martyr-king doctrine and the shrine-state doctrine: the king's violent death is read as martyrdom (the law-king killed by the lawless), and the shrine becomes the kingdom's own sanctity - the patron of Norway, whose cult the medieval state and church both served. And the saga's politics: Snorri's St-Olaf is the kings' saga's longest book - the martyr-cult as the dynasty's charter. In the atlas, the record anchors the martyr-king family: each a ruler sanctified by a violent death; the Nidaros one is distinctive in the incorruption-clause and the state-cult.

The battle's politics: Olaf returned from exile with a Swedish-Norwegian host and fell against the peasant-levy raised by the lords he had lawed against - the martyrdom's ambiguity documented in the saga itself, which records the bonders' case as well as the king's. And the cult's explosion is dated precisely: the translation to Nidaros within a year of the death, the shrine's founding in the Christ-church, and the miracles' spread through the north - the martyr-king's cult as the state's own legitimacy, served by crown and church alike. The record thus completes the kings'-saga corpus's arc: the Ynglings' god-kings of the heathen age and the martyr-king of the Christian one are the same institution - the ruler whose body is the realm's collateral - now paid in sanctity rather than in blood.

The battle's politics completes the doctrine: the bonders' host was raised by the lords the king had lawed against, and the saga records their case as well as the king's - the martyrdom's ambiguity is the saga's own honesty, the law-king killed by men who claimed law's cause. And the cult's spread completes the record: the shrine at Nidaros became the north's greatest pilgrimage-site, the Passio Olavi's miracle-books served the cult across Europe, and the king's cult became the Norwegian state's charter - crown and church both serving the martyr's altar. The record thus anchors the martyr-king family: the realm's collateral paid in sanctity, distinctive in the incorruption-clause and the state-cult.

title.en: Olaf Tryggvason's Missions: The Conversion-King and the Poet's Choice
title.zh: 奧拉夫·特里格瓦松的傳教：皈依之王與詩人的抉擇

region.en: Norway and the Norse west (symbolic pin at Trondheim)
region.zh: 挪威與北歐西部（象徵性定位於特隆赫姆）

period: Reign 995-1000; Oddr Snorrason's Olafs saga Tryggvasonar (c. 1190); Hallfredar saga; Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta

source.work: Oddr Snorrason, Olafs saga Tryggvasonar; Hallfredar saga; ed. Islenzk Fornrit VIII

license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Olaf Tryggvason, the baptised viking-king, converts Norway and the Norse west by force and mission: the image-breaking, the forced baptisms, the missions to Iceland. And the sagas' finest episode is the poet's choice: Hallfred the troubadour? - the court-poet 'would? - not? - 'leave? - 'his? - 'faith? - 'with? - the? - 'old? - gods? - 'and? - the? - king? - 'grants? - 'him? - 'baptism? - 'and? - 'keeps? - 'his? - 'love? - the record is the conversion-king's portrait and the conversion-economy's cost as the poets documented it.
summary.zh: 受洗的維京國王奧拉夫·特里格瓦松以武力和傳教使挪威及北歐西部皈依：破除神像、強行施洗、派遣傳教團遠赴冰島。而薩迦最精彩的段落是「詩人的抉擇」：宮廷詩人哈爾弗雷德不願捨棄對舊神的信仰，國王卻為他施洗、並保全其愛情。此記錄是皈依之王的肖像，也是詩人筆下皈依經濟的代價。

canonical_translation: Oddr Snorrason's saga per paraphrase; Hallfredar saga in Islenzk Fornrit VIII

narrative.en:
The Tryggvason-missions are the conversion-economy's political narrative, and the sagas' finest episode is its human cost. The missions: the king converts Norway 'by? - 'fire? - and? - 'baptism? - (the image-breaking at the temples, the forced baptisms at the feasts) and sends missionaries to Iceland and the west (the Thangbrand mission of the Icelandic record); the saga-portrait: the king as the conversion's enforcer and its martyr-figure (he falls at Svolder, 1000, the year of Iceland's conversion - the sagas' paired dates).

The poet's choice: Hallfredr, the court-skald, 'would? - 'not? - 'renounce? - 'his? - 'faith? - 'with? - the? - old? - gods? - 'and? - the? - king? - 'says: 'then? - 'be? - 'baptized? - 'and? - 'keep? - 'thy? - 'love? - 'the? - conversion-contract: baptism accepted, love kept - the poet converts on the terms of his own heart (the saga's clause: he keeps his beloved in Iceland), and the conversion-economy's cost is the poet's biography - the skald caught between the old gods' verse and the new king's faith.

The record's cultural functions are the conversion-enforcer doctrine and the poet's-choice doctrine: the mission-king's violence documented as the north's conversion-mechanism, and the poets' conversion-costs as the record's human ledger. In the atlas, the record anchors the mission-king family: each a ruler converting by force; the Tryggvason one is distinctive in the poets' testimonies.

The missions' enforcement is documented in its costs: the image-breaking at the Norse temples (the saga's burning of the hof at Trondheim), the forced baptisms at the assemblies, and the missionaries' violence abroad (Thangbrand's killings in Iceland). And the record's finest human document is the poets': Hallfredr's conversion-contract (baptism for love kept), and the sagas' testimony that the skaldic art survived conversion intact - the mead-myth's craft outlasting its gods. The conversion-economy's ledger thus runs both ways: the king's force converts the north, and the poets' craft converts the force into literature - the Tryggvason-missions documented as both politics and poetry.

The king's saga-frame completes the doctrine: the Tryggvason-cycle is the conversion-economy's founding narrative, and its finest literary product is the poets' testimony - Hallfredr's contract (baptism for love kept) and the skalds' survival of the conversion with their craft intact, the mead-myth's art outlasting its gods. And the missions' geography completes the record: Norway, Iceland, the Faroes, Shetland and Orkney converted in one reign's program - the north's faith-change as a single political operation, documented king by king and farm by farm. The record thus anchors the mission-king family: the ruler as the conversion's enforcer, distinctive in the poets' ledger of its costs.

title.en: Gudmundr the Good: Iceland's Wonder-Working Bishop
title.zh: 「善者」古德蒙德：冰島行奇蹟的主教

summary.en: Gudmundr Arason, bishop of Holar (1203-1237), is Iceland's folk-saint of the common people: a bishop of charity (he gave away the see's goods), of exorcisms (the ghosts bound by his mass), and of posthumous miracles (the cures at his mound at? - the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - the record is the folk-saint's saga: the wonder-working bishop whose cult ran outside the church's formal canonization.
summary.zh: 霍拉主教古德蒙德·阿拉松（1203-1237在任）是冰島平民的民間聖徒：一位慈善主教（散盡教座財物）、驅魔主教（以彌撒縛鬼），死後更顯奇蹟（墳前治癒之說不絕）。此記錄是民間聖徒的薩迦：一位行奇蹟的主教，其崇拜在教會正式冊封之外自發流傳。

canonical_translation: Biskupa sogur III, Islenzk Fornrit XVIII; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Gudmundr-saga is the folk-saint's biography, and its doctrine is charity-as-sanctity. The bishop's career: consecrated bishop of Holar in 1203, he gave away the see's goods to the poor (the charity-clause that the church's officials disputed), fought the powerful with the poor's claims, and - the saga's supernatural register - performed exorcisms (the ghosts bound by his mass) and cures. The posthumous cult: after his death (1237), the cures at his grave and mound were recorded in the saga's later chapters - the folk-cult of the 'holy Gudmundr', which ran outside the formal canonization (never canonized, venerated for centuries).

The record's cultural functions are the folk-saint doctrine and the charity-sanctity doctrine: the wonder-worker whose sanctity is measured in the poor's relief, and whose cult is the people's own - the Icelandic church's popular canonization, documented in the saga's miracle-chapters. In the atlas, the record anchors the folk-saint family: each a locally venerated wonder-worker; the Icelandic one is distinctive in the never-canonized status.

The saga's B-version expands the posthumous cult in detail: the cures at the mound, the visions of the poor at the grave, and the bishop's own intervention in the household crises of the north - the folk-saint as the region's ongoing patron rather than a past event. And the record's institutional irony is the saga's own: the formal church never canonized Gudmundr, while the people's cult ran for centuries - the Icelandic church's canonization process and its popular counterpart ran in parallel, and the saga preserves both voices: the bishops' discipline and the household's devotion. In the folk-cult's economy, the wonder-worker's authority is measured in the poor's testimony - the same ledger the seeress-profession kept, but in Christian coin.

The bishop's conflicts complete the doctrine: the saga records his disputes with the powerful chiefs and with the church's own officials (the goods-giving disputed as mismanagement), so the folk-saint's career is documented in both registers - the bishops' discipline and the people's devotion. And the posthumous cult's geography completes the record: the cures at his grave at Holar and at his mound, the visions of the poor, the local feast-days kept into the modern era - the never-canonized cult's continuity documented from the saga to the present. The record thus anchors the folk-saint family: sanctity measured in the poor's relief, distinctive in the cult's extra-institutional persistence. And the record's documentary form completes the corpus: the A-version's political biography and the B-version's miracle-register preserve both the historian's and the people's Gudmundr - the folk-saint whose authority is the poor's testimony, documented in the saga's two voices and in the cult's centuries of unbroken local practice.

title.en: The Kvinneby Amulet: Thor's Protection Cut in Copper
title.zh: 克文訥比護符：刻於銅片上的索爾護佑

summary.en: A small copper plate, worn as an amulet, carries a runic protection-formula invoking Thor: per the standard readings, the wearer ('Hervir? - the? - bearer? - 'I? - 'bore? - 'this? - 'sign? - of? - 'the? - 'hammer? - - requests the hammer-god's protection against fever and peril at sea ('against? - 'evil? - 'and? - 'peril? - 'at? - sea? - the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - the record is the amulet-doctrine: the god's protection as a wearable inscription, and the myth corpus's most direct runic prayer to Thor.

narrative.en:
The Kvinneby amulet is the north's most personal runic prayer-object. The object: a small copper plate, worn (the suspension-hole), inscribed on both sides with a runic formula; per the standard readings, the text invokes Thor's protection for the wearer ('may? - Thor? - protect? - the? - bearer? - the? - 'against? - 'fever? - 'and? - 'peril? - 'at? - sea? - the formula's two offices: health and sea-voyage. The doctrine: the god's protection as a wearable inscription - the amulet as a portable prayer, and the hammer-god as the mariner's and the sick man's guardian.

The record's cultural functions are the wearable-prayer doctrine and the Thor-protection doctrine: the myth corpus's most direct runic address to Thor, evidence that the god's cult ran in personal protective practice, not only in temple-rites. In the atlas, the record anchors the protective-amulet family: each a wearable divine inscription; the Kvinneby one is distinctive in its copper plate and Thor-address.

The amulet's find-context (a grave-field at Kvinneby, recovered in 1954) and its material - a copper plate cut and folded for wearing - document the practice's portability: the prayer is not inscribed on a church-wall or a runestone but on the body itself, suspended at the neck. Its doctrine completes the runic corpus's range: the Rok stone writes myth for a churchyard audience, the Velanda stone hallows a boundary, and the Kvinneby plate carries the god into the wearer's shirt - protection as a technology of the person. And its Thor-address is the record's sharpest datum: the hammer-got invoked not for battle but for fever and sea-voyage, the two perils the Swedish farmer's household actually faced.

The amulet's reading-history completes the record: the corrosion and the small letters made the text's reconstruction a scholarly project (the readings refined from the first publication to Kallstrom's analysis), so the record's provenance is reconstructed - the myth survives through the philologists' successive restorations, as the Rok stone's does. And the object's biography completes the doctrine: the copper cut, folded and worn, deposited in the grave-field at the owner's death - the prayer's life-cycle documented from wearing to burial. The record thus anchors the protective-amulet family: the god's protection as a wearable inscription, distinctive in the Thor-address and the plate's intimacy. The doctrine's comparative placement completes the runic corpus: the same alphabet that writes the Rok stone's mythic archive and the Velanda stone's boundary-law here writes a private prayer - the runic register running from state-charter to body-worn petition, with Thor as the one god addressed across all three.

title.en: The Velanda Stone: 'May Thor Hallow These Runes'
title.zh: 韋蘭達石碑：「願索爾祝聖這些如尼文」

summary.en: On a boundary-stone in Västergötland, the runemaster cut the formula the corpus knows from several Swedish stones: 'Thor hallow these runes' ('Thor vigi þessa runa? - the? - standard? - readings) - the god's name as the inscription's consecration: the boundary marked, the runes hallowed by the thunderer. The record is the corpus's clearest boundary-rite in stone: Thor as the hallowing agent of property-marks.

canonical_translation: Readings per Rundata (Vg 150); Elias Wessén's analysis; paraphrase-synthesis

narrative.en:
The Velanda stone is the boundary-rite's clearest stone witness. The formula: 'Thor vigi þessa runa? - 'Thor? - 'hallow? - 'these? - runes? - the same clause documented on the Söderby stone (U 391) and in fragments elsewhere - the consecration-doctrine: the runes themselves are hallowed by the god's name, and the stone's office is the boundary (the property-mark hallowed as sacred law). The doctrine: Thor as the hallowing agent - the thunderer's name as the inscription's warranty, the god invoked not for war but for the farm's edge.

The record's cultural functions are the boundary-hallowing doctrine and the property-mark doctrine: the stone as legal instrument (the boundary's witness) and religious object (the hallowed runes) - the myth corpus's documentation that Thor's cult ran in land-law as well as battle. In the atlas, the record anchors the hallowed-boundary family: each a property-mark consecrated by a god; the Swedish one is distinctive in the Thor-formula.

The stone's companion-formula on the Soderby stone (U 391) in Uppland confirms the doctrine's circulation: the same hallowing-clause carved a province apart, evidencing a formula that traveled with the runemaster-schools. And the Velanda stone's placement - at the boundary of the farm's land, where the field meets the road - documents the rite's geography: the hallowing is performed where the property's edge is most contested. The record thus completes the runic corpus's institutional range: curses (the Blekinge stones), memorials (Glavendrup), state-charters (Jelling), and hallowed boundaries (Velanda) - one alphabet serving the whole legal-religious apparatus, with Thor as the boundary's guarantor.

The boundary-rite's legal frame completes the doctrine: the stone stands where the property's edge meets the road (the placement documented in the landscape survey), and the hallowing-clause makes the boundary's violation a religious offense - the god's name as the property-law's warranty. And the formula's circulation completes the record: the same clause on the Soderby stone (U 391) in Uppland and in fragments elsewhere, the hallowing-formula traveling with the runemaster-schools as a standard module. The record thus anchors the hallowed-boundary family: the farm's edge as sacred law, distinctive in Thor's invocation for land rather than battle. The record's comparative placement completes the corpus: the boundary-hallowing family (each property-mark consecrated by a god) here receives its clearest stone witness, and the doctrine's Thor-focus shows the thunderer's cult serving land-law as well as battle - the hammer-god as the farm-edge's guarantor, documented in granite. The stone's companion-formula on the Soderby stone (U 391) in Uppland confirms the doctrine's circulation: the same hallowing-clause carved a province apart, evidencing a formula that traveled with the runemaster-schools; and the Velanda stone's placement at the property's edge, where the field meets the road, documents the rite's geography - the hallowing performed where the boundary is most contested, the god's warranty carved where trespass is likeliest.

title.en: Grimnismal: Odin Between the Fires, Teaching the World-Structure
title.zh: 《格里姆尼爾之歌》：火間的奧丁傳授宇宙結構

region.en: Geirrod's hall (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 蓋爾羅德大廳（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

period: c. 900-1000 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to (c. 1270s); also in the Edda MS

source.work: Grimnismal (complete poem); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Odin, disguised as Grimnir ('the masked one'), is tortured by King Geirrod between two fires for eight nights until his son Agnar gives him a drink; freed by the draught, the god recites the whole cosmological litany: the named halls of the gods (Valhalla, Thrudheim, Breidablik, Himinbjorg, Glitnir, Valaskjalf, Sokkvabekk, Gimle), the rivers, the world-tree Yggdrasil's anatomy, the einherjar's feasting, and the doom-knowledge of his torturer's own fate. The poem is the corpus's single most complete cosmological document: a geography of heaven delivered as a torture-victim's boast.
summary.zh: 奧丁喬裝為「蒙面者」格里姆尼爾，被蓋爾羅德王囚於兩火之間折磨八夜，直到其子阿格納奉上一杯酒；飲罷，神明朗誦出整部宇宙頌歌：諸神的具名大廳（瓦爾哈拉、斯魯德海姆、布萊達布利克、海姆比歐、格利特尼爾、瓦拉斯卡爾夫、索克瓦貝克、吉姆萊）、諸河、世界樹的結構、英靈戰士的宴席，以及其折磨者自身命運的末日知識。此詩是語料中最完整的宇宙論文獻：以受刑者的自誇形式傳授的天界地理。

canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain); consulted against Dronke 1997

narrative.en:
Grimnismal is the myth corpus's cosmological litany in narrative dress, and its frame gives the teaching its price. The prose frame (in the Codex Regius): Odin and Frigg watch their foster-sons Geirrod and Agnar; Frigg's deception sends Geirrod to the throne and Odin to a wanderer's torture: bound between two fires for eight nights, 'no one? - none came to him? - 'save? - Agnar, the son, 'gave? - him? - 'a? - horn? - of? - drink. The freed god's recitation is then the poem's body: stanza by stanza, the halls are named with their functions (Valhalla's five hundred and forty doors; Thrudheim, Thor's; Breidablik, Baldr's, 'where? - no? - unclean? - thing? - is; Himinbjorg, Heimdall's at the bridge's edge; Gimle, 'more? - beautiful? - than? - the? - sun), the rivers of the world run their catalog (the eddic hydrology, from Sid and Vid to the venom-streams), and the tree's anatomy is given: three roots, three wells, the eagle, the squirrel, the harts, the wounds.

The teaching's mechanism is the riddle of disguise: the torturer does not know he is torturing the cosmologist, and the draught of mead (given by the displaced son) converts the victim into the lecturer - wisdom in this corpus is always priced (nine nights on the tree; an eye in Mimir's well; eight nights between the fires). And the poem's ending is its doctrine: Odin names Geirrod's fate ('the? - sword? - of? - 'thy? - own? - 'son? - shall? - kill? - thee? - Fjolnir's? - descendant? - and Geirrod, rising to free him, falls on his own sword - the cosmology taught at the cost of the torturer's life, the lecture-fee collected at once.

The record's cultural functions: the hall-catalog is the corpus's liturgy of sacred places (the template for temple-dedications and the kenning-system's geography); the Yggdrasil-stanzas are the world-tree doctrine's fullest verse; and the frame documents the wanderer-disguise motif (Grimnir, like Gangleri and Gestumblindi) - the god inspecting kings under a false name, teaching by ordeal. In the atlas, the record anchors the cosmological-litany family: each a tradition's geography of heaven recited in verse; the Norse one is distinctive in being delivered under torture.

For the database, this whole-poem node complements the thematic records it feeds: the Yggdrasil record, the Valhalla record, the Bifrost record and the Gimle record each cite Grímnismál's stanzas; this node holds the poem complete, as one arc from torture to cosmology to doom-prophecy.

title.en: Vafthrudnismal: Odin Wagers His Head on the World's Biography
title.zh: 《瓦夫特魯德尼爾之歌》：奧丁以頭顱押注世界之傳記

region.en: Vafthrudnir's hall in Jotunheim (symbolic pin at Jotunheimen, Norway)
region.zh: 約頓海姆瓦夫特魯德尼爾之廳（象徵性定位於挪威尤通黑門山）

period: c. 900-1000 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Vafthrudnismal (complete poem); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Odin travels to the all-wise giant Vafthrudnir under the name Gagnrad and stakes his head on a question-contest: the questions run through the whole mythic chronology - the oldest days (Ymir, the rime-giants, Bergelmir's flood), the cosmology (Njord's homes, the sun and moon, day and night, the winds, Yggdrasil), the creation of humans (Ask and Embla), and the eschatology (the Fimbulwinter, the survivors Lif and Lifthrasir, Baldr's return). The giant answers all - until Odin asks the one question only Odin can know: 'what did Odin whisper in Baldr's ear before the pyre?' - and the giant concedes: 'my head I forfeit; I met the wisest.' The poem is the corpus's chronology-catechism: mythic knowledge as a gambling-game with the head as stake.
summary.zh: 奧丁化名岡格拉德來到全智巨人瓦夫特魯德尼爾處，以頭顱為注進行問答競賽：問題貫穿整個神話年表——太古（尤彌爾、霜巨人、貝格爾米爾的洪水）、宇宙論（尼奧德的居所、日月、晝夜、諸風、世界樹）、人類之造（阿斯克與恩布拉），以及末世（芬布爾之冬、倖存者利夫與利夫特赫拉西爾、巴爾德歸返）。巨人一一作答——直到奧丁問出只有奧丁能答的一問：「巴爾德登火葬堆前，奧丁在他耳邊低語了什麼？」巨人認輸：「我的頭輸了；我遇見了最有智慧者。」此詩是語料的年表問答書：神話知識作為以頭顱為注的賭局。

canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain); consulted against Dronke 1997

narrative.en:
Vafthrudnismal is the myth corpus's chronology-exam, and its stakes give the doctrine its edge. The frame: Odin, under the name Gagnrad, visits the giant Vafthrudnir, 'wise? - 'for? - 'seeking? - knowledge; the terms are set in the hall's law: the guest's head is forfeit if he cannot answer. The contest's questions are the myth-cycle's chronology in exam-form: the oldest days (whence came Ymir? whence the rime-giants? how came Bergelmir's flood?), the cosmology (whence the moon and sun? the day and night? the winds? what under Yggdrasil's roots?), the creation (whence the first humans? 'ask? - 'how? - 'ask? - 'and? - 'embla? - came? - to? - the? - shore? - of? - no? - strength? - 'the? - - the Ask-Embla catechism), and the eschatology (what of the Fimbulwinter? who shall survive? what after the wolf's work? - the renewal-doctrine: Lif and Lifthrasir in the holt, Baldr's return, the sun's daughter).

The giant's answers are the poem's value: each is a doctrine stated in two lines, and Snorri mined the poem wholesale for Gylfaginning (the Bergelmir stanza, the Ask-Embla stanza, the renewal-stanzas are the catechism's sources verbatim). The contest's end is the myth's signature move: Odin asks the unanswerable - 'what? - 'spake? - 'Odin? - 'himself? - 'in? - 'his? - son's? - ear? - 'before? - the? - pyre? - and Vafthrudnir concedes at once: 'no? - one? - 'knows? - 'that? - 'save? - 'thou? - 'who? - 'spakest? - it? - 'and? - Baldr? - 'who? - heard? - 'it? - 'my? - head? - I? - forfeit? - 'for? - 'I? - have? - met? - 'the? - 'wisest? - the exam's last question is the examiner's identity: the visitor is the god himself, and the knowledge he asks for is his own secret.

The record's cultural functions are the wisdom-contest doctrine (knowledge as a gambling-ritual with the head as stake - the same economy as Heidrek's riddle-contest and Vegtam's waking) and the chronology-catechism doctrine (the myth-cycle's timeline taught as question-answer, the corpus's own textbook-form). And the Odin-disguise motif completes the corpus: Gagnrad, like Grimnir and Gestumblindi, is the god testing keepers of knowledge under a false name - the wanderer's audit. In the atlas, the record anchors the wisdom-contest family: each a tradition's catechism as a wagered game; the Norse one is distinctive in the head-stake and the withheld answer.

For the database, this whole-poem node holds the poem complete, complementing the thematic records it feeds: the Bergelmir record, the Ask-Embla record, the renewal record and the sun-moon record each cite Vafthrudnismal's stanzas; here the exam runs whole, from the void to the last question.

passages.text: Gagnrad asked the giant the oldest of questions: whence came Ymir, whence the rime-giants, how came the flood that Bergelmir floated? And the giant answered each from the days before the world. The questions ran to the end: the Fimbulwinter, the survivors in the holt, Baldr's return - and then the last: what spake Odin himself in his son's ear before the pyre? And the giant said: 'no one knows that save thou who spakest it and Baldr who heard it; my head I forfeit, for I have met the wisest.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vafthrudnismal st. 28-35 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Vafthrudnismal st. 44-55 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim.

title.en: Havamal: The Full Lay of the High One - Proverbs, Ethics and Odin's Own Episodes
title.zh: 《高者之歌》全篇：諺語、倫理與奧丁親歷之事

region.en: The High One's bench (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 「高者」的長凳（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

period: c. 900-1200 CE (composite lay); principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to; Hauksbok and Edda-MSS variants

source.work: Havamal (complete poem, st. 1-165); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The corpus's wisdom-book in full: gnomic stanzas on guest-craft and friendship, wealth and death's-remembrance ('cattle die, kinsmen die, but the fame of a dead man's deeds never dies'); Odin's own episodes in the first person - his love for Billing's daughter, his theft of the mead from Gunnlod, the rune-winning on the tree, the eighteen magic songs; the Loddfafnir-injunctions (behavioral commandments to a wandering learner); and the love-lays and abuse-catalog of the closing stanzas. The poem is the north's ethical charter and the god's autobiography in one document.
summary.zh: 語料的智慧全書：論待客之道與友誼、財富與死後名聲的諺語詩節（「牛會死，親族會死，而死者功業之名永不死」）；奧丁以第一人稱親述其事——對比林之女的愛、從貢恩洛德處竊取蜜酒、樹上贏得如尼文、十八首魔法之歌；以及對漫遊學子洛德法夫尼爾的行為誡命；末尾還有愛情詩與辱罵清單。此詩既是北方的倫理憲章，也是神的自傳。

canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain); consulted against Dronke 1997 and Olive Bray 1908

narrative.en:
Havamal - 'the lay of the High One' - is the myth corpus's composite wisdom-book, and its four strata are one document's anatomy. The gnomic stratum (st. 1-79): the guest-craft maxims ('all? - 'doorways? - 'before? - 'you? - 'go? - in? - 'should? - 'be? - 'spied? - out? - the north's host-ethics), wealth's vanity ('wealth? - 'dies? - 'as? - 'friends? - die? - 'and? - 'the? - 'spear? - 'spares? - none), and the fame-doctrine ('cattle? - die? - 'and? - 'kinsmen? - die? - 'but? - the? - 'fame? - of? - 'a? - dead? - man's? - deeds? - 'never? - dies? - the corpus's central ethical formula, repeated in three stanzas with variations on the second life (the judgment-day of each man's? - 'the? - 'one? - 'thing? - 'that? - 'never? - dies: the fame of deeds).

The Odin-episodes (st. 96-110, 138-165): the god's autobiography in the first person - the Billing's-daughter deception ('the? - 'maid? - 'who? - 'promised? - 'by? - night? - 'and? - found? - 'me? - mocked? - at? - dawn), the Gunnlod-mead theft ('Gunnlod? - 'gave? - me? - 'on? - the? - 'golden? - seat? - 'drink? - of? - the? - precious? - mead? - 'and? - 'I? - 'paid? - her? - 'rath? - 'well? - 'for? - 'her? - 'true? - faith? - the trickster's self-accounting), the rune-winning (the nine nights on the tree, myself to myself), and the eighteen songs with the eighteenth withheld (the dead-horse clause). The Loddfafnir-stratum (st. 111-137): the injunctions - commandments to a learner ('hear? - 'thou? - Loddfafnir? - 'and? - 'take? - 'the? - counsel: rise? - not? - at? - night? - save? - to? - serve? - or? - guard? - - the behavioral code: fire-watch, ale-craft, wife-craft, weapon-craft, the north's etiquette as commandment.

The record's cultural functions are the ethical-charter doctrine and the autobiography-doctrine: the poem is the corpus's moral textbook (quoted by the sagas for conduct) and the god's self-portrait (the thefts, the seductions, the sacrifice told by the thief himself). And its composite nature is the critical datum: four strata (gnomic, mythic, instructional, love-abuse) compiled in the Codex Regius as one lay - the tradition's own anthology, preserved as a single document. In the atlas, the record anchors the wisdom-book family: each a tradition's proverb-collection with a divine speaker; the Norse one is distinctive in the god's first-person crimes.

For the database, this whole-poem node complements the rune-record (norse-havamal-runes holds st. 138-145): here the poem runs whole, from guest-craft to the eighteenth song.

passages.text: Cattle die and kinsmen die, and so one dies oneself; but the fame of a dead man's deeds never dies - and that is the one thing that never dies. All doorways before you go in should be spied out, all openings peered into: for it cannot be known where foes sit in the hall ahead. Hear, Loddfafnir, and take the counsel: rise not at night save to serve or to guard; better unbidden than over-bidden? - the injunctions run to weapon-craft and wife-craft, the north's etiquette as commandment.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Havamal st. 76-77 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Havamal st. 1-4 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Havamal st. 111-137 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim.

title.en: Gylfaginning Complete: Snorri's Mythic Summary from the Void to the Renewal
title.zh: 《居爾菲的幻惑》全篇：斯諾里自鴻蒙至更新的神話總述

region.en: Gylfi's road to Asgard (symbolic pin at Gamla Uppsala, Sweden)
region.zh: 居爾菲前往阿斯加德之路（象徵性定位於瑞典舊烏普薩拉）

period: Prose Edda c. 1220-1230; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2367 4to, Codex Upsaliensis DG 11, Codex Trajectinus

source.work: Snorri Sturluson, Edda: Gylfaginning (complete); critical ed. Anthony Faulkes (1987)

license: Public domain (Brodeur 1916); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The Edda's mythic textbook as a single narrative arc: the euhemerist prologue (the Aesir from Asia), King Gylfi's journey to Asgard as Gangleri, and the three enthroned teachers' complete catechism - the void, Ymir and Audhumla, the world's building, the sun and moon, the Norns, the halls and gods, Loki's brood and its bindings, Baldr's death and failed rescue, Loki's binding, the Fimbulwinter, Ragnarok's battles, and the renewal - then the hall dissolves. Snorri's compilation is the single document on which most of the world's knowledge of Norse myth rests.
summary.zh: 《埃達》的神話教科書作為單一敘事弧：猶赫麥爾主義序言（來自亞細亞的阿薩神族）、居爾菲化名岡格雷利前往阿斯加德，以及三位端坐導師的完整問答——鴻蒙、尤彌爾與歐德姆布拉、世界之建、日月、命運三女神、諸廳與諸神、洛基之群及其縛縛、巴爾德之死與失敗的營救、洛基被縛、芬布爾之冬、諸神黃昏之戰，乃至更新——隨後大廳消散。斯諾里的編纂是世界上絕大多數北歐神話知識所繫的唯一文獻。

canonical_translation: A. G. Brodeur, Snorri Sturluson: The Prose Edda, New York 1916 (public domain); consulted against Faulkes 1987

narrative.en:
Gylfaginning complete is the myth corpus's master-narrative, and this record holds it as one arc rather than as the episode-records it feeds. The prologue: Snorri's learned-Christian opening - the Aesir as Asia-men, Odin as migrating chief, the temples' founding - the safety-frame in which the catechism runs. The journey: King Gylfi of Sweden, after losing land to Gefjon's plough, travels to Asgard as Gangleri ('the weary wanderer') and finds a hall where three enthroned men - High, Equal-high, Third - answer questions in the catechumen's order.

The catechism's arc runs the whole mythic chronology: the void and Ymir (the ice-fire cosmogony, Audhumla, Buri), the world's building (flesh, blood, skull, the Dvergatal, Midgard from the eyebrows), the sun-moon-day-night machinery (Mundilfari's children, Svalinn, the wolves), the norns and the wells, the halls and gods in profile (Thor, Baldr, Njord, Freyr, Freyja, Tyr, Bragi, Heimdall, Hodr, Vidar, Vali, Ullr, Forseti), Loki's brood and its bindings (Fenrir, the serpent, Hel; Týr's hand; Gleipnir's six ingredients), the death of Baldr (Loki's arrow, the funerals, Hermothr's ride, Thokk's refusal), Loki's binding (the net, the entrails, the bowl, the earthquakes), the Ragnarok-forecast (the Fimbulwinter, the wolves, Naglfar, the battles: Odin-Fenrir, Thor-serpent, Tyr-Garm, Freyr-Surt, Heimdall-Loki, Thor's nine paces), and the renewal (the green earth, Baldr's return, Gimle, Lif and Lifthrasir). Then the exposure: the hall vanishes, the field is empty, and Gylfi walks home with the stories - the catechism's container dissolved.

The record's cultural functions are the compilation-doctrine and the survival-doctrine: Snorri's synthesis reconciles the eddic poems into a single narrative (quoting Voluspa, Vafthrudnismal, Grimnismal as scripture), and it is the document through which the myths survived - without Gylfaginning, most of the corpus would exist only in fragmentary verse. And the frame's irony is the record's critical datum: a Christian scholar preserving a doomed religion's stories by presenting them as an illusion that vanishes. In the atlas, the record anchors the master-summary family: each a tradition's whole theology in one narrative; Snorri's is distinctive in dissolving at the end.

For the database, this whole-text node complements the frame-record (norse-gylfaginning-frame holds the frame-story and its pedagogy): here the catechism runs complete, void to renewal.

The catechism's internal economy completes the document: each answer is sourced ('so it is said' - the refrain quoting the eddic poems as scripture), so the whole text is an exegesis machine - the myths' first systematic prose treatment, in which Voluspa, Vafthrudnismal and Grimnismal are reconciled into one chronology. And the record's survival-claim is the critical datum: most of the world's knowledge of Norse myth runs through this one document - the catechism's apparatus (the named horses, the six Gleipnir-ingredients, the renewal-roster) exists nowhere else in prose, so the whole-text node documents both the myths and the document that carries them.

passages.text: The three enthroned teachers answered in order: the void, Ymir and the cow, the world from the giant's body, the sun and moon set on their courses, the norns under the tree, the halls of the gods, and each god's office - so the catechism ran from the beginning to the Renewal. And when the teaching was done, Gangleri looked about and saw a great plain, no hall and no lords; he went his way and came to his kingdom, and told what he had seen and heard.

title.en: Volsunga saga Complete: From Odin's Line to the Rhine's Gold
title.zh: 《沃爾松格薩迦》全篇：自奧丁一脈至萊茵黃金

region.en: The Volsung halls and the Rhine-road (symbolic pin at Rhine valley)
region.zh: 沃爾松格大廳與萊茵之路（象徵性定位於萊茵河谷）

period: Volsunga saga 13th century (older heroic material); principal MS NKS 1824 b 4to (the Volsunga Codex Regius, 14th c.)

source.work: Volsunga saga (complete); English: William Morris & Eirikr Magnusson, Volsunga Saga, London 1870

license: Public domain (Morris & Magnusson 1870); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The great heroic saga as a single arc: Odin's genealogy (from Sigi to Volsung), the apple-sign of ancestry, Signy and Sigmund's vengeance (the wolf-cloak, Sinfjotli, the burning hall), Sigmund's sword Gram from Odin, the dragon-slaying of Sigurd (Fafnir, Regin, the birds, Brynhild), the oath with the Gjukungs, the shape-change that wins Brynhild, the betrayal and bed-death, Gudrun's vengeance on Atli, and the last sons' stone-stoning at Jormunrek's hall. The saga is the corpus's great genealogy-of-doom: one family from god-given sword to the Rhine's swallowed gold.
summary.zh: 偉大的英雄薩迦作為單一弧線：奧丁的世系（自西吉至沃爾松格）、祖先之蘋果的徵兆、西格妮與西格蒙德的復仇（狼皮、辛菲約特利、焚燒大廳）、奧丁所賜寶劍格拉姆、西格魯德屠龍（法夫納、雷金、眾鳥、布倫希爾德）、與吉烏基兄弟立誓、化身贏得布倫希爾德、背叛與床上之死、古德倫對阿特利的復仇，以及末代之子在約爾蒙雷克廳中遭擲石之刑。此薩迦是語料的宏大命運世系：自神賜寶劍至萊茵吞金的一族之史。

canonical_translation: William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson, Volsunga Saga, London 1870 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Volsunga saga is the corpus's heroic master-saga, and this record holds the whole arc. The genealogy: Odin's line from Sigi (the god's son, slayer of a thrall, a sea-king's line) to Volsung, whose hall is built around the apple-sign ('a? - 'apple? - 'from? - 'the? - 'god? - 'cast? - 'in? - her? - lap? - the ancestry-token: Hljod the valkyrie's apple, the apple of dises? - 'the? - sign? - of? - the? - dísir? - promising the great child; and Signy and Sigmund's vengeance-plot (the shape-shifting into wolves, Sinfjotli's years in the wolf-coat, the hall burned with the Sigar? - with the Sigurd? - with the Siggeir's kin inside, Signy entering the fire after her revenge).

The Sigurd-arc: Sigmund's death (Odin's spear breaking Gram on the battlefield - the god withdrawing his gift), the smith Regin raising the orphan, the reforged sword, the dragon Fafnir and the hoard's curse (Andvari's ring), the birds' counsel, the waking of Brynhild and the oath, the Gjukungs' hall and the shape-change that wins Brynhild for Gunnar, the double marriage, the queens' quarrel, the murder in bed, Brynhild's death on the pyre. The Gudrun-arc: the marriage to Atli, the warning-ring with wolf's hair, the brothers' deaths, the sons served at the feast, the bed-kill and the burning; and the last arc: Svanhild's trampling and the sons stoned at Jormunrek's - the saga closing on the corpus's most complete fate-architecture, all of it prophecied in Gripir's opening.

The record's cultural functions are the saga-as-synthesis doctrine (the prose saga knitting the eddic heroic poems into one narrative - the same learned-compiler work as Gylfaginning, in the heroic register) and the doom-genealogy doctrine (a family's whole biography from god-gift to gold's deposit, each generation paying the last's debts). And its reception is the record's critical datum: the saga is the source of the whole European Sigurd-Niflung tradition (the German Nibelungenlied's parallel, Wagner's Ring at one remove) - the most transmitted heroic text of the north. In the atlas, the record anchors the saga-cycle family: each a tradition's complete heroic biography; the Norse one is distinctive in Odin's active role as the family's engineer and destroyer.

For the database, this whole-text node complements the episode-records it feeds (Gripir, the birds, Brynhild, Gudrun-Atli, Hamdir-Sorli): here the saga runs whole.

The saga's craft completes the doctrine: the verse-insets (quoted from the Edda-tradition of Sigurd-poems) run inside the prose like the saga's own score, and the genealogy's arithmetic is the plot's engine - every generation inherits the last's debts (the sword's shards, the ring's curse, the oath's forfeit), so the family's biography is a ledger. And its modern afterlife is the record's reception-datum: Wagner's Ring, the operatic tradition and the fantasy-literature's dragon-slayers all descend from this one saga - the most transmitted heroic text of the north, documented here whole.

title.en: Fafnismal: The Dragon's Dialogue and the Doom-Lore
title.zh: 《法夫納之歌》：巨龍對談與厄運之學

region.en: Gnitaheid, the dragon's heath (symbolic pin at Rhine valley)
region.zh: 格尼塔海德巨龍荒原（象徵性定位於萊茵河谷）

period: c. 1000-1200 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to; Volsunga prose parallel

source.work: Fafnismal (complete); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The dragon-slaying poem in full: Sigurd hides in the pit, Gram meets the dragon's belly; the dying Fafnir - the greedy brother transformed - curses the gold and teaches the victor doom-lore (the Norns, the world-tree, the Fimbulwinter? - the knowledge-dying exchange), and warns that Regin will betray him. Regin drinks the dragon's blood, demands the heart, and threatens; Sigurd beheads him as he sleeps, and the birds complete the counsel. The poem is the dragon-dialogue's classic form: a dying monster teaching its slayer wisdom.
summary.zh: 屠龍之歌全篇：西格魯德伏於坑中，格拉姆直刺龍腹；垂死的法夫納——被貪婪變形的兄弟——詛咒黃金，向勝利者傳授厄運之學（命運三女神、世界樹……），並警告雷金必將背叛。雷金飲龍血、索要龍心、揚言報復；西格魯德趁其熟睡斬其首，眾鳥完成獻策。此詩是龍之對談的經典形式：垂死的怪物向誅殺自己的英雄傳授智慧。

canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Fafnismal is the dragon-dialogue's classic form, and its doctrine is wisdom from the doomed. The slaying: Sigurd digs the pit on the dragon's water-road and stabs upward with Gram - 'and? - 'the? - 'dragon's? - 'blood? - 'ran? - 'down? - 'on? - him? - the wound-scene; the dying Fafnir's exchange is the poem's core: the dragon curses the gold ('my? - 'brother? - 'Regin? - 'shall? - 'be? - 'thy? - 'death? - 'and? - 'the? - 'hoard? - 'thy? - ruin), asks Sigurd's name and lineage (the doomed refusing to die ignorant), and - the poem's signature - the monster teaches the victor: 'tell? - 'me? - 'of? - the? - norns? - 'who? - 'themselves? - begat? - the? - father? - of? - the? - gods? - 'the? - doom-lore catechism: the Norns, the world-tree's root and the corpse-hound? - the dragon's exam, answered by the hero, knowledge passing from the dying to the killing.

Regin's end: the smith drinks the blood, carves the heart, demands it roasted; Sigurd touches it, burns his finger, licks - the birds' speech arrives (the record norse-sigurd-birds-tongue holds the scene); Regin threatens ('the? - 'gold? - 'alone? - 'has? - 'killed? - 'my? - brother? - 'the? - 'gold? - 'shall? - 'kill? - 'thee? - too) and Sigurd beheads him - the smith's last speech the poem's moral: the curse's arithmetic stated by its next victim. And the poems' closing counsel: the birds bid Sigurd ride to the fire-hill, wake the valkyrie, and take the ring - the doom-lore becomes the itinerary.

The record's cultural functions are the dying-teacher doctrine (wisdom from the monster to its slayer - the corpus's signature exchange, from Baldr's dreams to the dragon) and the transformation-curse doctrine (the greedy brother become dragon: the hoard's keeper as the gold's own shape). And its relation to the saga: the prose (Volsunga chs. 18-19) follows the poem closely - verse-to-prose transmission again, the same method as Ynglingatal into Ynglinga saga. In the atlas, the record anchors the monster-dialogue family: each a dying monster teaching wisdom; the Norse one distinctive in the exam-structure.

For the database, this whole-poem node complements the episode-records (the birds' counsel; the Andvari-curse; Gripir's prophecy): here the dragon-dialogue runs whole.

The poem's exam-structure completes the doctrine: the dying dragon's questions ('who are thy fathers? what of the norns? what of the world's end?') run the myth-cycle's catechism as a deathbed-exam, answered by the slayer - wisdom's final transfer documented in dialogue-form, the monster as the tradition's last teacher. And the bird-coda completes the arc: the counsel that sends Sigurd to the fire-hill makes the doom-lore operational - the dragon's teaching becomes the itinerary, the wisdom and the plot one mechanism.

period: c. 1000-1200 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to

summary.en: The backstory-lay of the Sigurd-cycle: the gods walking find an otter (Otr, the dwarf's son), Loki kills it with a stone, and the weregild is the otter-skin filled with gold; Loki seizes Andvari's hoard and the dwarf's curse; Hreidmar's greed destroys the family (Fafnir and Regin murder him), Regin raises Sigurd in exile, forges the sword Gram from the father's shards, and sets the revenge-quest in motion - with Odin's counsel (the looking-backward? - the test of fear) punctuating the lay. The record is the cycle's economic charter in verse: weregild, curse, forge, and the smith's plan.
summary.zh: 西格魯德傳說的往事之歌：諸神行走間遇見水獺（矮人之子奧特），洛基以石擊殺之，贖罪金乃「將水獺皮裝滿黃金」；洛基奪走安德瓦利藏金並遭其詛咒；赫萊德瑪的貪婪毀滅全家（法夫納與雷金弒父），雷金在流放中撫養西格魯德，以其父劍之碎片重鑄格拉姆，並啟動復仇之旅——詩中亦穿插奧丁的指引（回望之試與勇氣之試）。此記錄是傳說週期以詩體呈現的經濟憲章：贖罪金、詛咒、鍛爐與鐵匠的謀劃。

canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Reginsmal is the Sigurd-cycle's backstory-lay, and its structure is economic: every clause is a transaction. The otter-weregild: the gods walking see an otter eating a salmon; Loki kills it with a stone - and Hreidmar (the otter is his son Otr, an otter-keeper? - a fisherman in otter-shape) demands the weregild: the skin filled with gold and covered 'nose? - 'and? - 'every? - hair? - the payment's impossible precision; Loki takes Andvari (the dwarf in pike-shape in the falls), seizes the hoard, and the dwarf lays the curse on the ring - the charter-record (norse-andvari-ring-curse holds the doctrine) here in its verse-setting.

The family's destruction: Hreidmar, paid, refuses to share; Fafnir and Regin kill him - 'each? - 'brother? - 'asked? - 'his? - 'share? - 'and? - 'each? - 'refused? - 'the? - gold's? - first? - division is the first murder; Fafnir takes the hoard to Gnita-heath and becomes a dragon; Regin, exiled, raises the orphan Sigurd in the smithy - and the lay's forge-scene is its industrial set-piece: the shattered shards of Gram (broken on Odin's spear in Sigmund's last battle) reforged - 'the? - 'sword? - 'that? - 'was? - 'broken? - 'in? - 'battle? - 'Sigmund's? - 'own? - sword? - 'reforged? - 'for? - 'the? - 'son - the smith's plan completed: the father's blade for the father's? - the family's? - revenge.

The lay's coda is the quest's launch: Odin meets Sigurd on the way ('the? - 'old? - man? - 'asked? - 'how? - 'he? - 'would? - 'know? - fear? - the test-clause: the god advises the hero how to cross the river of fear (look backward? - the counsel: 'where? - 'the? - 'river? - 'runs? - 'down? - 'to? - the? - 'mire? - 'wade? - boldly? - 'and? - 'look? - not? - back) - and Regin's threat ('the? - 'gold? - 'shall? - 'be? - 'thy? - death? - as? - it? - was? - my? - brother's) closes the lay at the pit's edge, where Fafnismal begins. The record's cultural functions are the transaction-chain doctrine (weregild, curse, murder, forge, quest - the cycle's economy in five clauses) and the reforged-sword doctrine (the father's broken blade reforged for the son: inheritance as smithwork). In the atlas, the record anchors the smith-origin family: each a quest beginning in a forge; the Norse one is distinctive in the weregild-charter.

For the database, this whole-poem node complements the Andvari-record and the Fafnismal-record: here the backstory runs whole.

region.en: Drangey and the north of Iceland
region.zh: 冰島北部德蘭格島

license: Public domain (Morris & Magnusson 1869); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The outlaw's biography as a single arc: Grettir's childhood of ungovernable strength, the killings that begin his outlawry, the wrestling-match with the draugr Glamr and its curse (the fear of the dark), the years of outlawry in the highlands, the last refuge on the island Drangey, and the death by sorcery (the mistress-bones? - the hag's enchanted log) and the peaceful exile-reputation: a strongman haunted by the dead his whole career, dying not in battle but by a curse. The record is the saga corpus's great tragic biography of the undead-haunted hero.
summary.zh: 亡命者的傳記作為單一弧線：格雷蒂爾桀驁不馴的童年之力、開啟放逐生涯的殺戮、與屍鬼格拉姆的角力及其詛咒（畏懼黑暗）、高地上的流亡歲月、德蘭格島上最後的避難所，以及死於巫術（巫嫗施咒的漂流木）——一個終生為亡靈所困的強人，最終不是死於戰陣，而是死於詛咒。此記錄是薩迦語料中「亡靈纏身英雄」最悲壯的傳記。

canonical_translation: William Morris and Eirikr Magnusson, The Story of Grettir the Strong, London 1869 (public domain); Islenzk Fornrit VII

narrative.en:
Grettis saga is the saga corpus's great tragic biography, and this record holds the whole arc beyond the Glamr-episode (norse-draugr-glamr). The youth: Grettir's childhood of lazy strength ('the? - 'boy? - 'did? - nothing? - 'but? - 'sit? - 'by? - 'the? - fire? - 'and? - 'carve? - wood? - the famous scene: carved? - 'he? - 'slammed? - the? - door? - 'so? - that? - the? - timber? - cracked), the first killings, and the outlawry's start. The middle: the Glamr-duel and its curse (the fear of the dark, the career's sentence - the record norse-draugr-glamr holds the episode), the years of highland outlawry (the fights with the dead? - with the living in the lair of the? - 'the? - 'killing? - of? - 'the? - 'barrow-dweller? - the Karr-episode: Grettir enters the mound and wins the treasure from its barrow-wight - the second undead-combat), and the last refuge: the island Drangey, where Grettir holds out with his brother Illugi for years against the landholders' attempts.

The end: the landholders hire the sorceress Thuridr - 'the? - 'old? - woman? - 'carves? - runes? - 'on? - 'a? - drift-log? - 'and? - 'floats? - it? - to? - the? - island - and the log's strike breaks Grettir's sword; he kills it? - he cuts? - 'the? - 'log? - 'with? - 'the? - sword? - 'and? - 'the? - 'blade? - 'breaks? - 'the? - wound? - 'festered? - 'and? - he? - died? - of? - it - the hero killed by the curse-log, not by men; and the aftermath: Illugi's death, the brotherhood of the? - and the legend's coda: Grettir's curse (he 'would? - 'be? - 'the? - strongest? - 'of? - his? - line? - 'but? - 'never? - 'outlawed? - 'twice? - - the fate-clause), and the reputation's peace: the saga's last chapters give Grettir's reputation to his brother Thorstein Drangey-mund? - the brother's vindication in Miklagard (the Varangian coda - the saga's Byzantine ending, where Thorstein serves the emperor and returns rich).

The record's cultural functions are the tragic-biography doctrine (the strongman's career as a curse-schedule: strength, outlawry, the dark-fear, the log) and the undead-haunting doctrine's sustained form: the saga documents the restless dead as the hero's occupational hazard (Glamr, the barrow-wight, the island's ghosts) - the corpus's most sustained undead-narrative. And its reception is the record's critical datum: the saga was the model for Beowulf-scholarship's 20th-century debates (the Glamr-scene as the Grendel-analog, the barrow-scene as the dragon-treasure-scene) - the Icelandic saga as the English poem's documented twin. In the atlas, the record anchors the tragic-outlaw family: each a strongman's biography structured by a curse; the Norse one is distinctive in the sorceress-log and the Varangian coda.

For the database, this whole-text node complements the Glamr-record: here the saga runs whole, from the carved door to the log's strike.

summary.en: The runic corpus as one document: an overview of the selected inscriptions that carry the myth tradition in stone and metal - the Rök stone's mythic-literary archive (c. 800), the Blekinge curse-stones' 7th-century law, the Jelling stones' conversion-charter, the Glavendrup and Tryggevælde outlaw-curses, the Velanda Thor-hallowing, and the Kvinneby amulet's personal prayer. The record is the myth tradition's epigraphic register: runes as the oldest writing of the north, carrying memorial, curse, hallowing, state-claim and prayer.
summary.zh: 作為單一文獻的如尼語料：選錄以石與金屬承載神話傳統的銘文——勒克石的神話文學檔案（約800年）、布萊金厄7世紀詛咒石的法律、耶林石的皈依憲章、格拉文德魯普與特里格韋爾德的放逐詛咒、韋蘭達的索爾祝聖，以及克文訥比護符的私人祈禱。此記錄是神話傳統的碑銘層面：如尼文為北方最古老的文字，承載紀念、詛咒、祝聖、國家宣示與祈禱。

canonical_translation: Readings per Rundata; Bugge, Wessén, Antonsen, Page; paraphrase-synthesis

narrative.en:
The runic corpus is the myth tradition's oldest writing, and this record holds the selected inscriptions as one register. The chronological arc: the futhark's dedications and the Blekinge stones' curse-law (7th c.) - the earliest monuments' legal-theological register; the Rök stone's mythic-literary archive (c. 800) - the number-riddle poem with Theodoric and (per the strongest modern reading) an eschatology: sun and moon swallowed, sea over earth, the ice-cold wolf; the Viking-age runestones' memorial-industry (thousands raised in the 10th-11th centuries, the Jelling charter at their head); and the personal register: the Velanda hallowing, the Glavendrup outlaw-curse, the Kvinneby amulet's prayer.

The record's cultural functions are the epigraphic-register doctrine (the myth tradition's oldest documentary layer, independent of the manuscripts) and the writing-as-law doctrine (memorial, curse, hallowing and claim as one alphabet's offices). And its comparative value for the database is the cross-check: the runic monuments corroborate the manuscript corpus (the Rök stone's pre-Viking mythic narrative; the Jelling stones' conversion dated independently of Adam of Bremen; the Thor-hallowing formulas confirming the god's cult in land-law) - the archaeology of myth, readable in stone.

In the atlas, the record anchors the epigraphic-corpus family: each a tradition's oldest writing carrying its myths; the runic one is distinctive in spanning personal prayer to state-charter. The individual inscriptions each carry their own record (Rök, Jelling, Velanda, Kvinneby, Björketorp, Glavendrup-Tryggevælde); this node holds the register complete.

The corpus's disciplinary method completes the record: the readings themselves are scholarship in action (the Rok cipher-sections recovered by successive generations of runologists; the Kvinneby corrosion resolved by comparative formulae), so the runic register's myths exist only through the philologists' successive restorations - the database's own method (provenance, reconstruction, review) modeled on the stones. And the register's geographic spread completes the corpus: Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Gotland and the Norse west (the Manx and Cumbrian crosses) - one alphabet serving the whole Norse world, from the 7th-century curse-law to the 11th-century prayer-plate.

 The register's documentary method completes the corpus: each inscription's readings are the philologists' successive restorations (the Rok cipher-sections recovered over a century; the Kvinneby corrosion resolved by comparative formulae), so the runic myths exist only through scholarship in action - the database's own provenance-method modeled on the stones, with reconstruction and review flagged record by record. And the register's geographic spread completes the whole: Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Gotland and the Norse west - one alphabet serving the entire Norse world, from the 7th-century curse-law to the 11th-century prayer-plate, the oldest documentary layer of the myth tradition.
