And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

title.en: The Line of Cain: Shepherds, Singers, Smiths
title.zh: 該隱之系：牧者、歌者、鐵匠

region.en: Land of Nod, city of Enoch (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 流浪之地，以諾城（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 4

summary.en: In Cain's exiled line the arts of civilization are founded: Enoch builds the first city, Jabal the tents and cattle of herders, Jubal the harp and organ of music, Tubalcain the forging of brass and iron — while Lamech's boast of a blood-vengeance seventy-sevenfold darkens the lineage. In Christian tradition this culture-registry is shadowed by the city of man, set against the line of Seth that began to call on the name of the LORD.
summary.zh: 文明之藝起於該隱流放之系：以諾築首城，雅八創畜牧帳棚，猶八創琴瑟之音，土八該隱冶銅打鐵；而拉麥誇口復仇七十七倍，血染世系。基督教釋經以人之城對照塞特之系——彼時人才求告耶和華的名。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The inventor catalogue is presented as an etiological genealogy of the crafts.

passages.text: And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch. And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle. And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ. And Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron.

And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: for God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.

title.en: Enoch Walked with God, and Was Not
title.zh: 以諾與神同行，不見於世

region.en: The patriarchal line of Seth (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 塞特譜系（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 5 with Jude 14-15, Genesis c. 6th-5th century BCE; Jude 1st century CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Genesis 5 and Jude 1

summary.en: Amid the nine-hundred-year patriarchs of Genesis 5, Enoch alone walks with God, lives 365 years, and simply 'was not; for God took him' — scripture's first bodily translation to heaven. Christian tradition made him the archetype of the rapture, and the Epistle of Jude quotes Enoch as a prophet foretelling the Lord's coming with ten thousands of his saints.
summary.zh: 創世記譜系中壽數近千的族長之間，唯以諾與神同行三百年，三百六十五歲而「不見於世，因神取了他去」——聖經首位活升天者。基督教傳統以之為被提原型；猶大書更引以諾為先知，預言主偕萬聖降臨。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The translation of Enoch is presented alongside other taken-up narratives.

passages.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: and Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: and all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: and Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.

And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

title.en: Sons of God and the Nephilim
title.zh: 神之子與拿非利巨人

region.en: Antediluvian earth (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 洪水前之世界（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 6:1-4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 6

summary.en: When humanity multiplies, the 'sons of God' take the daughters of men as wives, and their children are the Nephilim — the giants, mighty men of old, men of renown. With this mixing of the divine and human orders God limits the human span to 120 years; Christian interpretive tradition (building on 1 Enoch) read the sons of God as fallen angels, the Watchers who taught forbidden arts and fathered the giants.
summary.zh: 人類繁衍之際，神之子見人之女子美，遂娶為妻；其子即拿非利——上古英武有名之巨人。神於是將人的年日限為一百二十年。基督教釋經（承《以諾一書》）視「神之子」為墮落天使即守望者，教人禁術，生下巨人。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Tagging the sons of God with divine-marriage is an interpretive act comparing divine-human unions across traditions; the giant tag follows the LXX/traditional reading of Nephilim as giants, noted here.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, that the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose. And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown. And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.

title.en: Noah and the Flood
title.zh: 挪亞與大洪水

region.en: The ark, resting on the mountains of Ararat
region.zh: 方舟，止於亞拉臘山

period: Genesis 6-9, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 6-9

summary.en: God, grieved that every imagination of the human heart is evil, resolves to destroy all flesh with a flood and commands the just Noah to build a three-deck ark of gopher wood. The fountains of the great deep break up, rain falls forty days, all life drowns except the ark's eight souls and their beasts; a dove bearing an olive leaf announces the dry land, and God smells Noah's sacrifice, vowing never again to curse the ground, sealing the covenant with a bow in the cloud.
summary.zh: 神見人心所思盡惡，決以洪水滅絕血氣；命義人挪亞造歌斐木三層方舟。大淵泉源裂開，天窗敞開，暴雨四十日，生靈盡滅，唯舟中八口與走獸得存。鴿子銜橄欖葉報干地，神聞馨香之祭，誓言永不咒詛大地，以雲中虹為永約之記。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity and Judaism. Presented as the canonical flood narrative of the cross-tradition deluge cluster — scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart. And the LORD said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch. And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits. And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven. But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee. Of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee.

In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened. And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights. And the waters prevailed, and were increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters. And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered. And all flesh died that moved upon the earth: and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.

And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made: and he sent forth a raven, which went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth. Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground; but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark. And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

title.en: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan
title.zh: 挪亞葡萄園與迦南之咒

region.en: Noah's tent after the flood, near Ararat foothills
region.zh: 洪水後挪亞的帳棚，亞拉臘山麓

period: Genesis 9, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 9

summary.en: After the flood Noah plants a vineyard and lies uncovered in his drunkenness; Ham, father of Canaan, sees and tells his brothers, who walk backward to cover their father. Waking, Noah curses not Ham but Canaan — 'a servant of servants shall he be' — and blesses Shem and Japheth: an etiological curse giving Israelite victory over the Canaanites, later grievously misused; biblical scholars and churches now repudiate its later racial readings.
summary.zh: 洪水後挪亞栽葡萄園，醉臥失衣；含見父赤裸而告二弟，閃與雅弗倒退而進遮蓋之。挪亞醒後咒詛的不是含，而是迦南——「必作奴僕的奴僕」——並祝福閃、雅弗。此為解釋以色列戰勝迦南族的溯源故事；歷史上曾被曲解為種族主義之據，今為教會與學界所唾棄。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. This text's long history of racist 'curse of Ham' misreading is documented and rejected in modern scholarship; included as a boundary-marking curse narrative with that context made explicit.

passages.text: And Noah began to be an husbandman, and he planted a vineyard: and he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without. And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness.

And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him. And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant. God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.

title.en: Nimrod and the Tower of Babel
title.zh: 寧錄與巴別塔

region.en: Land of Shinar, plain of Babylon
region.zh: 示拿地，巴比倫平原

period: Genesis 10-11, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 10-11

summary.en: Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the LORD, founds Babel, Erech, Accad, and Nineveh — the beginnings of empire in Shinar. There the whole earth, still of one language, builds a city and a tower whose top may reach heaven, to make a name; the LORD comes down, confounds their speech, and scatters them abroad, leaving the place named Babel. Christian tradition reads the tower as humanity's imperial pride, and Pentecost's gift of tongues as its reversal.
summary.zh: 寧錄為耶和華面前的英勇獵戶，建巴別、以力、亞甲、尼尼微——示拿王國之始。當時天下人口音言語如一，遂築城與通天塔，欲揚己名；耶和華降臨，變亂口音，散眾於全地，遂名巴別。基督教傳統視此塔為人類帝國式狂傲，而五旬節方言恩賜即其逆轉。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a hubris-and-confusion etiology; the Pentecost reversal is noted as the Christian reading.

passages.text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD. And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar. Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh.

And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech. And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth. And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded. And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.

Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech. So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city. Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.

title.en: Cain and Abel: The First Murder
title.zh: 該隱與亞伯：第一樁兇案

region.en: Land of Nod, east of Eden (symbolic pin for the wanderer's land)
region.zh: 挪得之地（伊甸以東流浪者之地的象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 4:1-16, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The two sons of Adam and Eve bring offerings; God accepts the shepherd's and rejects the farmer's, and Cain kills his brother in the field. Marked by God so none may kill him, the first murderer becomes a wandering founder.
summary.zh: 亞當夏娃二子獻祭，神悅牧者之祭而拒農者之祭；該隱在田間殺弟。神為其立記號，免人殺之；首殺者遂為流浪而建城者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; Tetragrammaton rendered 'the LORD'; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Cain knew Abel his brother, and Cain said unto him, 'There is no justice, and there is no Judge, and there is no world to come, and there is no reward for the righteous and punishment for the wicked.' And they strove in the field, and Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
passages.note: This passage blends a rabbinic aggadic expansion (Genesis Rabbah 22) with the biblical notice of Genesis 4:8; paraphrase of both, not verbatim.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Cain: 'Where is Abel thy brother?' And he said: 'I know not; am I my brother's keeper?' And He said: 'What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto Me from the ground. And now, cursed art thou from the ground, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 4:9-11 (public domain).

passages.text: Cain feared that whoever found him would kill him, but God set a mark upon him, that no one should slay him, and he went out from the presence of the LORD and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden. There he built a city and named it after his son. The field had drunk the first blood of human history, and the wandering of the murderer became the founding of the first city. Paraphrase of Genesis 4:12-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 4:12-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lamech's Boast and the First Crafts
title.zh: 拉麥之歌與最初技藝

region.en: Land of Nod (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 挪得之地（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 4:17-24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Cain's line founds cities, tents, herds, metallurgy, and music — and escalates vengeance. Lamech sings the first recorded boast-song: 'I have slain a man for wounding me... if Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy and sevenfold.'
summary.zh: 該隱後裔建城、張幕牧畜、鍛造銅鐵、彈琴吹簫；而復仇升級。拉麥唱出首見之誇耀之歌：「傷我者我殺之……該隱遭報七倍，拉麥必遭報七十七倍。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle. And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and pipe. And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 4:20-22 (public domain).

passages.text: Lamech called to his two wives and boasted of his vengeance: he had killed a young man for a wound and would repay injuries seventy-sevenfold — violence multiplying itself down Cain's line. In the same breath, the chapter invents civilization: cities, nomadism, music, and metallurgy all descend from the murderer's family. Paraphrase of Genesis 4:23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 4:23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Enoch Walked with God, and Was Not
title.zh: 以諾與神同行而不見

region.en: Judean hills (symbolic pin for the silent taking)
region.zh: 猶大山地（無言被取之地的象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 5:21-24, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: In the death-lists of Genesis 5 one man breaks the pattern: Enoch, father of Methuselah, 'walked with God' and was taken without dying — the Bible's first ascension, seeded for the vast apocalyptic books later written under his name.
summary.zh: 創世記五章的死亡譜系中，唯有一人破例：以諾，瑪土撒拉之父，「與神同行」，未死而被取——聖經首次升天，為後世以其名所寫之啟示文學埋下根苗。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah. And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters. And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years. And Enoch walked with God, and he was not; for God took him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 5:21-24 (public domain).

title.en: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan
title.zh: 挪亞葡萄園與迦南受咒

region.en: Ararat foothills (symbolic pin; landing region of the ark)
region.zh: 亞拉臘山麓（方舟停靠區之象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 9:18-29, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The world's first vineyard yields the world's first drunkard: Noah lies uncovered in his tent, Ham sees his father's nakedness, and for the act (or its mockery) Noah curses Ham's son Canaan to servitude — the etiological frame the Torah gives for Israel's later relations with the Canaanites.
summary.zh: 世上首座葡萄園造出首位醉者：挪亞赤身臥於帳中，含見父之裸；因所行（或所譏）挪亞咒其子迦南為僕——此為色列後與迦南人關係之釋義框架。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition. The 'curse of Ham' has been misused historically to justify slavery; the record notes the text curses Canaan, not Ham's whole descent, and describes the verse without endorsing later interpretations.

passages.text: And Noah began to be a husbandman, and he planted a vineyard. And he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 9:20-22 (public domain).

passages.text: Shem and Japheth walked backward with a garment on their shoulders and covered their father without seeing him. Waking, Noah learned what Ham had done and pronounced the curse not on Ham himself but on Ham's youngest son: 'Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.' The passage ends by naming Noah's death at nine hundred and fifty years. Paraphrase of Genesis 9:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 9:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Tower of Babel and the Confusion of Tongues
title.zh: 巴別塔與言語變亂

region.en: Babylon, Shinar (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 示拿地巴比倫（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 11:1-9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: All earth speaks one language and builds a city and a tower 'with its top in heaven, lest we be scattered'. God comes down to look, confuses their language, and scatters them over the earth — the etiological myth of linguistic diversity, aimed at Mesopotamia's ziggurat culture.
summary.zh: 全地同一言語，同建城與塔，「塔頂通天，免得分散」。神降下觀看，變亂其口音，使其分散遍地——語言分歧之釋義神話，鋒芒直指美索不達米亞塔廟文化。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said: 'Go to, let us build us a city, and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name; lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.' And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 11:4-5 (public domain).

passages.text: The LORD saw that one people with one language could accomplish anything they planned, so He confounded their speech so that no one understood another, halted the building, and scattered them across the earth. The city's name — Babel — is heard as Hebrew 'balal', 'He confounded', punning on the great city Babylon. Paraphrase of Genesis 11:6-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 11:6-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lech Lecha: Abraham's Call to Go
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕蒙召前往

region.en: Haran to Shechem (route pin at Haran)
region.zh: 自哈蘭至示劍（以哈蘭為路線定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 12:1-9, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God tells Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land He will show, promising a great nation, blessing, and a name. Abram obeys at seventy-five, journeys through Canaan, and builds altars at Shechem and Bethel — the founding migration of Israel's history.
summary.zh: 神命亞伯蘭離本土親族父家，往所示之地，許以大國、祝福、大名。亞伯蘭七十五歲即行，經迦南，於示劍、伯特利築壇——以色列歷史之創始遷徙。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Now the LORD said unto Abram: 'Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto the land that I will show thee. And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and be thou a blessing.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 12:1-2 (public domain).

passages.text: Abram went as the LORD had spoken, with Sarai and Lot and all their substance, into the land of Canaan, and passed through to Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh. The LORD appeared and promised the land to his seed, and he built an altar; then he moved on to the hill country between Bethel and Ai, pitching his tent and calling on the name of the LORD. Paraphrase of Genesis 12:4-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 12:4-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Sarai in Pharaoh's Court
title.zh: 撒萊在法老宮中

region.en: Egypt, Nile Delta (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及尼羅河三角洲（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 12:10-20, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Famine drives Abram to Egypt; fearing for his life he presents his beautiful wife as his sister, and Pharaoh takes her. Plagues strike Pharaoh's house until the truth is out; Abram is expelled rich — the first of the patriarchal 'sister-wife' episodes that read as foreshadowings of Israel's sojourns.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅亞伯蘭入埃及；恐失性命，以美妻為妹，法老遂取之。法老家遭災，真相大白；亞伯蘭攜財而出——族長「妻妹」敘事之首，預表以色列寄居諸章。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister; that it may be well with me for thy sake, and that my soul may live because of thee. And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair. The princes of Pharaoh also saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
passages.note: Condensed verbatim from JPS 1917, Genesis 12:13-15 (public domain).

passages.text: For Sarai's sake the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues. Pharaoh summoned Abram: 'Why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?' and sent him away with his wife and all he had. The epos of Israel's later affliction in Egypt begins, ironically, with its first forefather protected there by plague. Paraphrase of Genesis 12:16-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 12:16-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Abram and Lot Divide the Land
title.zh: 亞伯蘭與羅得分地

region.en: Bethel, hill country of Canaan
region.zh: 伯特利，迦南山地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 13, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Herds too large for one land force Abram and his nephew Lot apart. Generous Abram lets Lot choose; Lot picks the well-watered plain of the Jordan, settling near Sodom, while Abram dwells in Canaan and receives the promise of all the land he can see.
summary.zh: 牧畜眾多，地不能容，亞伯蘭與姪羅得分開。亞伯蘭寬宏任其先擇；羅得取約旦滋潤平原，近所多瑪而居；亞伯蘭居迦南，蒙應許舉目所見之地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abram said unto Lot: 'Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we are brethren. Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou take the right hand, then I will go to the left.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 13:8-9 (public domain).

passages.text: Lot lifted his eyes to the well-watered plain of the Jordan and journeyed east, pitching toward Sodom, whose men were wicked. After his departure the LORD told Abram to look north, south, east, and west: all the land he saw would be given him and his seed for ever, numerous as the dust of the earth. Paraphrase of Genesis 13:10-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 13:10-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek's Bread and Wine
title.zh: 列王之戰與麥基洗德之餅酒

region.en: Valley of Siddim, Dead Sea (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西訂谷，死海（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 14, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Four eastern kings raid the cities of the plain and carry off Lot; Abram musters 318 retainers, rescues him by night, and refuses all spoil. The mysterious priest-king of Salem, Melchizedek, blesses him with bread and wine — the Bible's first tithe scene and the seed of a whole royal-priestly tradition.
summary.zh: 四東方王掠平原諸城，擄走羅得；亞伯蘭率家丁三百一十八人夜襲救回，不受分毫戰利。撒冷王祭司麥基洗德以餅酒祝之——聖經首次什一奉獻，王祭合一傳統之源。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was priest of God the Most High. And he blessed him, and said: 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth; and blessed be God Most High, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand.' And he gave him a tenth of all.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 14:18-20 (public domain).

passages.text: When Abram defeated the eastern coalition by a night march, the king of Sodom offered him the recovered goods; Abram swore by the LORD, God Most High, that he would not take so much as a sandal-thong, lest the king say 'I have made Abram rich' — save only the shares owed his allies and his men. Paraphrase of Genesis 14:21-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 14:21-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Covenant Between the Pieces
title.zh: 剖牲之約

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Childless Abram protests that his heir is a servant; God promises seed as the stars and, in a dread-smoking rite of cut animals passing between their halves, seals a covenant foretelling four hundred years of bondage and the deliverance to come — Abraham's first great vision.
summary.zh: 無子的亞伯蘭申訴繼者為僕；神應許後裔如眾星，並於烟與火爐中穿過剖開祭牲之間，立約預告四百年為奴與隨之拯救——亞伯拉罕首次大異象。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And He brought him forth abroad, and said: 'Look now toward heaven, and number the stars, if thou be able to number them'; and He said unto him: 'So shall thy seed be.' And he believed in the LORD; and He counted it to him for righteousness.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 15:5-6 (public domain).

passages.text: In a deep sleep a dread and great darkness fell on Abram, and God foretold: his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs, afflicted four hundred years, 'but in the fourth generation they shall come back hither'. Then a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces of the sacrificed animals — God binding Himself alone while Abram slept. Paraphrase of Genesis 15:12-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 15:12-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Hagar at the Spring: The God Who Sees
title.zh: 夏甲在泉旁：看顧人的神

region.en: Wilderness of Shur, road to Egypt
region.zh: 書珥曠野，往埃及之路

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 16, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sarai, barren, gives her Egyptian handmaid Hagar to Abram; when Hagar conceives, the two women's rivalry drives the pregnant girl into the wilderness. There an angel finds her by a spring, promises her a countless son, and she becomes the first person in scripture to give God a name: 'El Roi' — the God who sees.
summary.zh: 撒萊不育，以埃及使女夏甲予亞伯蘭；夏甲懷孕，二女相爭，孕者逃入曠野。天使於泉旁遇之，許其子不可勝數；她遂成聖經中首位為神命名者：「看顧人的神」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Hagar's story is also foundational in Islamic tradition (record cross-referenced there).

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur. And he said: 'Hagar, Sarai's handmaid, whence camest thou? and whither goest thou?' And she said: 'I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 16:7-8 (public domain).

passages.text: The angel promised that her seed would be multiplied beyond counting and named the boy Ishmael, 'God hears'. Hagar answered the first naming-theology in the Bible: 'Thou art a God that seest' — for she said, 'Have I even here seen Him that seeth me?' She returned and bore Abram a son in his eighty-sixth year. Paraphrase of Genesis 16:10-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 16:10-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Covenant of Circumcision: The Names Changed
title.zh: 割禮之約：改名之刻

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 17, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God appears to ninety-nine-year-old Abram as El Shaddai, changes his name to Abraham ('father of a multitude') and Sarai's to Sarah, commands circumcision of every male as the covenant's sign 'throughout your generations', and promises the laughter-child Isaac within the year.
summary.zh: 神向九十九歲之亞伯蘭以全能神顯現，改名亞伯拉罕（萬族之父），撒萊改撒拉；命凡男丁割禮為約之記，「世世代代」，並許笑者以撒年內而生。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And I will establish My covenant between Me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee. ... This is My covenant, which ye shall keep, between Me and you and thy seed after thee: every male among you shall be circumcised.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 17:7, 10 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verses.

passages.text: Abraham fell on his face laughing at the news that a hundred-year-old man and ninety-year-old woman would bear a son, and asked that Ishmael 'might live before Thee'. God answered: the covenant would run through Isaac, born of Sarah, while Ishmael too would father twelve princes and a great nation. That very day Abraham circumcised himself, Ishmael, and every male of his house. Paraphrase of Genesis 17:17-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 17:17-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Three Visitors Under the Terebinths of Mamre
title.zh: 幔利橡樹下之三訪客

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 18:1-15, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Abraham runs from his tent to greet three men and serves them a feast; they repeat that Sarah will bear a son. Overhearing from the tent, ninety-year-old Sarah laughs — and God has the last word: 'Is anything too hard for the LORD?'
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕奔出帳迎三客，設宴款待；三客重申撒拉將生子。撒拉在帳中暗笑——而神有末語：「耶和華豈有難成的事麼？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The narrative of hospitality (hachnasat orchim) became a foundational rabbinic paradigm of kindness.

passages.text: And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre; and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood over against him; and he saw, and ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed down to the earth.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 18:1-2 (public domain).

passages.text: Abraham hurried Sarah to knead cakes, chose a calf, and set curds and milk before the men under the tree. 'Where is Sarah thy wife?' they asked, and repeated the promise. Sarah laughed within the tent, thinking of her worn body and her husband's age, and denied laughing — but the Visitor said: 'Nay; but thou didst laugh.' Paraphrase of Genesis 18:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 18:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Abraham Bargains for Sodom
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕為所多瑪講價

region.en: Overlook toward Sodom from Mamre (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 自幔利遙望所多瑪（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 18:16-33, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God decides to tell Abraham what He plans for Sodom; Abraham stands before the LORD and haggles the city's minimum righteous population down from fifty to ten, asking: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?' The boldest prayer-negotiation in scripture.
summary.zh: 神決意將所多瑪之謀告亞伯拉罕；亞伯拉罕立於耶和華前，將城中義人最低數自五十講至十，問曰：「審判全地的主，豈不行公義麼？」——聖經最大膽之祈禱講價。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abraham drew near, and said: 'Wilt Thou indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Peradventure there be fifty righteous within the city; wilt Thou indeed sweep away and not forgive the place for the fifty righteous that are therein? That be far from Thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked ... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 18:23-25 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verse.

passages.text: Step by step Abraham talked the LORD down: forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty — 'Oh, let not the LORD be angry, and I will speak yet but this once' — to ten. And the LORD went His way, and Abraham returned to his place. The dialogue models chutzpah in prayer: justice argued with the Judge Himself. Paraphrase of Genesis 18:26-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 18:26-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lot at the Gate of Sodom
title.zh: 羅得在所多瑪城門

region.en: Sodom (traditional southern Dead Sea shore; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 所多瑪（傳統死海南岸；象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 19:1-11, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Two angels enter Sodom; Lot, like Abraham, runs to greet and feed them. The men of the city surround the house demanding the strangers; Lot offers his daughters instead; the angels strike the mob blind — the night that seals the city's doom.
summary.zh: 二天使入所多瑪；羅得如亞伯拉罕奔迎款待。城中之人圍屋索要客人；羅得竟以二女代之；天使使暴眾目盲——此夜城之厄運已定。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Later tradition read this as the paradigm of cruelty to strangers; the record states the narrative without endorsing later moralizations.

passages.text: And they called unto Lot, and said unto him: 'Where are the men that came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.' And Lot went out unto them to the door, and shut the door behind him.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:5-6 (public domain).

passages.text: Lot pleaded with the crowd as 'brethren' and offered his two daughters, but the men of Sodom pressed upon him. The angels pulled Lot inside, shut the door, and smote everyone at the entrance with blindness, 'both small and great', so that they wearied themselves finding the door. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:8-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 19:8-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah
title.zh: 所多瑪蛾摩拉之傾覆

region.en: Southern Dead Sea plain (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 死海平原之南（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 19:12-29, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: At dawn the angels hurry Lot, his wife, and two daughters out of the doomed city — 'flee for thy life, look not behind thee'. Fire and brimstone rain from the LORD; Lot's wife disobeys, looks back, and becomes a pillar of salt, while Abraham sees the smoke of the plain rise like a furnace.
summary.zh: 黎明天使催促羅得夫婦與二女出城——「逃命吧，不可回顧」。耶和華降硫磺與火；羅得之妻違命回望，化為鹽柱；亞伯拉罕遠望平原烟氣上騰如燒窯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said: 'Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the Plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be swept away.' The sun rose as Lot entered Zoar, and the LORD rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, overthrowing the cities and all the plain. Lot's wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt. Abraham rose early that morning and looked down to see the smoke of the land going up as the smoke of a furnace — 'and God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow'. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:17 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 19:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lot's Daughters in the Cave
title.zh: 羅得二女在山洞

region.en: Mountains above Zoar (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 瑣珥上方山地（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 19:30-38, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Fearing to dwell in Zoar, Lot retreats to a mountain cave. His daughters, believing the world's men are destroyed, make their father drunk on two successive nights to preserve their father's line; the sons born are Moab and Ben-ammi — the etiological, unflattering origin of Israel's neighbours the Moabites and Ammonites.
summary.zh: 羅得懼居瑣珥，退至山地洞中。二女以為世間男子盡滅，連續兩夜使父醉臥，以存父嗣；所生為摩押與便亞米——以色列鄰邦摩押亞捫之不榮起源釋義。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the firstborn said unto the younger: 'Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of the whole earth. Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:31-32 (public domain).

passages.text: Each daughter lay with her unknowing father on consecutive nights; both conceived. The elder bore a son named Moab — 'from the father' — ancestor of the Moabites; the younger bore Ben-ammi, father of the Ammonites. The Torah does not spare Israel's ancestors' kin: the nations' origins are told through shame. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:33-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 19:33-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Isaac Is Born: God Made Laughter
title.zh: 以撒出生：神使我喜笑

region.en: Beersheba region, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴一帶，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 21:1-8, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The LORD 'remembered Sarah as He had said' and the hundred-year-old promise is fulfilled: Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age. They name him Isaac — 'laughter' — and Sarah's earlier cynical laugh becomes a public celebration: 'God hath made laughter for me; every one that heareth will laugh with me.'
summary.zh: 耶和華「照先前所說眷顧撒拉」，百年應許得成：撒拉於亞伯拉罕年老時生子，名以撒（笑）；昔日譏誚之笑化作慶賀：「神使我喜笑，凡聽見的必與我一同喜笑。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Sarah said: 'God hath made laughter for me; every one that heareth will laugh on account of me.' And she said: 'Who would have said unto Abraham, that Sarah should give children suck? for I have borne him a son in his old age.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 21:6-7 (public domain).

passages.text: The LORD visited Sarah as He had promised; she conceived and bore Abraham a son at the set time God had spoken. Abraham named him Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, being a hundred years old. Sarah weaned him, and Abraham made a great feast the day Isaac was weaned. Paraphrase of Genesis 21:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 21:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Hagar and Ishmael Sent Out into the Wilderness of Beersheba
title.zh: 夏甲與以實瑪利被逐於別是巴曠野

region.en: Wilderness of Beersheba, Negev
region.zh: 別是巴曠野，南地

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 21:9-21, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sarah demands that Hagar's son be sent away 'for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir'; God tells Abraham to listen to her. Hagar wanders until the water is spent, lays the dying boy under a bush, and weeps — until God opens her eyes to a well and promises the lad a great nation.
summary.zh: 撒拉求逐夏甲之子，「這使女的兒子不可與我的兒子以撒一同承受產業」；神命亞伯拉罕聽從。夏甲曠野漂流，水盡，將垂死之童置灌木下而泣——神開其目見井，並許此童成大國。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ishmael's promise is foundational in Islamic tradition as well; cross-reference to islamic records planned.

passages.text: And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her: 'What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is. Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him fast by thy hand; for I will make him a great nation.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 21:17-18 (public domain).

passages.text: The matter grieved Abraham greatly, 'because of his son', but God confirmed Sarah's demand: 'in Isaac shall thy seed be called'. Hagar departed with bread and a skin of water into the wilderness of Beersheba; when the water was gone she cast the child under a shrub and sat opposite, weeping. Then God opened her eyes to a well; the lad grew in the wilderness, an archer, and took an Egyptian wife. Paraphrase of Genesis 21:11-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 21:11-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Binding of Isaac (Akedah)
title.zh: 捆綁以撒（阿刻達）

region.en: Mount Moriah, Jerusalem (traditional identification with the Temple Mount)
region.zh: 摩利亞山，耶路撒冷（傳統指聖殿山）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 22:1-19, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: God tests Abraham: 'Take now thy son, thine only son... and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there'. Father and son walk up the mountain in silence, the wood on Isaac's back; at the last moment an angel stays the knife, and a ram is offered instead. The Akedah is Judaism's supreme drama of faith and obedience.
summary.zh: 神試驗亞伯拉罕：「帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子……往摩利亞地去，在那裡把他獻為燔祭。」父子默然上山，柴在以撒背上；刀將落時，天使止之，遂獻公羊。阿刻達為猶太教信心順服之至高戲劇。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Central to Rosh Hashanah liturgy (shofar recalls the ram); treated as narrative, not as endorsement of child sacrifice, which the text itself replaces.

passages.text: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood. And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 22:9-10 (public domain).

passages.text: Isaac had asked the only question on the road — 'the fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb?' — and Abraham had answered, 'God will provide Himself the lamb'. As the knife rose, the angel of the LORD called twice: 'Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God'. Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket, and sacrificed it instead. He named the place 'The LORD Will Provide', and the angel swore the great promise anew: 'thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies'. Paraphrase of Genesis 22:7-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 22:7-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Sarah Dies: The Purchase of Machpelah
title.zh: 撒拉卒：購麥比拉洞

region.en: Hebron, Cave of Machpelah
region.zh: 希伯崙，麥比拉洞

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 23, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Sarah dies at Kiriat-arba (Hebron) at a hundred and twenty-seven. Abraham negotiates formally with the Hittites and buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver 'current money with the merchant' — the first land Abraham owns in the promised land, a grave.
summary.zh: 撒拉卒於基列亞巴（希伯崙），年一百二十七。亞伯拉罕與赫人正式議價，以四百舍客勒白銀「通用的銀子」購麥比拉洞——應許之地首業，乃一墳墓。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Machpelah (Tomb of the Patriarchs) remains a contested holy site today; record describes text only.

passages.text: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the children of Heth, even four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. ... And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre — that is, Hebron — in the land of Canaan.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 23:16, 19 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verses.

passages.text: Abraham stood before the Hittites as 'a stranger and a settler' and asked for a burial site. Ephron, son of Zohar, publicly offered the cave 'in the presence of the people of the land', inflating the price; Abraham paid the full sum without haggling. The legal formality — witnesses, currency, field and cave with its trees — makes the patriarchs' tomb the first deeded property in Canaan. Paraphrase of Genesis 23:3-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 23:3-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: A Wife for Isaac: The Servant at the Well
title.zh: 為以撒娶妻：僕人在井旁

region.en: Aram-naharaim, well of Haran
region.zh: 亞蘭拿哈蘭，哈蘭井旁

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 24:1-27, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: Abraham sends his eldest servant to his kindred with ten camels, under oath never to take a Canaanite wife for Isaac. At the well the servant prays for a sign: the girl who waters him and his camels is the one. Rebecca's kindness to the camels proves her before a word is spoken.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕遣老僕攜十駝往本族，起誓勿為以撒娶迦南女。僕於井旁求兆：願為我與駝飲水者即是。利百加善待駝群，未出一言而自證。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he said: 'O LORD, the God of my master Abraham, send me, I pray Thee, good speed this day, and show kindness unto my master Abraham. Behold, I stand by the fountain of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water; and let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say: Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and if she say: Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also — let the same be she that Thou hast appointed for Thy servant, even for Isaac.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 24:12-14 (public domain); condensed without ellipsis.

passages.text: Before he finished speaking, Rebecca, born of Bethuel, came out with her pitcher, drew water for the stranger, and then ran again to the trough until all ten camels were satisfied. The servant gave her a nose-ring and bracelets and asked whose daughter she was; when she answered, he bowed his head and blessed the LORD who had led him 'in the right way'. Paraphrase of Genesis 24:15-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 24:15-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Rebecca Chooses: The Betrothal at Haran
title.zh: 利百加自擇：哈蘭許婚

region.en: Haran, house of Bethuel
region.zh: 哈蘭，彼土利之家

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 24:28-67, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: The servant retells his mission in Laban's hall and asks for an answer; the family tries to delay, but Rebecca herself decides: 'I will go'. Meeting Isaac meditating in the field at evening, she alights from her camel, veils herself, and enters Sarah's tent — and Isaac is comforted after his mother's death.
summary.zh: 僕在拉班堂中覆述使命，求定奪；家人欲留，利百加自決：「我去」。以撒傍晚在田間默想，利百加下駝蒙面入撒拉之帳——以撒喪母之痛遂得安慰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said: 'We will call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.' And they called Rebecca, and said unto her: 'Wilt thou go with this man?' And she said: 'I will go.' The servant told of the signs at the well and laid out gifts; Laban and Bethuel answered that the matter was 'of the LORD' and could not be gainsaid. Morning gifts changed hands, the family blessed Rebecca to be 'mother of thousands of ten thousands', and she went. Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, took her as wife, and loved her — and the text notes simply that Isaac was comforted for his mother. Paraphrase of Genesis 24:50-67 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 24:57-58 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 24:50-67 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Abraham's Later Sons and His Death at a Good Old Age
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕後嗣與其壽終

region.en: Mamre, Hebron (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

source.work: Genesis 25:1-11, JPS Tanakh 1917

summary.en: After Sarah's death Abraham takes Keturah, who bears six more sons — ancestors of the eastern tribes. He gives them gifts and sends them east, but gives all he has to Isaac; the sons of the concubines and Isaac himself bury him in Machpelah, where he is gathered to his people 'old and full of years'.
summary.zh: 撒拉卒後，亞伯拉罕娶基土拉，又生六子——東方諸族之祖。亞伯拉罕以財物遣之東去，卻將一切所有予以撒；眾子與以撒同葬之於麥比拉，「年老壽高」歸於本族。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac. But unto the sons of the concubines, that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 25:5-6 (public domain).

passages.text: Keturah's sons — Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah — would people the caravan routes of Arabia and the East, among them Midian, whose land would later shelter Moses. Abraham died at a hundred seventy-five and was buried by his two principal sons, Isaac and Ishmael, in the cave he had bought. Paraphrase of Genesis 25:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Genesis 25:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Call of Abram
title.zh: 亞伯蘭蒙召

region.en: Haran to Shechem, land of Canaan
region.zh: 自哈蘭至示劍（迦南地）

period: Genesis 12, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 12

summary.en: The LORD tells the seventy-five-year-old Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land he will be shown, promising to make of him a great nation through whom all families of the earth will be blessed. Abram goes, builds altars at Shechem and Bethel, and Christian tradition sees in this migration the founding charter of the pilgrim people of God.
summary.zh: 耶和華對七十五歲的亞伯蘭說：要離開本地、本族、父家，往所指示之地去；應許使他成大國，萬族因他得福。亞伯蘭遵命而行，在示劍、伯特利築壇。基督教傳統視此遷徙為朝聖之民、因信而行之始。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared by Judaism and Christianity. Presented as a founding-migration narrative.

passages.text: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee: and I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: and I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him.

And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came. And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the LORD appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.

title.en: Abram's Sister-Wife Deception in Egypt
title.zh: 亞伯蘭埃及謊稱妹妻

region.en: Egypt, Pharaoh's court
region.zh: 埃及，法老宮中

period: Genesis 12, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 12

summary.en: Famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister to save his own life; Pharaoh takes her into his house and rewards Abram richly, until plagues fall on the court and the truth is out. The king sends them away unharmed — the first of the twice-told 'sister-wife' tales in which the patriarchs' survival cunning is ironically preserved by the outsiders they deceive.
summary.zh: 饑荒使亞伯蘭下埃及；他懼死，謊稱撒萊為妹。法老娶她入宮，厚賜亞伯蘭；耶和華卻降大災於法老全家。真相既明，法老遣之而去，毫髮無傷——此乃族長「妹妻」雙重敘事之首，倖存之機巧反由受騙的外邦人保全。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a deception-survival tale type; scholarly framing.

passages.text: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there. And it came to pass, when he was come near to enter into Egypt, that he said unto Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon: therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive. Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.

The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house. And he entreated Abram well for her sake. And the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram's wife. And Pharaoh called Abram and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife? now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.

title.en: Melchizedek Blesses Abram
title.zh: 麥基洗德祝福亞伯蘭

region.en: King's Dale, near Salem (Jerusalem)
region.zh: 王谷，撒冷（耶路撒冷）附近

period: Genesis 14, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 14

summary.en: When four eastern kings plunder Sodom and carry off Lot, Abram arms his 318 trained servants, strikes them by night, and brings back all the goods and people. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses the victor, who gives him a tenth of all — a mysterious priest-king whom Christian tradition (in Hebrews 7) reads as a figure of Christ, the eternal priest, and whose bread and wine echo the Eucharist.
summary.zh: 四王擄掠所多瑪，擄走羅得；亞伯蘭率三百一十八名家丁夜襲，救回人財。撒冷王、至高神的祭司麥基洗德攜餅與酒而出，為他祝福；亞伯蘭將所得十分之一獻上。基督教《希伯來書》以此無譜之王為基督永恆祭司的預表，餅酒亦隱合聖餐。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Melchizedek's Christological reading (Hebrews 7) is noted; presented as a comparative sacred-kingship narrative.

passages.text: And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew; for he dwelt in the plain of Mamre. And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan. And he divided himself against them, he and his servants, by night, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah. And he brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.

And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God. And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth: and blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all. And the king of Sodom said unto Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goods to thyself. And Abram said, I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet, and that I will not take any thing that is thine.

title.en: The Covenant Between the Pieces
title.zh: 切分祭牲之約

region.en: Mamre, near Hebron
region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙附近

period: Genesis 15, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 15

summary.en: In a vision the childless Abram is told his heir will come from his own body and his seed will be as the stars; 'he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness' — the verse Paul makes the cornerstone of justification by faith. Sealing the covenant, Abram cuts the sacrificial animals, falls into a dread darkness, and a smoking furnace and burning lamp pass between the pieces, while prophecy of 400 years of servitude in a strange land is spoken.
summary.zh: 異象中，無子的亞伯蘭得諭：後裔將自其身而出，多如眾星；「亞伯蘭信耶和華，耶和華就以此為他的義」——保羅因信稱義之基石經文。獻祭牲剖分兩半，亞伯蘭沉睡於大黑暗；冒煙的爐並燒著的火把從肉塊中經過，立約為憑，並預言四百年寄居異邦。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Paul's faith-righteousness reading (Romans 4) is the classic Christian use of this text.

passages.text: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward. And Abram said, LORD God, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless? And, behold, the word of the LORD came unto him, saying, This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

And he said unto him, Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon. And he took unto him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each piece one against another. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces. In the same day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land.

title.en: Hagar in the Wilderness
title.zh: 夏甲曠野得見活神

region.en: Wilderness of Shur, well Beerlahairoi
region.zh: 書珥曠野，庇耳拉海萊井

period: Genesis 16 and 21, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 16 and 21

summary.en: Barren Sarai gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram as wife; conceiving, Hagar flees her mistress's harshness into the wilderness, where the angel of the LORD finds her by a spring, promises a countless seed, and names her son Ishmael — 'thou God seest me,' she says, naming the well Beerlahairoi. Cast out later with her son, she sits a bowshot off weeping that she may not see the child die, until God opens her eyes to a well and makes of Ishmael a great nation.
summary.zh: 撒萊使埃及使女夏甲與亞伯蘭同房；夏甲有孕後被苦待而逃至曠野。耶和華的使者在泉旁尋見她，應許後裔無數，並為其子命名以實瑪利；她稱那井為庇耳拉海萊——「看顧人的神」。後母子被逐，坐泣於一箭之遙，神開她的眼得見水井，以實瑪利終成大國。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared with Islam (Ishmael as Arab ancestor). Presented comparatively with sensitivity to both traditions.

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur. And he said, Hagar, Sarai's maid, whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go? And she said, I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai. And the angel of the LORD said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands. And the angel of the LORD said unto her, I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.

Behold, thou art with child and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the LORD hath heard thy affliction. And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me? Wherefore the well was called Beerlahairoi.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and the child, and sent her away: and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. And she went, and sat her down over against him a good way off, as it were a bow shot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And God heard the voice of the lad; and God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.

title.en: Abraham, the Everlasting Covenant, and Isaac Promised
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕、永約與以撒之諾

region.en: Canaan, at the oaks of Mamre
region.zh: 迦南地，幔利橡樹

period: Genesis 17, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 17

summary.en: When Abram is ninety-nine, God Almighty appears, renames him Abraham — 'father of many nations' — establishes the everlasting covenant sealed in the flesh by circumcision on the eighth day, renames Sarai Sarah, and promises that the ninety-year-old Sarah will bear a son named Isaac with whom the covenant will stand. Abraham falls on his face and laughs; Christian tradition reads the covenant as fulfilled spiritually in Christ, 'the seed of Abraham', in whom all nations are blessed.
summary.zh: 亞伯蘭九十九歲時，全能的神向他顯現，改名亞伯拉罕——「多國之父」——立永約，以割禮為約之記號；撒萊改名撒拉，並應許九十歲的她將生以撒，約要在以撒身上堅立。亞伯拉罕俯伏在地喜笑。基督教傳統視此約在基督——亞伯拉罕的後裔——身上成全，萬國因之得福。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared by Judaism and Christianity (and echoed in Islam). Circumcision covenant presented as ritual-origin narrative.

passages.text: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the LORD appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect. And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly. Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee. And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant.

This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you. And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be. And I will bless her, and give thee a son also of her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of people shall be of her.

Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear? And God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.

title.en: The Three Visitors and Sarah's Laughter
title.zh: 三客來訪與撒拉的笑

region.en: Tent door at the plains of Mamre
region.zh: 幔利平原，帳棚門口

period: Genesis 18, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 18

summary.en: In the heat of the day Abraham entertains three men under a tree with cakes, a dressed calf, butter, and milk — one of whom is the LORD. They announce that Sarah, past the age of women, will bear a son; Sarah laughs within the tent and denies it, and is told 'Is any thing too hard for the LORD?' Christian iconography reads the three strangers as a foreshadowing of the Trinity, and the episode as the great Old Testament exemplar of hospitality.
summary.zh: 天正熱時，亞伯拉罕以餅、犢、奶油牛奶款待帳棚前的三位客人——其中一位乃是耶和華。他們宣告年老停經的撒拉將生子；撒拉在帳棚內暗笑，被告知「耶和華豈有難成的事麼？」。基督教聖像畫以三客預示三位一體，此事亦為舊約款待之範式。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Trinitarian reading is a Christian interpretive tradition, noted here; the text itself is Jewish scripture.

passages.text: And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lift up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground, and said, My LORD, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant. And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal.

And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent. And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him. Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age; and it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women. Therefore Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?

And the LORD said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old? Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son. Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.

title.en: Sodom Overthrown, Lot's Wife a Pillar of Salt
title.zh: 所多瑪傾覆，羅得妻成鹽柱

region.en: Cities of the plain, south Dead Sea (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 平原諸城，死海南端（象徵性定位）

period: Genesis 19, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 19

summary.en: Two angels lodge with Lot in Sodom; the city's men besiege the door demanding the strangers, and Lot offers his daughters in vain before the angels strike the mob blind. At dawn Lot's family is dragged from the city — 'escape for thy life; look not behind thee' — and fire and brimstone rain from the LORD upon Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. In a cave the daughters make their father drunk and bear Moab and Benammi, founders of Israel's neighboring nations.
summary.zh: 二天使夜宿羅得家；所多瑪人圍門索人，羅得欲以二女代之，天使使眾人眼盲。黎明羅得一家被拉出城——「逃命吧，不可回頭看」——耶和華降硫磺與火；羅得妻回顧，變成鹽柱。後二女於山洞灌醉其父，生摩押與便亞米，即以色列二鄰族之祖。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as a destruction-and-refugee narrative with an incest-founding etiology; later interpretive uses of the Sodom story vary widely and are not endorsed here.

passages.text: But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter: and they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them. And Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him, and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut to the door.

And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city. And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city. And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain.

Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven; and he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground. But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt. And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place where he stood before the LORD: and he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and, lo, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace.

title.en: The Binding of Isaac
title.zh: 以撒被綁獻祭

region.en: Mount Moriah, land of Moriah
region.zh: 摩利亞山地

period: Genesis 22, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 22

summary.en: God tests Abraham: 'Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest... and offer him there for a burnt offering.' On the third day father and son climb Mount Moriah, Isaac bearing the wood and asking where the lamb is; Abraham binds him on the altar and raises the knife before the angel's cry stays his hand, and a ram caught by its horns is offered in the son's place. Christian tradition reads the akedah as a type of the Father's sacrifice of the Son — God who provides himself a lamb.
summary.zh: 神試驗亞伯拉罕：「帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子，你愛的以撒……把他獻為燔祭。」三日後父子登摩利亞山，以撒背柴，問燔祭的羊羔在哪裏；亞伯拉罕築壇綁子，舉刀欲殺，天使呼叫止手，公羊以角掛於稠密小樹代獻。基督教傳統以此預表聖父犧牲聖子——神必自己預備羔羊。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Judaism and Christianity, both of which hold the akedah as a foundational text of tested faith; the Christian typological reading is noted.

passages.text: And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering.

And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering? And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together. And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood. And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

And the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I. And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me. And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.

title.en: Abraham Buys the Cave of Machpelah
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕購麥比拉洞

region.en: Hebron (Kirjatharba), Canaan
region.zh: 希伯崙（基列亞巴），迦南地

period: Genesis 23, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 23

summary.en: Sarah dies at Hebron at 127, and the wandering Abraham, 'a stranger and a sojourner' among the Hittites, negotiates publicly at the city gate for Ephron's field and the cave of Machpelah, paying 400 shekels of silver — the patriarchs' only owned piece of the promised land, where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and (by Jacob's wish) Jacob are buried. The site remains a shrine to this day, shared and contested.
summary.zh: 撒拉於希伯崙享壽一百二十七歲而終。寄居異地的亞伯拉罕在城門口眾人面前，以四百舍客勒銀子購以弗崙田間的麥比拉洞——族長在應許之地唯一的產業。亞伯拉罕、撒拉、以撒、利百加、利亞並雅各皆葬於此。聖地至今仍是共享而紛爭不斷之所。

sensitivity.note: The Hebron tomb remains a live religious site for Jews and Muslims; the record covers only the ancient narrative.

passages.text: And Sarah was an hundred and seven and twenty years old: these were the years of the life of Sarah. And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her. And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying, I am a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a buryingplace with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.

And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, saying, Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead. And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace.

title.en: Rebekah at the Well
title.zh: 井旁的利百加

region.en: City of Nahor, Mesopotamia (Haran region)
region.zh: 拿鶴城，美索不達米亞（哈蘭一帶）

period: Genesis 24, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 24

summary.en: Abraham sends his eldest servant sworn by the LORD to find Isaac a wife from his own kindred; at the evening well the servant prays for a sign — the girl who offers water to him and his ten camels — and before he finishes speaking Rebekah arrives and does exactly that. Betrothal gifts, Laban's welcome, her decisive 'I will go', and Isaac's taking her into Sarah's tent close the longest and gentlest chapter in Genesis.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕遣老僕起誓，回本族為以撒娶妻。僕人至井旁禱告求記號——凡遞水予他並十駝飲者即所選之女。話未完，利百加出現，恰如此行。聘禮既下，利百加說「我去」，與以撒相遇於暮色田野，入撒拉帳棚成婚，以撒得安慰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The well sign is a divination-adjacent test, tagged as oracle-divination with that interpretive caveat.

passages.text: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh: and I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell: but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.

And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water. And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day. And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac.

And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder. And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up. And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink. And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

title.en: Jacob and Esau: Birthright for Pottage
title.zh: 雅各與以掃：長子名分換紅湯

region.en: Canaan, Isaac's tents
region.zh: 迦南地，以撒帳棚

period: Genesis 25, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 25

summary.en: Rebekah's twins struggle in her womb; the oracle answers 'two nations are in thy womb, and the elder shall serve the younger'. Esau is born red and hairy, Jacob grasping his heel; the hunter and the quiet tent-dweller divide their parents' love, and one famished evening Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of red lentil pottage, 'thus Esau despised his birthright.'
summary.zh: 利百加腹中雙子相爭，神諭答曰：「兩國在你腹內……將來大的要服事小的。」以掃渾身有毛而紅，雅各手抓其踵。善獵者與安靜帳棚者各得父母偏愛；一日以掃打獵困乏，以紅豆湯將長子名分賣給雅各——「以掃輕看了他長子的名分」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The twin-oracle tag of sibling-creators is interpretive — the pair found rival nations (Israel and Edom), noted here.

passages.text: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and Rebekah his wife conceived. And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD. And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb. And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau. And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob. And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. Now Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
