And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint: and Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint. And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright. And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; thus Esau despised his birthright.

title.en: Jacob Steals the Firstborn Blessing
title.zh: 雅各竊取長子祝福

region.en: Isaac's tent at Beersheba
region.zh: 別是巴，以撒的帳棚

period: Genesis 27, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 27

summary.en: Blind old Isaac, wanting venison before blessing Esau, is outmaneuvered by Rebekah: Jacob brings kid-meat dressed as game, goatskins cover his smooth hands and neck, and the dying-speech blessing is irrevocably given — 'the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.' Esau returns to a bitter cry that cannot be undone; Isaac gives him a lesser doom of the sword and the wilderness, and Esau resolves to kill Jacob.
summary.zh: 老眼昏花的以撒欲食野味後祝福以掃，利百加設計：雅各仿野味烹羊羔，羊皮裹手貼頸。祝福出口不可挽回——「聲音是雅各的聲音，手卻是以掃的手」。以掃歸來放聲大哭，只得次等命定：靠刀劍度日；遂懷恨欲殺雅各，雅各亡命哈蘭。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the classic doomed-blessing (irrevocable word) tale; the moral ambiguity of the deception is part of the text's long interpretive history.

passages.text: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying, Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD before my death. Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee. Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth: and thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may bless thee before his death.

And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son: and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck. And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy first born. And Isaac said, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son. And Jacob went near; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. And he discerned him not; so he blessed him.

And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed: therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine: let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

title.en: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
title.zh: 雅各的天梯與伯特利

region.en: Bethel (Luz), on the road to Haran
region.zh: 伯特利（路斯），往哈蘭路上

period: Genesis 28, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 28

summary.en: Fleeing Esau, Jacob sleeps on a stone at a nameless place and dreams of a ladder set on earth whose top reaches heaven, angels ascending and descending, and the LORD standing above it promising land, countless seed, and safe return. Waking, he cries 'Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not', sets the stone up as a pillar, anoints it, and names the place Bethel, the house of God — vowing the tenth and, in Christian reading, seeing in the ladder Christ the bridge between heaven and earth (John 1:51).
summary.zh: 雅各逃離以掃，枕石而臥，夢見天梯立地通天，神的使者上去下來，耶和華立於梯上應許土地、後裔與平安歸回。醒來呼曰：「耶和華真在這裏，我竟不知道！」遂立石為柱、澆油其上，名其地為伯特利——神的家。基督教釋經以梯喻基督，天地之間的橋（約翰福音一51）。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ladder-as-Christ reading is the Christian interpretive tradition, noted here.

passages.text: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.

And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of. And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven. And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel.

title.en: Seven Years for Rachel, Deceived by Leah
title.zh: 為拉結服事七年，被利亞所欺

region.en: Haran, land of the people of the east
region.zh: 哈蘭，東方之地

period: Genesis 29-30, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 29-30

summary.en: At Haran's well Jacob rolls away the stone, kisses Rachel, and weeps; he serves Laban seven years for her, 'and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her' — only to wake after the wedding feast and find Leah, veiled, in the dark. He gains Rachel a week later by serving seven years more. The two rival wives and their maids bear the twelve sons of Israel, Leah's womb opened because she was hated and Rachel's at last with Joseph.
summary.zh: 雅各在哈蘭井旁推石飲羊，吻拉結而哭；為她服事拉班七年，「因深愛拉結，就看這七年如同幾天」——婚宴翌晨才發現黑暗中竟是利亞。再服七年始得拉結。二妻與二使女為他生下以色列十二支派；利亞因失寵而蒙眷顧，拉結終生約瑟。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Deceiver deceived; the divine-marriage tag is loose (a marriage-quest narrative), noted here.

passages.text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep; for she kept them. And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother. And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept. And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.

And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter. And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me. And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her. And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me?

And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn. Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years. And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years. And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren. And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb. And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach: and she called his name Joseph.

title.en: The Flight from Laban and the Mizpah Covenant
title.zh: 逃離拉班與米斯巴之約

region.en: Mount Gilead, east of the Jordan
region.zh: 基列山，約旦河東

period: Genesis 31, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 31

summary.en: Told by God to return, Jacob slips away while Laban is shearing sheep; Rachel steals her father's household gods and hides them in camel's furniture, sitting on them and pleading the custom of women. Warned in a dream, Laban pursues, searches, finds nothing, and the two raise a heap of stones — Galeed and Mizpah — swearing the LORD watch between them when they are absent one from another.
summary.zh: 神諭雅各歸回，趁拉班剪羊毛之際潛逃；拉結偷了父親家中的神像，藏於駱駝馱簍，坐在其上託詞「身上不便」。拉班夢中被神警告，追及基列，搜遍帳棚而不得。二人累石為證，立約於米斯巴——「願耶和華在你我中間鑒察」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Boundary-covenant etiology of the Mizpah heap.

passages.text: And Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels; and he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gotten, for to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan. And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.

And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob was fled. And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey; and they overtook him in the mount Gilead. And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said unto him, Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad. And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father's house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not. And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched but found not the images. Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee. And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.

title.en: Jacob Wrestles at Peniel
title.zh: 雅各在毗努伊勒摔跤

region.en: Ford of the Jabbok river
region.zh: 雅博渡口

period: Genesis 32-33, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 32-33

summary.en: Sick with fear of Esau's four hundred men, Jacob sends everything across the Jabbok and is left alone; a man wrestles with him till daybreak, touches the hollow of his thigh, and blesses him when Jacob will not let go — 'thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.' Jacob calls the place Peniel, 'for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved', and limps for life; the children of Israel do not eat the sinew that shrank. The next day the brothers embrace and weep.
summary.zh: 雅各懼以掃四百人，將家眷財物渡過雅博河，獨自留下；有個人與他摔跤直到黎明，摸其大腿窩，雅各緊抓不放求祝福——「你的名不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列，因為你與神與人較力，都得了勝。」雅各名其地為毗努伊勒：「我面對面見了神，我的性命仍得保全」，從此瘸腿；以色列人不吃大腿窩的筋。翌日兄弟相擁而泣。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The name-change and the food prohibition are the ritual-origin elements; interpretive traditions differ on who the wrestler is.

passages.text: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two womenservants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jabbok. And he took them, and sent them over the brook, and sent over that he had. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.

And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed. And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved. And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.

And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother. And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept. And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself. And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand.

title.en: Dinah and the Massacre of Shechem
title.zh: 底拿與示劍屠城

region.en: Shechem, city of Hamor
region.zh: 示劍，哈抹之城

period: Genesis 34, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 34

summary.en: Shechem, the Hivite prince's son, takes and defiles Dinah, then loves her and asks for her in marriage. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully: all the men of the city consent to circumcision as the price of intermarriage; on the third day, while they are sore, Simeon and Levi put the city to the sword, spoil it, and carry off wives, children, and wealth. Jacob fears the land will rise against him; his sons answer coldly, 'Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?'
summary.zh: 示劍玷污底拿，後因愛她求婚。雅各眾子以詭詐回答：全城男丁為通婚受割禮；第三日眾人疼痛之際，西緬與利未提劍屠城，擄掠財物婦孺。雅各懼迦南人聚集攻滅全家，眾子冷冷回答：「他豈可待我們的妹子如同妓女麼？」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a violation-and-vengeance narrative; the massacre is presented without endorsement, and Jacob's rebuke is part of the text.

passages.text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land. And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her. And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel. And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.

And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister: We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us: but in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised. And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised.

And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males. And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out. The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister. And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land.

title.en: Tamar and the Pledges of Judah
title.zh: 他瑪與猶大的信物

region.en: Road to Timnath, by Adullam
region.zh: 往亭拿路上，亞杜蘭附近

period: Genesis 38, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 38

summary.en: Er dies, Onan refuses to raise up seed to his brother and dies, and Judah withholds young Shelah from Tamar — so Tamar veils herself as a shrine prostitute at the road gate, takes Judah's signet, bracelets, and staff as pledge, and conceives. Accused of harlotry and dragged out to be burned, she produces the pledges: 'she hath been more righteous than I,' Judah admits. Of the twins Pharez and Zarah, Pharez carries the line to David — and, in Matthew's genealogy, to Jesus.
summary.zh: 珥死，俄南不肯為兄立後而死，猶大又扣下示拉；他瑪遂蒙面扮妓，坐在往亭拿的路口，取猶大的印、帶子與杖為當頭而懷孕。被告淫亂拉出要燒時，她出示信物；猶大說：「她比我更有義。」其孿生子法勒斯攜猶大支派血統至大衛，馬太福音家譜更達於耶穌。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Levirate law and pledge-trickery narrative; the messianic lineage reading (Matthew 1) is noted.

passages.text: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar. And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him. And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother. And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother. And the thing which he did displeased the LORD: wherefore he slew him also.

And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife. When Judah saw her, he thought her to be an harlot; because she had covered her face. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it? And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thine hand. And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.

And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt. When she was brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff. And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.

title.en: Joseph's Dreams and the Coat in the Pit
title.zh: 約瑟的夢與坑中的彩衣

region.en: Dothan, hills of Canaan
region.zh: 多坍，迦南山丘

period: Genesis 37, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 37

summary.en: Israel's coat of many colours marks his love for Joseph, and the seventeen-year-old's two dreams — sheaves bowing to his sheaf, sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him — sharpen the brothers' hatred. Sent to check on them at Dothan, he is stripped, thrown into a dry pit, and sold by Judah's counsel to Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver; the brothers dip the coat in goat's blood, and Jacob refuses comfort, 'I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning.'
summary.zh: 以色列為約瑟作彩衣，十七歲的少年連得二夢——禾捆下拜，日月十一星下拜——招致兄長嫉恨。奉父命赴多坍探望，兄長們剝其彩衣，投之於無水的坑，經猶大提議，以二十舍客勒銀子賣給以實瑪利商人。眾兄以羊羔血染彩衣，雅各不肯受安慰：「我必悲哀著下陰間到我兒子那裏。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The dreams function as true prophecy in the narrative arc.

passages.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours. And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him. And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more. For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.

And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him. And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him. And they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him: and they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it. And Judah said unto his brethren, Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites. And they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

title.en: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
title.zh: 約瑟與波提乏之妻

region.en: Potiphar's house, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，波提乏家中

period: Genesis 39, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 39

summary.en: Sold to Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard, Joseph prospers so that all his master's house is blessed through him; made overseer of everything, he refuses the master's wife day by day — 'how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?' — until, catching her grip on his garment, he flees leaving it in her hand. Her false cry convicts him before her husband, and the innocent slave is cast into the prison where the king's prisoners are bound.
summary.zh: 約瑟被賣給法老的內臣波提乏，事事蒙福，治理全家；卻日日拒絕主母——「我怎能作這大惡，得罪神呢？」終有一日，主母抓其衣裳，他棄衣而逃。主母誣告，主人怒而將無辜的奴隸下在監裏，與王的囚犯同囚。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Chastity-falsely-accused tale type; the trickster tag applies to the wife's deception.

passages.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites. And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand. And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me. But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand; there is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out. That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us. And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home. And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison. But the LORD was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

title.en: The Butler's Dream in Pharaoh's Prison
title.zh: 法老監中酒政之夢

region.en: Prison of the captain of the guard, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，護衛長監中

period: Genesis 40, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 40

summary.en: Pharaoh's chief butler and baker offend him and are bound in Joseph's prison; both dream, and Joseph — 'Do not interpretations belong to God?' — reads the vine with three branches as three days to restoration, and the three white baskets eaten by birds as three days to hanging. All falls out on Pharaoh's birthday; yet the restored butler forgets Joseph for two full years.
summary.zh: 法老的酒政與膳長得罪主人被囚，同夜各得一夢。約瑟說「解夢不是出於神麼」——葡萄三枝即三日復職，頭上三筐白餅被飛鳥吃盡即三日被掛。果然應驗於法老生日；然而復職的酒政竟忘了約瑟，一忘兩年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Dream-interpretation narrative.

passages.text: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison. And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, and, behold, they were sad. And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.

In my dream, behold, a vine was before me; and in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes: and Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand. And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place.

When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head: and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head. And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: The three baskets are three days: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee. And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday. Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

title.en: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph as Vizier
title.zh: 法老之夢與約瑟為相

region.en: Pharaoh's court, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及法老宮廷

period: Genesis 41, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 41

summary.en: Two years on, Pharaoh dreams of seven fat kine devoured by seven lean kine and of seven full ears blasted by seven thin, and none of Egypt's magicians can read it. The butler remembers Joseph, who is brought from the dungeon, shaved and changed, and declares 'It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace' — seven years plenty, then seven years famine. Pharaoh sets the ring on Joseph's hand, clothes him in fine linen, names him Zaphnathpaaneah, and rides him in the second chariot; the storehouses of Egypt are filled against the famine.
summary.zh: 兩年後，法老夢見七肥牛被七瘦牛所吞，七好穗被七枯穗所滅；埃及術士皆不能解。酒政想起約瑟，遂自監中提出，剃頭換衣入宮。約瑟說：「這不在乎我，神必將平安的話回答法老。」——七豐年後七荒年。法老將手上戒指戴在約瑟手上，賜名撒發那忒巴內亞，使其乘副車巡行埃及全地，倉廩囤糧以備荒年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The foreign vizier narrative; the second-chariot investiture is the kingship element.

passages.text: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river. And, behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow. And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. And he slept and dreamed the second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good; and, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.

Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day. And there was there with us a young man, an Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; and it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was. Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace. The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one. Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land. Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.

And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art: thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou. And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck; and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee.

title.en: The Silver Cup in Benjamin's Sack
title.zh: 便雅憫袋中的銀杯

region.en: Joseph's house, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，約瑟府中

period: Genesis 42-44, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 42-44

summary.en: When ten brothers bow before the governor of Egypt begging corn, they do not know him, but he remembers his dreams and tests them: Simeon bound, corn returned with their money, Benjamin demanded. On the second visit Joseph weeps in private at the sight of his brother, feasts them, then hides his silver divining cup in Benjamin's sack; the cup is 'found', Judah offers himself as surety — 'let thy servant abide instead of the lad' — and the trap of mercy is sprung.
summary.zh: 十個哥哥向埃及宰相俯伏糴糧，不識其人，約瑟卻記得幼年的夢，並試驗他們：捆西緬、還銀糧、索便雅憫。再來時，約瑟見幼弟而暗自飲泣，設宴款待，又將銀杯藏於便雅憫袋中；搜出後，猶大以己身代之——「求你容僕人住下，替這童子作我主的奴僕」——憐憫的網羅已然張開。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The cup is used for divination in the narrative detail; tagged accordingly.

passages.text: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another? And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence. And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth. And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them; and he remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them.

And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there. And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth. And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack. And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack. Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city. And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren. For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me?

title.en: I Am Joseph: Reunion in Goshen
title.zh: 我是約瑟：歌珊重逢

region.en: Goshen, land of Egypt
region.zh: 埃及歌珊地

period: Genesis 45-46, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 45-46

summary.en: Unable to restrain himself before all his retinue, Joseph cries 'Cause every man to go out from me' and reveals himself weeping aloud — 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' He forgives: 'ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive.' Pharaoh sends wagons, the stunned Jacob's spirit revives, and at Beersheba God appears to Israel in visions of the night promising to go down with him and bring him up again. Father and son fall on each other's necks in Goshen.
summary.zh: 約瑟在隨從面前不能再自禁，喊道「人都要離開我出去」，放聲大哭表明身份：「我是約瑟！我父親還在麼？」他饒恕他們：「從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的，要保全許多人的性命。」法老遣車接眷；雅各聞言心裏甦醒，在別是巴夜間異象中得神應許同行下埃及。父子在歌珊相擁而泣。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The descent into Egypt founds the Israel-in-Egypt cycle that Exodus continues.

passages.text: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren. And he wept aloud: and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard. And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.

And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life. So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.

And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac. And God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here am I. And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again.

title.en: Jacob's Last Words: The Sceptre of Judah
title.zh: 雅各遺言：猶大的杖

region.en: Jacob's bed, land of Goshen, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及歌珊地，雅各床前

period: Genesis 47-49, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 47-49

summary.en: Gathering his twelve sons at his deathbed 'to tell you that which shall befall you in the last days', Jacob blesses and characterizes each tribe in turn: Reuben unstable as water, Simeon and Levi scattered for the massacre, Judah a lion's whelp of whom 'the sceptre shall not depart... until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be' — the verse Christian tradition reads messianically of Christ — and Joseph the fruitful bough of double blessing. He charges burial in Machpelah and dies, and is mourned by all Egypt seventy days.
summary.zh: 臨終召集十二子「把你們日後必遇的事告訴你們」：流便如水滾沸不得居首，西緬利未因屠城分散，猶大如小獅——「圭必不離猶大，杖必不離他兩腳之間，直等細羅來到，萬民都必歸順」——基督教傳統以此為彌賽亞基督之預言；約瑟則是多結果子的樹枝，蒙雙倍祝福。遺命葬麥比拉洞，埃及為其哀哭七十日。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Shiloh verse is one of the most contested messianic readings in scripture; the Christian tradition's reading is noted alongside the tribal-blessing frame.

passages.text: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days. Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power: unstable as water, thou shalt not excel. Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations. O my soul, come not thou into their secret; for in their anger they slew a man, and in their selfwill they digged down a wall.

Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee. Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up? The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall: the archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him: but his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob. Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil. All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is it that their father spake unto them, and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.

title.en: The Mourning of Egypt and Joseph's Bones
title.zh: 埃及哀榮與約瑟遺骨

region.en: Goshen to Machpelah, funeral road beyond Jordan
region.zh: 歌珊至麥比拉洞，約旦河外送葬之路

period: Genesis 50, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 50

summary.en: Joseph embalms his father and leads chariots and horsemen, all the elders of Egypt, in a seven-day lamentation at the threshingfloor of Atad — so grievous the Canaanites name it Abelmizraim — before burying Jacob in Machpelah. Then the brothers, fearing revenge, send word of Jacob's command; Joseph weeps and answers 'am I in the place of God?' Dying at 110, Joseph takes an oath of the children of Israel that God will surely visit them and they shall carry up his bones from hence — the oath that Exodus and Joshua will honor.
summary.zh: 約瑟以香料薰父遺體，率法老諸臣與車馬，在約旦河外的亞達禾場哀哭七日，迦南人驚呼「這是埃及人一場極大的哀哭」，遂名亞伯麥西。雅各葬於麥比拉。諸兄懼報復遣使求赦，約瑟哭泣而答「我豈能代替神呢」。約瑟享壽一百一十歲而終，臨終令以色列人起誓：神必眷顧你們，你們要把我的骸骨從這裏搬上去。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The bones-oath frames the Exodus cycle that follows.

passages.text: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel. And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days. And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt, and there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.

And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days. And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abelmizraim, which is beyond Jordan. For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah.

And when Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him. And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.

title.en: The Midwives and the Baby in the Ark of Bulrushes
title.zh: 收生婆與蘆葦箱中的嬰孩

region.en: Nile riverbank, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及，尼羅河畔

period: Exodus 1-2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 1-2

summary.en: A Pharaoh 'which knew not Joseph' enslaves Israel and orders every Hebrew boy drowned in the river; the midwives Shiphrah and Puah fear God and disobey, telling him Hebrew women deliver before they arrive. A Levite mother hides her goodly son three months, then sets him in a slime-sealed ark of bulrushes among the flags, where Pharaoh's daughter finds him, has pity, and — through the quick tongue of his watchful sister — pays his own mother to nurse him, naming him Moses, 'because I drew him out of the water.'
summary.zh: 「不認識約瑟的新王」壓迫以色列，下令溺殺希伯來男嬰；收生婆施弗拉與普阿敬畏神而不從。利未女子藏子三月，後將其放入塗石漆石油的蘆葦箱，置於河邊蘆荻中。法老女兒發現嬰孩，動了憐憫之心；其姊機敏召來生母代哺。公主為其命名摩西——「因我把他從水裏拉出來」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Judaism and Christianity. The exposed-hero-on-water is presented alongside other river-escape birth narratives.

passages.text: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah: and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live. But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.

And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi. And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink. And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it. And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children. Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee? And she called the child's mother. And the child grew, and she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

title.en: Moses Slays the Egyptian and Flees to Midian
title.zh: 摩西殺埃及人而逃米甸

region.en: Egypt to Midian, by the well
region.zh: 自埃及至米甸井旁

period: Exodus 2, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 2

summary.en: Grown up in Pharaoh's house but going out to look on his brethren's burdens, Moses kills an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew and hides him in the sand; the next day a Hebrew challenges him — 'who made thee a prince and a judge over us?' — and the deed is known, so he flees to Midian. At a well he drives off shepherds harassing Jethro's seven daughters, waters their flock, and marries Zipporah, naming his son Gershom, 'I have been a stranger in a strange land'; meanwhile Israel's cry rises to God, who remembers his covenant.
summary.zh: 摩西在法老宮中長大，卻出去看弟兄的重擔；見埃及人打希伯來人，便殺之藏於沙中。次日被同族揭破——「誰立你作我們的首領和審判官呢？」——遂逃往米甸。在井旁驅散欺凌葉忒羅七女之牧羊人，為其羊群飲水，娶西坡拉為妻，生子革舜——「我在外邦作了寄居的」。以色列人在捆鎖中歎息哀求，神記念祂的約。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the fugitive-prince-to-shepherd phase of the hero cycle.

passages.text: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand. And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known. Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock. And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land. And it came to pass in process of time, that the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage. And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

title.en: The Burning Bush and the Name I AM
title.zh: 焚而不毀的荊棘與「自有永有者」

region.en: Horeb, the mountain of God
region.zh: 何烈山，神的山

period: Exodus 3-4, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 3-4

summary.en: Keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses turns aside to see why a bush burns and is not consumed, and the LORD calls from within it, appointing him to bring Israel out of Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey. Moses' three refusals — Who am I? What is your name? I am slow of speech — are answered by 'I AM THAT I AM', three signs (rod to serpent, leprous hand, water to blood), and Aaron as his mouth; Jesus later grounds his own divine claims on this name.
summary.zh: 摩西牧羊至何烈山，見荊棘被火燒著卻未燒燬，便轉過去看；耶和華從荊棘裏呼叫，差他領以色列出埃及，入流奶與蜜之地。摩西三度推辭——我算甚麼？你叫甚麼名字？我拙口笨舌——神以「我是自有永有的」答之，並賜三個神蹟記號，以亞倫為其口。耶穌後來正是以此名自證其神聖身份。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The divine name is treated with reverence in both Judaism and Christianity; quoted here as public-domain scripture in a comparative framing.

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed. And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt. And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I. And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows; and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.

And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say unto them? And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. And the LORD said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.

And Moses said unto the LORD, O my LORD, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth? have not I the LORD? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say. And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.

title.en: Zipporah at the Night Inn
title.zh: 西坡拉於夜間客店

region.en: Wayside inn, road from Midian to Egypt
region.zh: 米甸往埃及路旁客店

period: Exodus 4:24-26, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 4

summary.en: One of scripture's strangest three verses: on the road back to Egypt the LORD meets Moses and seeks to kill him, until Zipporah takes a sharp stone, circumcises her son, and casts the foreskin at his feet — 'Surely a bloody husband art thou to me' — and so he lets him go. Commentators read it as the unfinished circumcision of Moses' son endangering the covenant-bearer; the blood rite averts the night attack.
summary.zh: 聖經中最奇異的三節經文：歸埃及途中，耶和華遇見摩西，想要殺他；西坡拉急取火石刀，為兒子行割禮，丟在摩西腳前說——「你真是我的血郎了」——神便放他。釋經者以為：未行割禮之子危及立約者之身，血禮解夜間之危。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. An obscure and much-debated episode; presented as a covenant-blood narrative.

passages.text: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him. Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me. So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.

title.en: Let My People Go: Bricks Without Straw
title.zh: 容我的百姓去：無草製磚

region.en: Pharaoh's court and brickfields, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及法老宮廷與磚窯

period: Exodus 5, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 5

summary.en: Moses and Aaron demand a three-day journey to sacrifice, and Pharaoh answers 'Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go' — then doubles the cruelty by cutting the straw supply while keeping the brick quota, so the officers are beaten and the people blame Moses. The tale of bricks made without straw became the proverb of impossible demands, and the crushed people turn on their deliverer: 'ye have made our savour to be abhorred.'
summary.zh: 摩西亞倫求三日行程往曠野獻祭；法老答「耶和華是誰，使我聽他的話？我不認識耶和華」——反下令不再供草，磚數如常，官長被責打，百姓怨懟摩西。「無草製磚」自此成為不可能之要求之成語；受壓的百姓反咬其拯救者：「你們使我們在法老眼前可憎。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Pharaoh's divine-king denial frames the contest of kingships.

passages.text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. And Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.

And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying, Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves. And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle. And the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.

Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people. But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh: and they said unto them, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh.

title.en: Aaron's Rod Swallows the Sorcerers' Rods
title.zh: 亞倫的杖吞了術士的杖

region.en: Pharaoh's court, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及法老宮廷

period: Exodus 7, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 7

summary.en: Before Pharaoh, Aaron casts down his rod and it becomes a serpent; the Egyptian wise men and sorcerers match the sign with their enchantments — 'but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.' The court duel of magic opens the plague cycle, and the hardened heart of Pharaoh begins its long, strange refrain.
summary.zh: 法老面前，亞倫丟杖變蛇；埃及的博士和術士也用邪術照樣而行——「但亞倫的杖吞了他們的杖」。這場法術對決揭開災禍的序幕；法老剛硬的心，自此成為奇特的反覆疊句。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Egyptian court sorcery is presented as the narrative foil, not endorsed; the witch tag follows the text's own category of enchanters.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Shew a miracle for you: then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent. And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the LORD had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments. For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods. And he hardened Pharaoh's heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.

title.en: The Ten Plagues of Egypt
title.zh: 埃及十災

region.en: Land of Egypt, Nile to palace
region.zh: 埃及全地，尼羅河至王宮

period: Exodus 7-10, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 7-10

summary.en: Blood turns the Nile to stench; frogs swarm into ovens and kneadingtroughs; dust becomes lice the magicians cannot copy — 'this is the finger of God'; flies divide Goshen from the palaces; murrain kills the cattle; boils break the magicians' standing; thunder, fire-mingled hail, locusts on the east wind, and a darkness 'which may be felt' for three days fall in turn, each answered by a partial concession and a re-hardened heart — 'that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.'
summary.zh: 尼羅河化為血腥；青蛙入爐灶揉麵盆；塵土變虱，術士不能複製——「這是神的手段」；成群蒼蠅分別歌珊與王宮；瘟疫斃牲畜；瘡使術士站不住；雷雹夾火；東風捲來蝗蟲；三日黑暗「似乎可以摸得著」。每一次半讓步之後心便再剛硬——「好叫你知道普天下沒有像我的」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The plague cycle is presented as narrative; modern scholarship reads it against Egyptian natural hazards without adjudicating the theological claim.

passages.text: And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood. And the fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river. And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt. And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt. And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

And Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt. And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast. Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them.

And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt. So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation. Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: the LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.

And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts. For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land. And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt. And there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days: they saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

title.en: The Passover and the Midnight Strike
title.zh: 逾越節與半夜之擊

region.en: Goshen and Egypt, night of the Exodus
region.zh: 歌珊與埃及，出埃及之夜

period: Exodus 11-12, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 11-12

summary.en: Each household takes a lamb without blemish, kills it at evening, marks lintel and doorposts with hyssop-dipped blood, and eats it in haste — loins girded, staff in hand, unleavened bread and bitter herbs. At midnight the LORD smites all the firstborn of Egypt, from Pharaoh's throne-heir to the captive in the dungeon; there is not a house without one dead, and a weeping Egypt thrusts Israel out with jewels of silver and gold. 'It is the LORD's passover' becomes the founding feast, kept forever; Christians read the unblemished lamb's blood as foreshadowing Christ, 'our passover', and the Last Supper is a Passover meal.
summary.zh: 各家取無殘疾羔羊，傍晚宰殺，以牛膝草蘸血塗門楣門框，束腰拿杖急速而食——無酵餅、苦菜。半夜，耶和華擊殺埃及一切長子，自法老長子至牢中囚徒；無一家不死一人，埃及舉國大哭，催促以色列速速離去，並以金銀相贈。「這是耶和華的逾越節」成為永遠遵守的定例。基督教視無瑕疵羔羊之血預表基督——「我們逾越節的羔羊」，而主的晚餐正是一次逾越節筵席。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism (Passover) and Christianity (Last Supper typology); presented as ritual-origin narrative with both readings noted.

passages.text: In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house. Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats: and ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening. And they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.

And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD's passover. For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the LORD. And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

And Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover. And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning. And it came to pass, that at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.

And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead. And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as ye have said. Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also. And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

title.en: Pillar of Cloud and Fire, with the Bones of Joseph
title.zh: 雲柱火柱與約瑟的骸骨

region.en: Succoth to Etham, edge of the wilderness
region.zh: 疏割至以倘，曠野邊緣

period: Exodus 13, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 13

summary.en: Rather than the short Philistine road and its war, God leads the harnessed people the long way by the wilderness of the Red Sea; Moses carries the bones of Joseph, honoring the oath of Genesis 50. The LORD goes before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire — the visible presence that guides, shades, and lights the march.
summary.zh: 神不領百姓走近捷的非利士道路，恐怕他們遇戰而回，卻繞道紅海曠野而行；摩西攜約瑟骸骨同去，履行創世記末章的誓言。耶和華日間在雲柱中領路，夜間在火柱中光照——那可見的同在，引導、遮蔽、照看整支行列。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The cloud-and-fire presence is a classic theophany form.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt: but God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt. And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night: he took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.

title.en: The Crossing of the Red Sea
title.zh: 過紅海

region.en: Shore of the Red Sea, Egypt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 紅海之濱，埃及（象徵性定位）

period: Exodus 14, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 14

summary.en: Trapped between Pharaoh's six hundred chariots and the sea, Israel cries out — 'were there no graves in Egypt?' — and Moses answers the great line: 'Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.' The angel and pillar of cloud move behind to darken the Egyptians; a strong east wind drives the sea back all night, and Israel crosses on dry ground with the waters a wall on either hand. The morning watch finds the chariot wheels dragging; the sea returns and covers the host — 'there remained not so much as one of them.'
summary.zh: 法老六百輛戰車迫近，以色列被夾於海與軍之間，哀呼「難道在埃及沒有墳地嗎？」摩西答以千古名句：「不要懼怕，只管站住，看耶和華今天向你們所要施行的救恩。」天使與雲柱移至其後；東風整夜吹海，海水分開，以色列行於乾地，水在他們左右作了牆垣。晨更時埃及車輪脫落，海水復合，全軍覆沒——「連一個也沒有剩下」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as the central deliverance narrative of the Exodus cycle.

passages.text: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto the LORD. And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: and it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night. And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left. And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. And the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them. But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea.

title.en: The Song of the Sea and Miriam's Timbrels
title.zh: 海之歌與米利暗的手鼓

region.en: Seashore after the crossing
region.zh: 過海後的海岸

period: Exodus 15, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 15

summary.en: Moses and Israel sing the oldest poem in scripture: 'I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea... Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods?' Miriam the prophetess takes a timbrel and all the women follow with dances, answering the refrain — the founding victory hymn of the tradition, sung and set to music from ancient liturgy to Handel.
summary.zh: 摩西與以色列眾人歌頌聖經中最古的詩篇：「我要歌頌耶和華，因他大大戰勝，將馬和騎馬的投在海中……耶和華啊，眾神之中誰能像你？」女先知米利暗手拿鼓，眾婦女隨她擊鼓跳舞應和——這是傳統的得勝之歌，自古禮儀至韓德爾的神劇，傳唱不絕。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The victory hymn is the founding song of the tradition.

passages.text: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea. The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father's God, and I will exalt him. The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name. Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.

Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders? Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them. Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation. The LORD shall reign for ever and ever.

And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances. And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

title.en: Bitter Waters Made Sweet at Marah
title.zh: 瑪拉苦水變甜

region.en: Marah and Elim, wilderness of Shur
region.zh: 瑪拉與以琳，書珥曠野

period: Exodus 15:22-27, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 15

summary.en: Three days without water end at Marah, whose springs are too bitter to drink; the people murmur 'What shall we drink?' and Moses cries to the LORD, who shows him a tree that, cast into the waters, makes them sweet. There the first wilderness statute is given — 'I am the LORD that healeth thee' — and Elim follows with its twelve wells and seventy palms, a green resting place on the edge of the desert.
summary.zh: 三日無水之後至瑪拉，水苦不能飲；百姓埋怨「我們喝甚麼呢？」摩西呼求耶和華，神指示一棵樹，丟入水中水就變甜了。在那裏頒下曠野第一條律例——「我耶和華是醫治你的」。隨後以琳有十二股水泉、七十棵棕樹，是曠野邊上的綠洲歇息處。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Wells-and-palms etiology of the wilderness stations.

passages.text: So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water. And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink? And he cried unto the LORD; and the LORD shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them.

And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee. And they came to Elim, where were twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.

title.en: Bread from Heaven: Manna and Quails
title.zh: 天上來的糧：嗎哪與鵪鶉

region.en: Wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai
region.zh: 汛的曠野，以琳與西奈之間

period: Exodus 16, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 16

summary.en: Hunger makes the freed slaves dream of Egypt's fleshpots; the LORD rains bread from heaven, and quails cover the camp at evening. The small round thing 'as small as the hoar frost on the ground' is gathered an omer a head — he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack — breeding worms if hoarded, doubling on the sixth day, absent on the seventh: the daily bread that teaches the sabbath. An omer is laid up before the Testimony 'for your generations', and Israel eats manna forty years.
summary.zh: 饑餓使自由的奴隸懷念埃及的肉鍋；耶和華賜天糧，晚間鵪鶉飛來遮滿營地。早晨露水蒸發後，野地面上有如霜樣的小圓物——嗎哪。按飯量各取一俄梅珥——多收的沒有餘，少收的也沒有缺；留到早晨就生蟲變臭，第六日收雙份，第七日無。每天的分糧教曉安息日；一俄梅珥存於法櫃前「為後世代」，以色列吃嗎哪四十年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The manna rule is the sabbath's first practical teaching; the omer pot is its memorial rite.

passages.text: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: and the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger. Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host. And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground. And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.

And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack. And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank. And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man. And Moses said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning. Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.

And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey. And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness. As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept. And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited.

title.en: Water from the Rock at Massah and Meribah
title.zh: 何烈磐石出水

region.en: Rephidim, near Horeb
region.zh: 利非訂，何烈山附近

period: Exodus 17, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 17

summary.en: Thirst drives the people to stone-throwing mutiny — 'Is the LORD among us, or not?' — and God answers by standing on the rock in Horeb for Moses to strike: water gushes for the people and cattle. The place is named Massah and Meribah, temptation and strife, the standing etiology of both a spring and the sin of testing God.
summary.zh: 乾渴令百姓幾乎用石頭打死摩西——「耶和華是在我們中間不是？」神答以：祂要站在何烈山的磐石那裏，摩西擊打磐石，水就從磐石流出，使百姓和牲畜都喝。那地方名叫瑪撒（試探）、米利巴（爭鬧）——一處水泉與一宗試探神之罪的永久起源。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Rock-spring etiology; Paul later reads the rock as a type of Christ.

passages.text: And there was no water for the people to drink. Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.

And the LORD said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go. Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel. And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not?

title.en: Amalek and the Hands Held Up
title.zh: 亞瑪力之戰與舉手之禱

region.en: Top of the hill at Rephidim
region.zh: 利非訂山頂

period: Exodus 17:8-16, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 17

summary.en: Amalek attacks Israel in the wilderness, and Moses, enthroned on a stone at the hilltop with the rod of God, raises his hands — while they are held up Israel prevails, when they drop Amalek does; Aaron and Hur steady the weary arms until sunset. Joshua wins the battle with the sword; the victory is written in a book, an altar is named Jehovahnissi — the LORD my banner — and war with Amalek is sworn 'from generation to generation.'
summary.zh: 亞瑪力人在曠野攻擊以色列。摩西手握神的杖登上山頂，坐在石頭上舉手——手舉起以色列就得勝，手下垂亞瑪力就得勝；亞倫與戶珥扶住疲憊的雙臂直到日落。約瑟夫——約書亞以刀劍得勝；戰績寫於書上，築壇名耶和華尼西——耶和華是我旌旗——並起誓必世世代代與亞瑪力人爭戰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The eternal-war clause against Amalek has a heavy later interpretive history; presented as text, with the raised-hands intercession the episode's most-cited element.

passages.text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand. And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses' hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun. And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword. And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovahnissi: for he said, Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

title.en: Jethro's Counsel: Judges by Thousands and Tens
title.zh: 葉忒羅獻策：設立千夫長

region.en: Camp before the mount of God
region.zh: 神山前的營地

period: Exodus 18, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 18

summary.en: Jethro arrives with Zipporah and the boys, hears the Exodus story, blesses the LORD — 'now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods' — and sacrifices with the elders. Watching Moses judge the people alone from morning to evening, the old priest of Midian delivers the classic counsel of delegation: able men who fear God as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens; hard cases only to Moses. Moses hears him, and the judicial structure of Israel is born from a foreign father-in-law's advice.
summary.zh: 葉忒羅攜西坡拉與二子來見，聽出埃及之事，稱頌耶和華——「我如今知道耶和華比萬神都大」——並與長老同席獻祭。見摩西自朝至暮獨自審判百姓，這位米甸老祭司獻上授權分層的千古良策：選敬畏神、誠實無妄之人作千夫長、百夫長、五十夫長、十夫長；難斷之事才呈摩西。以色列司法制度自此而生，竟出於異邦岳父之口。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first judicial hierarchy of Israel, credited to a Midianite priest.

passages.text: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the LORD had done to Israel, whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians. And Jethro said, Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh. Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them. And Jethro, Moses' father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father in law before God.

And when Moses' father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even? And Moses' father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: and let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.

title.en: Thunder and Law at Mount Sinai
title.zh: 西奈雷霆與律法

region.en: Mount Sinai
region.zh: 西奈山

period: Exodus 19-20, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 19-20

summary.en: On the third day, with the people washed and fenced off from the mount under pain of death, thunder and lightning, a thick cloud, a trumpet exceeding loud, and a trembling mountain: 'the LORD descended upon it in fire, and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace.' From the mount God speaks the Ten Commandments — no other gods, no graven image, no vain name, the sabbath, honour of parents, the four 'thou shalt nots' of killing, adultery, theft, false witness, and no coveting — until the terrified people beg Moses: 'Speak thou with us... but let not God speak with us, lest we die.'
summary.zh: 第三日，雷轟閃電、密雲遍山、角聲甚大，全營盡皆發顫；「耶和華在火中降於山上，山的煙氣上騰，如燒窯一般」。神從山上宣講十誡——除我以外不可有別神、不可拜偶像、不可妄稱神名、守安息日、當孝敬父母、不可殺人、姦淫、偷盜、作假見證、不可貪婪——百姓戰兢求摩西：「求你和我們說話……不要神和我們說話，恐怕我們死亡。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism and Christianity. The Decalogue is quoted as public-domain scripture in comparative framing.

passages.text: And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled.
