The unclean spirits beg to be sent into a herd of about two thousand swine, which rush down a steep place into the sea and are choked; the townsfolk find the tormented man 'sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind' — and beg Jesus to leave.
summary.zh: 住在墳塋裏、鎖鏈捆不住、晝夜喊叫用石頭砍自己的被附之人，遠遠跑來拜耶穌：「我名叫群，因為我們多的緣故。」污鬼央求進入約二千頭豬的豬群，豬群闖下山崖投入海裏淹死了；眾人來見那曾鬼附的人「坐著，穿上衣服，心裏明白過來」——卻央求耶穌離開他們的境界。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Exorcism narrative; the swine's destruction is part of the recorded story.

passages.text: And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit, who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains: because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him. And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.

But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him, and cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not. For he said unto him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit. And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.

And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them. And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea. And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.

title.en: The Ruler's Dead Daughter and the Touching of the Hem
title.zh: 管會堂者復活的女兒與摸衣繸的女人

region.en: Capernaum and its roads
region.zh: 迦百農及其路上

period: Gospel of Mark, c. 65-75 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 41: Mark, chapter 5

summary.en: Two healings interleave: a synagogue ruler begs Jesus for his dying daughter, and on the way a woman who has bled twelve years and spent all on physicians touches his garment from behind — 'straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up' — while Jesus feels virtue go out and makes her confess. Word comes that the girl is dead; 'Be not afraid, only believe', he says, puts out the wailing mourners who laugh him to scorn, and speaks the Aramaic 'Talitha cumi; Damsel, I say unto thee, arise' — and she rises and walks.
summary.zh: 兩樁醫治交織：管會堂的睚魯為垂死的女兒求告；路上，患血漏十二年被醫生耗盡一切的女人，從後頭摸他的衣裳——「血漏的源頭立刻乾了」——耶穌自覺有能力出去，要她當眾承認。有人報信說孩子死了；他說「不要怕，只要信」，斥退嗤笑的哀哭者，以亞蘭語說「大利大古米！閨女，我吩咐你起來」——女孩立即起來行走。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The interleaved double healing is the gospel's most famous narrative construction.

passages.text: And, behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet, and besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live. And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.

And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse, when she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?

And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague. While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue's house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further? As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.

And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and entereth in where the damsel was lying. And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise. And straightway the damsel arose, and walked.

title.en: Clay and Siloam: The Man Born Blind
title.zh: 泥與西羅亞池：生來瞎眼的人

region.en: Pool of Siloam, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，西羅亞池

period: Gospel of John, c. 90-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 9

summary.en: To the disciples' question — who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind? — Jesus answers 'Neither... but that the works of God should be made manifest in him', makes clay of spittle, and sends the man to wash in the pool of Siloam; 'he went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.' On the sabbath, the healed man is hauled before the Pharisees, excommunicated for defending his healer, and found again by Jesus: 'Dost thou believe on the Son of God?'
summary.zh: 門徒問：這人生來瞎眼，是誰犯了罪，是他本人還是父母？耶穌答「也不是這人犯了罪，也不是他父母犯了罪，是要在他身上顯出神的作為來」，用唾沫和泥抹在他眼睛上，囑他往西羅亞池去洗——「他去一洗，回頭就看見了」。安息日行此神蹟，那人被帶到法利賽人面前，因維護醫治者而被趕出會堂，耶穌再尋見他問「你信神的兒子麼？」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The clay-anointing echoes the Genesis dust-man motif; tagged as an interpretive cross-link.

passages.text: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth. And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind? Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world. When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay, and said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

The neighbours therefore, and they which before had seen him that he was blind, said, Is not this he that sat and begged? Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he. Therefore said they unto him, How were thine eyes opened? He answered and said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight.

title.en: Lazarus, Come Forth
title.zh: 拉撒路，出來

region.en: Bethany, near Jerusalem
region.zh: 伯大尼，近耶路撒冷

period: Gospel of John, c. 90-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 11

summary.en: Told that his friend is sick, Jesus stays two days — 'Lazarus is dead... I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe' — and comes to Bethany where the corpse has lain four days. Martha meets him with the grief-question, and hears the great 'I am' of the gospel: 'I am the resurrection, and the life.' At the cave's mouth, amid Martha's practical protest ('by this time he stinketh'), Jesus weeps, then cries with a loud voice, 'Lazarus, come forth' — and the dead man shuffles out still bound in graveclothes. The miracle that triggers the plot to kill Jesus in John's telling.
summary.zh: 聞友患病，耶穌仍住了兩日——「拉撒路死了……我沒有在那裏就歡喜，這是為你們的緣故，好叫你們相信」——抵達伯大尼時死者已葬四日。馬大迎著訴苦，耶穌以福音書最大的「我是」作答：「復活在我，生命也在我。」墓穴門前，馬大務實地說「他如今必是臭了」，耶穌心裏悲歎、流淚，然後大聲呼叫「拉撒路，出來！」死人裹著壽衣手腳纏布走出。約翰福音中，此神蹟正是謀害耶穌之陰謀的導火線。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The raised friend is the gospel's hinge miracle, read as sign of the general resurrection.

passages.text: Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha. Therefore his sisters sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick. When Jesus heard that, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby. When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was. Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead. And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.

Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already. Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again. Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.

When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, and said, Where have ye laid him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see. Jesus wept. Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him! Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it. Jesus said, Take ye away the stone.

And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go. Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.

title.en: Five Loaves and Two Fishes
title.zh: 五餅二魚

region.en: Desert place by the Sea of Galilee
region.zh: 加利利海旁的野地

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 14

summary.en: The only miracle in all four gospels: in a desert place the disciples urge sending the crowd to buy food, and Jesus answers, 'They need not depart; give ye them to eat.' Five loaves and two fishes are blessed, broken, and distributed — and five thousand men eat, with twelve baskets of fragments left over. The Eucharist's shadow falls across the scene: taken, blessed, broken, given.
summary.zh: 四福音書唯一共載的神蹟：野地裏門徒勸眾人往村裏買食物，耶穌說「不用他們去，你們給他們吃吧」。五餅二魚望天祝福、擘開分遞——五千人吃飽，零碎還裝滿了十二個籃子。聖餐的影子籠罩全場：拿起、祝謝、擘開、遞給。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The feeding is read eucharistically across the tradition.

passages.text: And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick. And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals. But Jesus said unto them, They need not depart; give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.

He said, Bring them hither to me. And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude. And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full. And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children.

title.en: Peter Walks on the Water and Sinks
title.zh: 彼得行於水面而沉

region.en: Sea of Galilee, in the fourth watch of the night
region.zh: 加利利海，夜間四更

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 14

summary.en: In the fourth watch of the night Jesus comes to the storm-tossed boat walking on the sea; the frightened disciples hear 'Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.' Peter dares the request, 'Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water' — and walks, until the boisterous wind frightens him and, beginning to sink, he cries 'Lord, save me.' The outstretched hand and the rebuke — 'O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?' — end with the ship's company worshiping: 'Of a truth thou art the Son of God.'
summary.zh: 夜間四更，耶穌在海面上走向被風浪顛簸的船；驚惶的門徒聽見「你們放心，是我，不要怕」。彼得求：「主，如果是你，請叫我從水面上走到你那裏去。」他果真行走，直到狂風使他害怕、往下沉，喊道「主啊，救我！」耶穌伸手拉住他責備：「小信的人哪，為甚麼疑惑呢？」船上的人隨即敬拜：「你真是神的兒子了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The water-walking is a classic epiphany; Peter's sinking is the tradition's emblem of doubt amid faith.

passages.text: And straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away. And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone. But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary. And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased. Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.

title.en: The Transfiguration on the High Mountain
title.zh: 高山變像

region.en: An unnamed high mountain (symbolic pin at Mount Tabor)
region.zh: 未名高山（象徵性定位於他泊山）

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 17

summary.en: Six days after Peter's confession, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them — face shining as the sun, raiment white as the light — with Moses and Elijah talking with him, the law and the prophets bearing witness. Peter's offered tabernacles are cut short by a bright cloud and the Father's voice repeating the baptismal words and adding, 'hear ye him.' Eastern Christianity keeps the feast as the great feast of divine light.
summary.zh: 彼得認信六日後，耶穌攜彼得、雅各、約翰上高山，在他們面前變了形像——面貌如日頭，衣裳潔白如光——摩西與以利亞顯現同他說話，律法與先知為其作證。彼得欲搭三座棚的話未完，一片光明的雲彩遮蓋他們，雲裏有聲音重複受洗時的話，並加上「你們要聽他」。東方教會以「主顯聖容節」為大節，慶祝神性之光。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Central feast of Eastern Orthodoxy; Moses-Elijah appearance links to the law-and-prophets theme.

passages.text: And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart, and was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light. And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.

Then answered Peter, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias. While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him. And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid. And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid. And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only.

title.en: Zacchaeus in the Sycomore Tree
title.zh: 桑樹上的撒該

region.en: Jericho
region.zh: 耶利哥

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 19

summary.en: The chief tax collector of Jericho, rich and little of stature, climbs a sycomore tree to see Jesus pass; Jesus looks up and invites himself to dinner — 'Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.' Amid the murmuring crowd, Zacchaeus stands and pledges half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution, and hears the sentence that defines the story: 'This day is salvation come to this house... For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.'
summary.zh: 耶利哥的稅吏長撒該，富有而身量矮小，爬上桑樹要看走過的耶穌；耶穌抬頭便自請入住其家——「撒該，快下來，今天我必住在你家裏」。眾人議論之際，撒該站著承諾：家產一半分給窮人，訛詐的四倍償還；耶穌宣告：「今天救恩到了這家……人子來，為要尋找拯救失喪的人。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The little man in the tree is the children's icon of repentance.

passages.text: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho. And, behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich. And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature. And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way. And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully. And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner. And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold. And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham. For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

title.en: He That Is Without Sin
title.zh: 無罪者先投石

region.en: Temple courts, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷聖殿院中

period: Gospel of John, c. 90-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 8

summary.en: Scribes and Pharisees drag a woman taken in adultery into the temple and set her in the midst, demanding the stoning Mosaic law requires as a trap. Jesus stoops and writes on the ground, then answers: 'He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.' One by one, 'being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest'; Jesus and the woman are left alone — 'Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.'
summary.zh: 文士和法利賽人把行淫時被拿的婦人拖進聖殿，設在她當中，以摩西律法要求石刑為陷阱逼問。耶穌彎腰用指頭在地上畫字，然後說：「你們中間誰是沒有罪的，誰就可以先拿石頭打她。」他們聽見這話，「從老到少，一個一個的都出去了」；殿中只剩耶穌與婦人——「我也不定你的罪；去吧，從此不要再犯罪了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The scene is the tradition's master-text on mercy versus law.

passages.text: And the scribes and Pharisees brought unto him a woman taken in adultery; and when they had set her in the midst, they say unto him, Master, this woman was taken in adultery, in the very act. Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou? This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not. So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground.

And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst. When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee? She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.

title.en: The Great Draught of Fishes
title.zh: 一網大魚

region.en: Lake of Gennesaret (Sea of Galilee)
region.zh: 革尼撒勒湖（加利利海）

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 5

summary.en: Teaching from Simon's boat, Jesus tells the washed-out fisherman to launch into the deep and let down the nets; Simon answers with daybreak's defeat — 'Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net' — and encloses so great a multitude of fishes that the net breaks and both boats begin to sink. Simon Peter falls at Jesus' knees: 'Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.' The answer founds the apostolate: 'Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.'
summary.zh: 耶穌在西門的船上講道後，叫勞碌整夜毫無所獲的漁夫把船開到水深之處下網；西門答：「夫子，我們整夜勞力，並沒有打著甚麼；但依從你的話，我就下網。」網險些拉不上來，兩船將沉。西門彼得俯伏在耶穌膝前：「主啊，離開我，我是個罪人！」答話奠定使徒職分：「不要怕，從今以後，你要得人了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The miraculous catch parallels the fishing motif of the call narratives.

passages.text: And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret, and saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets. And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon's, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship. Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net. And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake. And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink. When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.

title.en: The Sower and the Four Soils
title.zh: 撒種的比喻與四種土

region.en: Seaside, teaching from a ship
region.zh: 海邊，船上施教

period: Gospel of Mark, c. 65-75 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 41: Mark, chapter 4

summary.en: The parable of parables: seed falls by the wayside (devoured by fowls), on stony ground (sprung up, scorched, rootless), among thorns (choked, unfruitful), and on good ground (thirtyfold, sixtyfold, an hundredfold) — with the interpretive key that the sower sows the word, and the soils are hearers. It also carries the strange theory of parables themselves: 'Unto you it is given to know the mystery... but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables.'
summary.zh: 比喻中的比喻：種子落在路旁（被飛鳥吃盡）、土淺石頭地（發苗快、日頭一曬就枯乾）、荊棘裏（被擠住不結實）、好土裏（三十倍、六十倍、一百倍）——解釋之鑰：撒種之人所撒的乃是道，四種土即四種聽者。比喻的理論亦在此：「神國的奧祕只叫你們知道……對外人講，凡事就用比喻。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sower is the interpretive master-parable of the tradition.

passages.text: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow: and it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up. And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth: but when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away. And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit. And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred. And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables. And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables? The sower soweth the word. And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

title.en: The Mustard Seed and the Seed Growing Secretly
title.zh: 芥菜種與暗中生長的種子

region.en: Seaside, Galilee
region.zh: 加利利海邊

period: Gospel of Mark, c. 65-75 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 41: Mark, chapter 4

summary.en: Two tiny-to-vast seed parables: the kingdom as a man scattering seed who sleeps and rises while 'the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself', and the mustard seed, 'less than all the seeds that be in the earth', that grows into the greatest of herbs with branches where the fowls of the air lodge — the tradition's emblems of small beginnings and hidden growth, from mission strategy to personal conscience.
summary.zh: 兩則由小至大的種子比喻：神國如同撒種之人黑夜睡覺白日起來，種子「自己發芽生長」，大地自會結果；又如芥菜種——「比地上百種還小」——卻長成最大的菜，枝葉可供飛鳥棲宿。從宣教方略到個人良心，這是傳統「微小開端、暗中生長」的雙重意象。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The mustard seed is proverbial across the tradition.

passages.text: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; and should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how. For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it? It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth: but when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.

title.en: The Good Samaritan
title.zh: 好撒瑪利亞人

region.en: Road from Jerusalem to Jericho
region.zh: 耶路撒冷下耶利哥之路

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 10

summary.en: To the lawyer's test — 'who is my neighbour?' — Jesus answers with the man beaten by thieves on the Jericho road: a priest and a Levite pass by on the other side; a Samaritan, the heretic outsider, binds his wounds with oil and wine, carries him, pays the innkeeper two pence with an open account — 'when I come again, I will repay thee.' The question is reversed: not 'who is my neighbour' but 'which of these three was neighbour?' — 'Go, and do thou likewise.'
summary.zh: 律法師試問「誰是我的鄰舍？」耶穌以下耶利哥路上被強盜打個半死之人作答：祭司與利未人皆繞道而行；被視為異端的撒瑪利亞人卻以油酒裹傷、扶上牲口、以二錢銀子託付店主並留下未償清的帳——「此外費用的，我回來必還你」。問題被倒轉：不是「誰是我的鄰舍」，而是「這三個人中誰是鄰舍」——「你去照樣行吧。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Samaritan hero inverts ethnic expectation; 'good Samaritan' is now common law language worldwide.

passages.text: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead. And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.

But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, and went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him. And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee. Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

title.en: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
title.zh: 迷失的羊與失落的一塊錢

region.en: Wilderness and house, Judaea
region.zh: 猶太地的野地與家宅

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 15

summary.en: Answering the murmur 'this man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them', Jesus tells the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine for the one lost sheep, lays it on his shoulders rejoicing, and calls a feast — 'joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance' — then the woman with ten pieces of silver who lights a candle and sweeps the house till she finds one: joy in the presence of the angels.
summary.zh: 面對「這個人接待罪人，又同他們吃飯」的竊竊私語，耶穌講牧羊人撇下九十九隻去尋那迷失的羊，找著了便扛在肩上回家請客——「一個罪人悔改，在天上也要這樣為他歡喜，較比為九十九個不用悔改的義人歡喜更大」。又講婦人有十塊錢失了一塊，點燈打掃屋子細細地找——找著便請鄰舍同樂：天使面前也這樣為一個悔改的罪人歡喜。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The lost-sheep image is the tradition's emblem of the value of the one.

passages.text: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him. And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them. And he spake this parable unto them, saying, What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost. I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance. Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost. Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

title.en: The Prodigal Son and the Elder Brother
title.zh: 浪子回頭與長兄

region.en: A far country; the father's house
region.zh: 遠方異國；父親家中

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 15

summary.en: The younger son demands his inheritance, wastes it in a far country, and sinks to feeding swine and coveting their husks; 'when he came to himself' he rehearses his confession on the road home — and the father runs, falls on his neck, and kills the fatted calf: 'this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.' The elder brother, faithful and bitter — 'thou never gavest me a kid' — is answered with the parable's quiet core: 'Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry.'
summary.zh: 小兒子索分家產，遠方揮霍，淪為喂豬之工，恨不得以豬食充飢；「醒悟過來」便在歸途演練認罪之辭——父親卻相離尚遠就動了慈心，跑去抱著他的頸項連連親嘴，宰了肥牛犢：「我這個兒子是死而復活、失而又得的。」勤勞而怨恨的長兄抗議「你從來沒有給我一隻山羊羔」，得到全喻安靜的核心：「兒啊，你常和我同在，我一切所有的都是你的。只是你這個兄弟是死而復活、失而又得的，所以我們理當歡喜快樂。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. 'Dead and alive again' makes the parable a resurrection story in miniature; the elder brother is the tradition's image of the resentful righteous.

passages.text: And he said, A certain man had two sons: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: and bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing. And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends. And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

title.en: The Rich Fool: Soul, Take Thine Ease
title.zh: 無知的財主：靈魂啊，只管安逸

region.en: Judaea, on the way to Jerusalem
region.zh: 猶太地，往耶路撒冷路上

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 12

summary.en: A rich man's ground brings forth plentifully, and he plans bigger barns and a self-addressed retirement — 'Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry' — to which God answers the coldest line in the gospels: 'Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?' — 'So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.'
summary.zh: 財主的田產豐收，便盤算拆了小倉房蓋更大的，自言自語：「靈魂哪，你有許多財物積存，可作多年的費用，只管安安逸逸的吃喝快樂吧！」神卻以福音書中最冷峻的一句作答：「無知的人哪，今夜必要你的靈魂，你所預備的要歸誰呢？」——「凡為自己積財，在神面前卻不富足的，也是這樣。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sudden-death reversal is the tradition's classic memento mori.

passages.text: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully: and he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.

But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God. And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on. Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them.

title.en: The Rich Man and Lazarus at the Gulf
title.zh: 財主與拉撒路：深淵之隔

region.en: Abraham's bosom and the place of torment
region.zh: 亞伯拉罕的懷裏與受苦之處

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 16

summary.en: The purple-clad rich man fares sumptuously while the sore-covered beggar Lazarus longs for crumbs, dogs licking his sores; both die — Lazarus carried by angels to Abraham's bosom, the rich man lifting his eyes in torment across 'a great gulf fixed' that none can cross. His plea for a drop of water, then for a messenger to his brothers, is refused: 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them... If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.'
summary.zh: 穿紫袍綢緞、天天奢華宴樂的財主與門口討飯、渾身生瘡、狗來舔瘡的乞丐拉撒路；二人先後死去——拉撒路被天使帶去放在亞伯拉罕的懷裏，財主在火焰中隔著「有深淵限定」舉目遙望。他求一滴水涼舌、求遣人警告五個兄弟，皆被拒絕：「他們有摩西和先知的話可以聽從……若不聽從摩西和先知的話，就是有一個從死裏復活的，他們也是不聽勸。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The gulf-fixed afterlife geography shaped Western hell imagery; the named beggar is unique among parable characters.

passages.text: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day: and there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, and desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.

And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried; and in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence. Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house: for I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them. And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

title.en: The Parable of the Talents
title.zh: 按才受託的比喻

region.en: Mount of Olives discourse
region.zh: 橄欖山講論

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 25

summary.en: A man travelling into a far country delivers five, two, and one talent 'to every man according to his several ability'; on his return the five- and two-talent servants have doubled their trust — 'Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord' — while the one-talent servant, who buried his coin in the earth, is cast into 'outer darkness' as wicked and slothful. The word 'talent' has meant 'gift' ever since.
summary.zh: 往遠方去的主人按各人的才幹交給僕人五千、二千、一千銀子；回來結算，領五千與二千的連本帶利翻倍——「好，你這又良善又忠心的僕人，你在不多的事上有忠心，我要把許多事派你管理，可以進來享受你主人的快樂」——把一千埋在地裏的僕人卻被斥為又惡又懶，扔進外面黑暗裏。自始，「他連得」一詞便意味「恩賜」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The stewardship parable is read as eschatological readiness.

passages.text: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey. Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two. But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord's money.

After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them. And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown: and I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine. His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not: thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers. Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents. And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

title.en: The Sheep and the Goats: Inasmuch as Ye Have Done It
title.zh: 綿羊山羊之喻：作在最小的一個身上

region.en: Throne of glory, Mount of Olives discourse
region.zh: 榮耀寶座，橄欖山講論

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 25

summary.en: The Son of man in his glory separates all nations as a shepherd divides sheep from goats, and the criterion of both destinies is startlingly concrete: 'I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me' — 'Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.'
summary.zh: 人子在榮耀裏降臨，把萬民分別如牧人分綿羊山羊；兩般結局的準則出奇地具體：「我餓了，你們給我吃；渴了，你們給我喝；我作客旅，你們留我住；我赤身露體，你們給我穿；我病了，你們看顧我；我在監裏，你們來看我」——「這些事你們既作在我這弟兄中一個最小的身上，就是作在我身上了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The last-judgment criterion of mercy works; tagged with prophetic-vision for the apocalyptic frame.

passages.text: When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: and before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats: and he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: for I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

title.en: The Last Supper: Take, Eat; This Is My Body
title.zh: 最後的晚餐：拿起來吃，這是我的身體

region.en: Upper room, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，樓上客房

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 26

summary.en: At a Passover meal Jesus takes bread, blesses, breaks, and gives: 'Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup... Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins' — the founding rite of the Eucharist, celebrated in every Christian tradition under many theologies of presence. He then foretells the scattering of the flock and Peter's coming denial before the cock crows.
summary.zh: 逾越節筵席上，耶穌拿起餅來祝福、擘開、遞給門徒：「你們拿著吃，這是我的身體。又拿起杯來……你們都喝這個，因為這是我立約的血，為多人流出來，使罪得赦。」——聖餐禮由此立定，各基督教傳統以不同的臨在神學代代遵行。隨即預言羊群散與彼得雞鳴前三次不認主。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of the highest centrality (Eucharist). Quoted as public-domain scripture in comparative framing; denominational doctrines of the supper differ and are not adjudicated here.

passages.text: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom. And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.

Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad. Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended. Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.

title.en: Gethsemane: Let This Cup Pass From Me
title.zh: 客西馬尼：這杯若不能離開我

region.en: Gethsemane, Mount of Olives
region.zh: 橄欖山，客西馬尼園

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 26

summary.en: Beyond the brook Kidron, 'sorrowful and very heavy' — 'my soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death' — Jesus prays three times while the chosen three sleep: 'O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.' The prayer that names the whole passion as obedience under dread; he returns to find 'the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.'
summary.zh: 過了汲淪溪，「憂傷幾乎要死」的耶穌三次禱告，所選三人卻沉沉睡去：「我父啊，倘若可行，求你叫這杯離開我；然而不要照我的意思，只要照你的意思。」這禱告把整場受難命名為恐懼之下的順服；末了起身：「時候到了，人子被賣在罪人手裏了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The agony in the garden is central to passion liturgy.

passages.text: Then cometh Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder. And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy. Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me. And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour? Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done. And he came and found them asleep again: for their eyes were heavy. And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words. Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

title.en: I Know Not the Man: Peter's Three Denials
title.zh: 我不認得那個人：彼得三次不認主

region.en: High priest's palace, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，大祭司宅中

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 26

summary.en: Following afar off into the high priest's courtyard while his master is tried inside, Peter is picked out by a maid, then a second, then by his Galilean accent — 'thy speech bewrayeth thee' — and denies with curses: 'I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew. And Peter remembered the word of Jesus... And he went out, and wept bitterly.' The tradition's most enduring portrait of failure by a chief witness.
summary.zh: 大祭司院裏審判之際，遠遠跟進的彼得被一使女、又一使女、繼而憑加利利口音指認——「你的口音把你露出來了」——賭咒發誓說「我不認得那個人」。立時雞叫；彼得想起耶穌的話，「就出去痛哭」。首要見證人的失敗，成為傳統中最長久的畫像。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The denial is the tradition's classic failure-and-restoration arc.

passages.text: Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee. But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest. And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth. And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.

And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee. Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew. And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.

title.en: Thirty Pieces of Silver and the Field of Blood
title.zh: 三十塊錢與血田

region.en: Temple courts and the potter's field, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿與窯戶之田

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 27

summary.en: Seeing his master condemned, the betrayer repents and brings back the thirty pieces of silver — 'I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood' — is brushed off by the priests ('see thou to that'), casts the coins into the temple, and goes and hangs himself. The silver, blood-price, buys the potter's field for burying strangers, 'wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.'
summary.zh: 見主被定罪，賣主者懊悔，把三十塊錢拿回來——「我賣了無辜之人的血是有罪了」——祭司冷淡回應「那與我們有甚麼相干？你自己承當吧」；他把銀錢丟在殿裏，出去吊死了。血價銀子買下窯戶之田埋葬外鄉人，「那塊田直到今日還叫做血田」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The suicide is presented as text without endorsement; the 'field of blood' etiology is the sacred-place element.

passages.text: Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in. Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.

title.en: Before Pilate: Crucify Him, Release Barabbas
title.zh: 彼拉多面前：釘他十字架，釋放巴拉巴

region.en: Praetorium, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，衙門

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 23

summary.en: Pilate, having examined the prisoner and found 'no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him', offers the Passover release; the crowd demands the seditious murderer Barabbas instead, crying 'Crucify him, crucify him.' Thrice Pilate protests — 'Why, what evil hath he done?' — 'and the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed. And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.'
summary.zh: 彼拉多查問後宣告「我查不出這人有甚麼罪來」，提出逾越節釋放之例；群眾卻喊「除掉這個人，釋放巴拉巴給我們」——那因作亂殺人下監的囚犯。彼拉多三次抗辯「這人作了甚麼惡事呢？」——「他們的聲音就得了勝，彼拉多才照他們所求的定案」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The trial scene carries a long history of Christian anti-Jewish misreading; the record presents the narrative while noting that modern scholarship and churches repudiate collective blame.

passages.text: And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people, said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him: no, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him. I will therefore chastise him, and release him.

And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas: (who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.) Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them. But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go. And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed. And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.

title.en: The Good Thief: Today Shalt Thou Be With Me
title.zh: 好強盜：今日你要同我在樂園裏了

region.en: Calvary, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，各各他

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 23

summary.en: Crucified at 'the place, which is called Calvary' between two criminals, Jesus prays for his executioners — 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do' — while rulers, soldiers, and one thief mock him. The other thief rebukes his fellow — 'this man hath done nothing amiss' — and asks only, 'Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom', receiving the day's great promise: 'Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.'
summary.zh: 在「名叫各各他」的地方，耶穌被釘在兩個罪犯之間，卻為行刑者禱告：「父啊，赦免他們，因為他們所作的，他們不曉得。」官長兵丁與一個強盜譏誚他；另一強盜責備同伴——「這個人沒有作過一件不好的事」——只求「耶穌啊，你得國降臨的時候，求你記念我」，便得那日的大應許：「我實在告訴你，今日你要同我在樂園裏了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The penitent thief is venerated as St Dismas; the last-moment conversion is a beloved motif.

passages.text: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left. Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots. And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.

And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us. But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss. And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

title.en: The Empty Tomb and the Risen Lord
title.zh: 空墳墓與復活的主

region.en: Garden tomb, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，園中墳墓

period: Gospel of Matthew, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 28

summary.en: At dawn on the first day of the week, a great earthquake rolls back the stone; an angel whose countenance is like lightning sits upon it and tells the women, 'He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay... go quickly, and tell his disciples.' Running with fear and great joy, they meet Jesus himself — 'All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him' — the founding scene of the Christian resurrection claim and of the first day of the week as the Lord's day.
summary.zh: 七日的頭一日天快亮時，地大震動，石頭滾開；面貌如閃電的天使坐在石上，對婦女說：「他不在這裏，照他所說的，已經復活了。你們來看安放主的地方……快去告訴他的門徒。」婦女又害怕又大大歡喜地跑去報信，途中遇見耶穌——「願你們平安。她們就上前抱住他的腳拜他。」——基督教復活信仰與七日頭一日（主日）由此奠基。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The resurrection claim is the central confession of Christianity; recorded as narrative for comparative study of death-reversal myths.

passages.text: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre. And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it. His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow: and for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men.

And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay. And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you. And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word.

And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him. Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

title.en: The Road to Emmaus: Known in the Breaking of Bread
title.zh: 以馬忤斯路上：擘餅時被認出

region.en: Emmaus, threescore furlongs from Jerusalem
region.zh: 以馬忤斯，距耶路撒冷二十五里

period: Gospel of Luke, c. 80-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 24

summary.en: Two disciples walk out of Jerusalem in grief — 'we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel' — and a stranger joins them, expounding the scriptures about the Christ, until they urge, 'Abide with us.' At table he takes bread, blesses, breaks, and gives; 'their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.' 'Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?' — and they run back to tell the eleven.
summary.zh: 兩個門徒懷著失望出城——「我們素來所盼望要贖以色列的就是他」——一位生客同行，將經上指著基督的話講解明白，直到他們強留「請你同我們住下吧」。坐席時他拿起餅來祝謝擘開遞給，「他們的眼睛明亮了，這才認出他來；忽然耶穌不見了」。「在路上他和我們說話，我們的心豈不是火熱的麼？」——二人即刻跑回耶路撒冷報信。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The meal recognition scene is the Eucharist's favorite resurrection appearance.

passages.text: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know him. And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him. But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel.

And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and he made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them. And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.

And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures? And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them, saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon. And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.

title.en: Doubting Thomas: My Lord and My God
title.zh: 多馬的懷疑：我的主，我的神

region.en: Upper room behind shut doors, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，門都關了的樓房

period: Gospel of John, c. 90-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 20

summary.en: Absant when the risen Jesus appears, Thomas will not believe the others' report: 'Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.' Eight days later Jesus comes through shut doors and offers exactly that evidence — 'be not faithless, but believing' — and Thomas's answer is the gospel's highest confession: 'My LORD and my God.' The blessing that follows reaches across the centuries: 'blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.'
summary.zh: 主復活顯現時多馬不在，便說：「我非看見他手上的釘痕，用指頭探入那釘痕，又用手探入他的肋旁，我總不信。」八日後，耶穌從關著的門進來，偏偏邀請他那樣驗證——「不要疑惑，總要信」——多馬的回答是福音書最高的認信：「我的主！我的神！」隨後的祝福直達千百年後：「那沒有看見就信的有福了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. 'Doubting Thomas' has become proverbial; the confessional apex of John's gospel.

passages.text: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the LORD. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.

And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you. Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into his side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My LORD and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

title.en: Mary Mistakes the Risen Christ for the Gardener
title.zh: 馬利亞誤認園丁

region.en: Garden by the sepulchre, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，墳墓旁的園子

period: Gospel of John, c. 90-110 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 20

summary.en: Weeping outside the empty tomb, Mary Magdalene stoops to see two angels in white — 'Woman, why weepest thou?' — then turns and sees a figure she takes for the gardener, even offering to carry the body away herself. One word breaks through: 'Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.' Sent to tell the brethren 'I ascend unto my Father, and your Father', she becomes the first apostle of the resurrection — 'the apostle to the apostles.'
summary.zh: 馬利亞站在空墳外哭，低頭見兩位白衣天使問「婦人，你為甚麼哭？」；轉身見一人，誤認為是園丁，甚至願親自把遺體搬走。一聲呼名穿透一切：「耶穌說：馬利亞。她轉過身來，用希伯來話對他說：拉波尼（就是夫子的意思）。」受差去向弟兄報信「我要升上去見我的父，也是你們的父」——她成為復活信息的第一位使者，「使徒的使徒」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first-witness scene underlies the honorific 'apostle to the apostles'.

passages.text: But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre, and seeth two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain. And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my LORD, and I know not where they have laid him.

And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master. Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God. Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the LORD, and that he had spoken these things unto her.

title.en: The Ascension from the Mount of Olives
title.zh: 橄欖山升天

region.en: Mount of Olives, near Jerusalem
region.zh: 橄欖山，近耶路撒冷

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 1

summary.en: Forty days of risen appearances end as 'he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.' Two men in white apparel ask the gazing disciples, 'why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus... shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven' — and the company returns to Jerusalem to pray in the upper room, one hundred and twenty strong, awaiting the promise of the Spirit.
summary.zh: 四十日復活顯現終結之時，「他就被取上升，有一朵雲彩把他接去」。兩個白衣人問呆望天空的門徒：「加利利人哪，你們為甚麼站著望天呢？這離開你們被接升天的耶穌……他怎樣往天上去，你們還要怎樣來。」眾人回耶路撒冷，在樓上房間同心合意恆切禱告——一百二十人等候聖靈的應許。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ascension is celebrated as a principal feast; the return-promise frames Christian eschatology.

passages.text: And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. And while they looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.

Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day's journey. And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes. These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

title.en: Ananias and Sapphira Lie to the Holy Ghost
title.zh: 亞拿尼亞與撒非喇欺哄聖靈

region.en: Jerusalem, apostles' feet
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，使徒腳前

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 5

summary.en: In the community where 'neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own', Ananias and Sapphira sell land, keep back part of the price, and present the rest as the whole. Peter's rebuke — 'thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God' — is followed by sudden death, his, then three hours later hers at the same feet; 'great fear came upon all the church.' The young church's feared and debated tale of concealed giving.
summary.zh: 在「沒有一人說他的東西有一樣是自己的」的團體中，亞拿尼亞夫婦賣田產，私自留下幾分，其餘放在使徒腳前充作全數。彼得斥責——「你不是欺哄人，是欺哄神了」——隨即仆倒斷氣；三小時後妻子在同樣腳前同樣倒下。「全教會和聽見這事的人都甚懼怕。」初期教會最令人戰慄、也最被爭論的隱匿奉獻故事。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The deaths are presented as narrative without endorsement.

passages.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, and kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land? Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God. And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.

And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in. And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much. Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out. Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and great fear came upon all the church.

title.en: The Stoning of Stephen, First Martyr
title.zh: 首位殉道者司提反被石頭打死

region.en: Outside the city walls, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷城外

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapters 6-7

summary.en: Full of the Holy Ghost, Stephen sees 'the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God'; the council stops their ears, casts him out, and stones him — with the clothes laid at the feet of the young man Saul, consenting. Stephen's last words fold the tradition's martyrdom pattern: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit... Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.' The persecution scatters the church, and the gospel spreads.
summary.zh: 滿得聖靈的司提反舉目望天，見「天開了，人子站在神的右邊」；公會捂耳呼喊，把他推到城外用石頭打——見證人把衣裳放在旁邊的少年人掃羅腳前。司提反臨終呼求確立殉道模式：「求主耶穌接收我的靈魂……主啊，不要將這罪歸於他們。說了這話，就睡了。」教會遭大逼迫四散，福音反得廣傳。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The prototype martyr; the Saul connection is the hinge of the Damascus conversion.

passages.text: When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth. But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, and cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria.

title.en: Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
title.zh: 腓利與埃提阿伯太監

region.en: Desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza
region.zh: 耶路撒冷下迦薩的路上

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 8

summary.en: Sent by an angel onto the desert road, Philip catches the treasurer of Candace, queen of Ethiopia, reading Isaiah in his chariot — 'Understandest thou what thou readest?... How can I, except some man should guide me?' Philip preaches Jesus from the suffering servant passage; at the water by the road the eunuch asks, 'what doth hinder me to be baptized?' — and is baptized, going on his way rejoicing, while Philip is caught away by the Spirit. African Christianity has long claimed this as its founding charter.
summary.zh: 使者差腓利上那條通往迦薩的曠野路，追上埃提阿伯女王干大基手下總管銀庫的太監——他正坐在車上誦讀以賽亞書。「你所念的，你明白嗎？……沒有人指教我，怎能明白呢？」腓利便從受苦僕人的經文傳講耶穌；路旁有水，太監問「我受洗有甚麼妨礙呢？」——受洗後歡歡喜喜走路，腓利被主的靈提了去。非洲教會久以本章為建基憲章。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Ethiopian eunuch is honored in Ethiopian Orthodox memory as the bearer of the faith.

passages.text: And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me?

Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus. And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized? And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.

title.en: Saul on the Road to Damascus
title.zh: 掃羅在大馬士革路上

region.en: Road near Damascus
region.zh: 大馬士革近郊路上

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 9

summary.en: Breathing threatenings and slaughter, the persecutor travels to Damascus with warrants for 'this way'; suddenly a light from heaven shines around him and he falls to earth: 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?... I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.' Led blind into the city, he is met three days later by the disciple Ananias — 'a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles' — receives his sight like scales falling, is baptized, and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues.
summary.zh: 口吐威嚇兇殺話的逼迫者，持大祭司公文往大馬士革捉拿「信奉這道的人」；忽然天上有大光四面照著他，他就仆倒在地：「掃羅，掃羅，你為甚麼逼迫我？……我就是你所逼迫的耶穌。你用腳踢刺是難的。」被拉進城，三日看不見、不吃不喝；門徒亞拿尼亞奉命去按手——「他是我所揀選的器皿，要在外邦人和君王並以色列人面前宣揚我的名」——鱗狀的東西掉下，他就看見，起來受洗，隨即在各會堂宣講耶穌。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The conversion is the hinge of Christian universalism; tagged theophany for the heavenly light and voice.

passages.text: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest, and desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem. And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: and he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus. And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink. And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth.

But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: for I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake. And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

title.en: Peter's Sheet Vision and Cornelius's Household
title.zh: 彼得的布異象與哥尼流一家

region.en: Rooftop at Joppa; Caesarea
region.zh: 約帕房頂；該撒利亞

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 10

summary.en: Praying hungry on a rooftop, Peter falls into a trance: heaven opens, a great sheet knitted at four corners descends full of unclean beasts, and a voice commands, 'Rise, Peter; kill, and eat' — 'What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common', thrice repeated. Sent for by Cornelius, the God-fearing centurion, Peter preaches in Caesarea and the Holy Ghost falls on the uncircumcised hearers — 'Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?' The charter of the Gentile mission.
summary.zh: 屋頂禱告時餓了的彼得魂遊象外：天開了，四角垂下的大布縑滿俗物與不潔之物，聲音說「彼得，起來，宰了吃」——「神所潔淨的，你不可當作俗物」，一連三次。羅馬百夫長哥尼流遣人相請；彼得在該撒利亞講道，聖靈降在一切未受割禮的聽道者身上——「這些人既受了聖靈，與我們一樣，誰能禁止用水給他們施洗呢？」外邦宣教的憲章自此立定。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sheet vision is the tradition's charter of universality and the overturning of purity codes.

passages.text: Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour: and he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance, and saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending upon him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air. And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean. And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven.

While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost: for they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter, Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

title.en: The Angel Breaks Peter Out of Prison
title.zh: 天使救彼得出監

region.en: Herod's prison, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，希律的監牢

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 12

summary.en: Intending to bring Peter forth after Passover, Herod keeps him sleeping bound with two chains between soldiers — while the church prays without ceasing. The angel smites Peter on the side, the chains fall off, the iron gate 'opened to them of his own accord'; Peter thinks it a vision until the angel departs and he stands alone in the street — 'Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel' — and comes to Mary's house where the praying church can hardly believe the knocking is really him.
summary.zh: 希律要在逾越節後提彼得出來辦他，彼得卻被兩條鐵鏈鎖著睡在二兵士之間——教會卻為他切切禱告神。使者拍他的肋旁，鐵鏈脫落；「臨街的鐵門就自己開了」；他以為見異象，直到天使離開，才獨立街中——「我現在真知道主差遣他的使者，救我脫離希律的手」——到了馬利亞家門口，禱告的人群竟不敢相信真是他敲門。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The prison-delivery is a classic angelic-rescue type.

passages.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him. And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison. And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.

When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him. And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod. And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.

title.en: Midnight Hymns in the Philippian Jail
title.zh: 腓立比監中的半夜歌聲

region.en: Philippi, Macedonia
region.zh: 馬其頓，腓立比

period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 16

summary.en: Answering a night vision — 'a man of Macedonia... Come over into Macedonia, and help us' — Paul crosses to Europe, converts the purple-seller Lydia, and after an exorcism is beaten and jailed with Silas.
